## QNW-WIT265 · Printed p. 265 · The divine Names in manifestation and concealment

Source: https://archive.org/details/machra3-khosous/page/n263/mode/1up

Speaker: Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī · al-Nuṣūṣ (2008 appendix)

### Arabic · passage 1

بالممكنات ، وشروق نوره على أعيان الموجودات ليس غير ذلك . 

فهو سبحانه من حيث هذا الوجه إذا لومح تعين وجوده متقيدا بالصفات اللازمة لكل متعين من الأعيان الممكنة ، التي هي في الحقيقة نسب علمه جمعا وفرادى ، وما يتبع تلك الصفات من الأمور المسمّاه شؤونا وخواص وعوارض ، والآثار التابعة لأحكام الاسم الدهر المسمّاه أوقاتا ، والمراتب أيضا والمواطن ، فإن ذلك التعين والتشخص يسمّى خلقا وسوى ، كما ستعرف عن قريب سره إن شاء اللّه تعالى . 

وينضاف إليه إذ ذاك كل وصف ، ويسمّى بكل اسم ، ويظهر بكل رسم ، ويقبل كل حكم ، ويتقيّد في كل مكان بكل رسم ، ويدرك لكل مشعر من بصر وسمع وعقل وفهم ، وغير ذلك من القوى والمدارك فاذكر . 

واعلم أن ذلك بسريانه في كل شيء بنوره الذاتي المقدّس عن التجزئ والانقسام ، والحلول في الأرواح والأجسام فافهم ، ولكن كل ذلك متى أحب وكيف شاء . 

وهو في كل وقت وحال القابل لهذين الحكمين الكليين المذكورين المتضادين بذاته ، لا بأمر زائد ، والجامع بين كل أمرين مختلفين من غائب وحاضر وصادر ووارد ، إذا شاء ظهر في كل صورة ، وإن لم يشأ لم ينضاف إليه صورة . 

لا يقدح تعيّنه وتشخّصه بالصور ، واتصافه بصفاتها في كمال وجوده وعزه وقدسه ، ولا ينافي ظهوره في الأشياء وإظهاره وتعينه وتقيده بها وبأحكامها من حيث هي علوه وإطلاقه من القيود ، وغناه بذاته عن جميع ما وصف بالوجود ، بل هو سبحانه الجامع بين ما تماثل من الحقائق وتخالف فيتألف ، وبين ما تغاير وتباين فيختلف . 

بتجليه الوجودي ظهرت الخفيات ، وتنزلت من الغيب إلى الشهادة البركات من حيث أسمائه : الباسط والمبدي ، وبارتفاع حكم تدليه تخفى وتنعدم الموجودات باسميه : 
القابض والمعيد . 

إنه تعالى كان محتجبا بعزه ، كان غفورا ، وإن أحب أن يعرف دنا وظهر فيما شاء كيف شاء ، فكان ودودا ، فبالمحبة يبدي من كونه محبّا وهي تبديه ، وبها من كونه محبّا ومحبوبا يعيد كل شيء في قبضته ، ومقهور تحت قوة بطشه لقوة فعله وضعف المنفعل .

### English · passage 1

...to possible things and His light shines upon the entities of existents, and in no other way.

When viewed from this aspect, His existence is determined and restricted by the attributes necessarily attached to each determinate possible entity. In reality these are relations of His knowledge, collectively and individually, together with what follows from those attributes: matters called affairs, properties and accidents; effects following the rulings of the Name “Time,” called times; and also ranks and abodes. This determination and individuation are called “creation” and “other,” whose secret you will shortly understand, God willing.

Every description is then ascribed to Him. He is called by every Name, appears through every designation, accepts every judgment, and is restricted in every place by every designation. He is apprehended by every faculty of perception—sight, hearing, intellect, understanding and other powers and means of apprehension. Remember this.

Know that this occurs through His pervading everything by His essential light, which is holy beyond partition, division or indwelling in spirits and bodies. Understand. Yet all this occurs whenever He loves and however He wills.

At every time and in every state He admits, through His own Essence rather than something additional, both of the universal and opposed judgments just mentioned. He joins every pair of different things: absent and present, outgoing and incoming. If He wills, He appears in every form; if He does not, no form is ascribed to Him.

His determination and individuation through forms, and His qualification by their attributes, do not impair the perfection of His existence, might or holiness. His appearing in things, making them appear, and being determined and restricted through them and their rulings do not contradict His elevation, freedom from restrictions or essential independence of everything described as existent. Rather, He joins realities which resemble and differ from one another so that they are brought together, and those which are other and distinct so that they differ.

Through His existential self-disclosure hidden things appear and blessings descend from the unseen into the witnessed, in respect of His Names “the Expander” and “the Originator.” When the ruling of His descent is withdrawn, existents become hidden and cease to exist through His Names “the Contractor” and “the Restorer.”

When He is concealed by His might, He is Forgiving; when He loves to be known, He draws near and appears in whatever He wills, however He wills, and is Loving. Through love He originates as lover, and love makes Him appear; through it, as lover and beloved, He restores everything into His grasp, subdued beneath the force of His might because of the strength of His action and the weakness of what receives it.

## QNW-WIT266 · Printed p. 266 · Conclusion of the appended discourse

Source: https://archive.org/details/machra3-khosous/page/n264/mode/1up

Speaker: Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī · al-Nuṣūṣ (2008 appendix)

### Arabic · passage 1

ومظهر قدرته وآلة حكمته في فعله بسنته ، ومحل ظهور سر القبض والبسط والإبداء والإخفاء والغيب والشهادة والكشف والحجاب الصوري السببي ، الذي به يفعل ما ذكره لا مطلقا هو عرشه المجيد . 

ولهذا قال سبحانه وتعالى مبدأ سر هذا الأمر : لِمَنْ كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ أَوْ أَلْقَى السَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ [ ق : 37 ] ، إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ * إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ * وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ * ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ * فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [ البروج : 12 - 16 ] . 

في مرتبتي الإطلاق والتقييد ، وقوله تعالى :فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ جواب سؤال مقدار ، علم أنه يبدو من معترض محجوب . 
* * *

### English · passage 1

The manifestation of His power, the instrument of His wisdom in acting according to His customary way, and the locus where the secret appears of contraction and expansion, origination and concealment, unseen and witnessed, unveiling and the formal, causal veil—through which He performs what has been mentioned, though not without qualification—is His Glorious Throne.

For this reason He said, disclosing the secret of this matter, “For one who has a heart, or gives ear while present” (Q 50:37): “Surely your Lord's grasp is mighty. It is He who originates and restores. He is the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Glorious Throne, Doer of whatever He wills” (Q 85:12–16), in the two ranks of absoluteness and restriction.

His words “Doer of whatever He wills” answer an anticipated question which He knew would arise from a veiled objector.

Related passage IDs: MSH-P229, MSH-P230

## QNW-WIT267 · Printed p. 267 · Final appended passage and colophon

Source: https://archive.org/details/machra3-khosous/page/n265/mode/1up

Speaker: Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī · al-Nuṣūṣ (2008 appendix)

### Arabic · passage 1

نصّ شريف هو آخر النصوص : 
اعلم أن أعظم الشبه والحجب أن التعددات الواقعة في الوجود الواحد يوجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه ، فتوهم أن الأعيان ظهرت في الوجود وبالوجود ، وإنما ظهرت آثارها في الوجود ولم تظهر هي ، ولا تظهر أبدا ؛ لأنها لذاتها لا تقتضي الظهور . 
ومتى أخبر محقق بغير هذا أو نسب إليها الوجود والظهور ، فإنما ذلك الإخبار بلسان بعض المراتب والأذواق النسبية : أي إنما تثبت صحتها بالنسبة إلى مقام معين أو مقامات مخصوصة دون ذوق مقام الكمال . 

وأما النص الذي لا ينسخ حكمه فهو ما ذكرناه ، وهكذا كل ما ذكر في هذا الكتاب ، فإنه الحق الصريح الذي هو الأمر عليه ، وما سواه فقد يكون صحيحا مطلقا كهذا الذي ذكرنا ، وقد يكون صحيحا بالنسبة والإضافة إلى مقام ما ، كما سبقت الإشارة إليه . 

ومتى وضح لك ما ذكرته في هذا النص علمت أن الظهور للوجود ، لكن بشرط التعدّد مع آثار الأعيان فيه ، وأن البطون صفة ذاتية للأعيان ، والوجود أيضا من حيث تعقل وحدته ، والأمر دائر بين ظهور وبطون لغلبة ومغلوبية ، بمعنى أنه ما نقص من الظاهر اندرج في الباطن وبالعكس ، والنسب والإضافات صور أحوال وأحكام تنشئ بين المراتب ، فيظهر بعضها بعضا ، ويخفي بعضها بعضا ، بحسب الغلبة والمغلوبية المشار إليها آنفا فافهم . 

تمّ الكتاب والحمد لله وحده وصلّى الله على سيّدنا محمد وآله وصحبه وسلم * * *

### English · passage 1

**A noble text, the last of the texts.**

Know that the greatest doubts and veils [arise when] the multiplicities occurring in the one existence “necessitate the effects of the fixed entities within it” [the opening construction is textually uncertain], so that one imagines that the entities themselves have appeared in existence and through existence. Only their effects have appeared in existence; the entities themselves have not appeared and never will, for they do not intrinsically demand manifestation.

Whenever a realized knower reports otherwise or ascribes existence and manifestation to them, that report is in the language of certain ranks and relative tastes. Its validity is established relative to a particular station or certain stations, not according to the tasting of the station of perfection.

The definitive text whose ruling is not superseded is what we have stated. The same applies to everything stated in this book: it is the plain truth of how the matter is. What is said elsewhere may be unqualifiedly true, like what we have stated, or true relatively and in connection with a particular station, as indicated earlier.

When what I have explained in this text becomes clear to you, you will know that manifestation belongs to existence, but under the condition of multiplicity together with the effects of the entities within it; and that hiddenness is an essential attribute of the entities, and also of existence insofar as its unity is conceived. The matter turns between manifestation and hiddenness through predominance and subordination: whatever diminishes from the manifest is included in the hidden, and conversely. Relations and attributions are forms of states and rulings arising between ranks: some make others manifest, and some conceal others, according to the predominance and subordination just indicated. Understand.

The book is complete. Praise belongs to God alone, and may God bless our master Muḥammad, his family and companions, and grant them peace.

### Editorial note

The opening construction is textually difficult. This appendix reads للوجود (“belongs to existence”), whereas the lemma quoted at commentary p.232 reads في الوجود (“in existence”); the commentary’s gloss then uses للوجود. These internal differences within one printed volume are not independent manuscript variants. The appendix’s colophon does not supply the commentary’s missing final clause.

Related passage IDs: MSH-P231, MSH-P232

## Method for an edition deserving “critical”

1. Secure high-quality image of M08, A21 and at least independent manuscript witness(es); record provenance, dates, folios, lacunae, and interventions.
2. Transcribe each witness separately, retaining spelling and lineation; do not back-project web punctuation onto manuscripts.
3. Enter every lemma of Qūnawī into a separate quotation layer; tag attributed earlier Sufi, kalām, Qurʾānic, ḥadīth, and modern editor layers.
4. Collate *actual readings*: record `M08: X | A21: Y | ms-siglum: Z` **only after checking each image**. Until then preserve `suspect / suggested / unverified` states.
5. Reconcile the independent 20/21/22 divisions by incipit and explicit rather than section numbers alone.
6. Re-translate passages affected by readings; only then promote any completed units to critically checked status.

**Not yet done:** manuscript collation, reconstruction of Qūnawī's 20/21 division, verification of quotations in the cited originals, and verification of editorial printing errors against physical facsimile. These remain explicit deficits, not hidden omissions.

| MSH4-T28 | 134 | The online main text becomes entangled with a *long modern editorial footnote*. The long moralizing note starting «يسأل عنه...» is omitted; Qūnawī lemma resumes on p135. | Preserve online reading; check printed image, Āshtiyānī, and independent source where relevant |
| MSH4-T29 | 135 | The reference after «والله بما تعملون بصير» is given as Q 60:3; citation location and interpretive usage to cross-check against Qurʾān. | Preserve online reading; check printed image, Āshtiyānī, and independent source where relevant |
| MSH4-T30 | 137 | Essential *barqī* unveiling endures as complete **knowledge after the flash**, not a perpetual identical flash; compare pp108–110 and p137. | Preserve online reading; check printed image, Āshtiyānī, and independent source where relevant |
| MSH4-T31 | 138 | Received «إيراداتهم» rather than «إراداتهم» in one occurrence; do NOT silently emend. The modern footnote identifying the master as Ibn ʿArabī is not an independently collated medieval witness. Quoted visionary report is Qūnawī’s, not the commentator’s autobiographical experience. | Preserve online reading; check printed image, Āshtiyānī, and independent source where relevant |

### Attribution layers in the new batch

- **Q:** bracketed lemmata following «قال رضي الله عنه» generally reproduce **Qūnawī**, and should not automatically be entered as al-Mahāʾimī's independent doctrine.
- **M:** the prose introducing, explaining and occasionally criticizing the lemma is **al-Mahāʾimī**, including conjectural qualifications like «ولست منهم» (p.118).
- **D:** quoted Qurʾānic verses, sayings and earlier authors require source identification and where relevant hadith verification. A quotation is evidence of the commentator's use of it, not proof of its authenticity.
- **E:** the modern print editor's notes are **excluded** from the authorial main text at pp.119, 121, 126, 128, 133, 134, 138 and elsewhere. This is an editorial exclusion, not a lacuna in the medieval prose.
- **P:** at page breaks, the original often ends in the middle of a sentence. Continuations are present on the next page. Preserve all original page boundaries without inventing connectors.

**Unattained standards:** independently photographed 2008 collation; Āshtiyānī (1421 AH) collation; manuscript witness variants; paleographical confirmation; full quotation source checking; expert review of metaphysical terminology.

# Stage 09 addendum — independent text/reception evidence (9 November 2026)

**Status:** source transcription and quotation comparison, *no manuscript collation*; variants not silently adopted in the base text.

## APP-01: direction of causation

2008 embedded Qūnawī quotation in al-Mahāʾimī (p.230): `التعددات الواقعة في الوجود الواحد توجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه`.
2008 separately reproduced Qūnawī text (p.267): `التعددات الواقعة في الوجود الواحد يوجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه`.
Separate Qūnawī transcription and Jāmī, *Naqd al-Nuṣūṣ*, printed p.47: `التعددات الواقعة في الوجود الواحد بموجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه`.

The third reading, **بموجب**, reverses the likely causal construal: multiplicity occurs by virtue of the effects of the fixed entities rather than itself producing those effects. Al-Mahāʾimī's own gloss on p.231 says `هذه التعددات إنما هي آثار الأعيان الثابتة`, which supports this sense. The third reading is a *supported alternative*, not a manuscript-established emendation.

Sources: https://www.ibnalarabi.com/qunawi/nusus.php?id=22 ; https://ablibrary.net/book_content/3772/178 .

## APP-05: in existence or belonging to existence

2008 embedded lemma (p.232): `علمت أن الظهور في الوجود`.
2008 original appendix (p.267): `علمت أن الظهور للوجود`.
Al-Mahāʾimī's own gloss p.232 and Jāmī, *Ashiʿʿat al-Lamaʿāt*, printed p.129, both employ `الظهور للوجود`. Jāmī quotes Qūnawī by name and also states `وأن البطون صفة ذاتية للأعيان`. This independently supports the *sense*, not a particular manuscript exemplar.

Source: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/17500/129?lang=ar .

## Separate Qūnawī edited edition (Eshkūrī and Nawāʾī)

A 121-page edition of *Risālat al-Nuṣūṣ* with Eshkūrī's notes and Nawāʾī's editorial work includes reported variant sigla. Printed p.48: `المعدّدات` versus `المعدومات (خ ل)`; `نبهت عليه` versus `تنبهت عليه (خ)`. Printed p.55: `تعيّنه` versus `التعيّن (خ ل)`. The sigla's precise manuscript assignments are unverified, and these selected examples have not been shown to correspond to APP-01 or APP-05.

Sources: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/5348/52?lang=ar ; https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/5348/59?lang=ar .

## Remaining work and source confidence

- **Arabic imported:** Mahāʾimī pp.11–149 and 230–232 only (142 pages). English first-pass pp.11–232 (222 pages).
- **Arabic absent from structured reader:** Mahāʾimī pp.150–229 (80 pages), independent Qūnawī original pp.237–266 (30 pages). Original page proofs available pp.235,236,267.
- **Āshtiyānī edition:** catalogued, 335pp, ISBN 964424804X, but text not obtained, no reading from it claimed. https://ge.nii.ac.jp/ncid/BA64748920
- **Commentary p.232:** syntactically incomplete at `فإذا ظهرت آثار الوجود بشرط` in the electronic transcription; do not conjecturally supply a completion.
- **Manuscript witnesses collated:** zero. No physical print page photograph checked at this stage.

## Prior Stage 08 internally collated two printed occurrences of the same 2008 edition

# Stage 08 — Synoptic textual apparatus for al-Mahāʾimī and Qūnawī

**Date:** 9 November 2026. **Status:** printed-witness internal comparison; NOT manuscript collation.

## Source identities and provenance

The Arabic quotation within al-Mahāʾimī’s commentary in the 2008 Beirut edition (printed pp. 230–232) has been compared against the independently reproduced Qūnawī original at the back of the **same** 2008 volume (printed p. 267). These are **two locations within one printed edition**, not two independently established textual witnesses. The cited digital transcriptions may reproduce mistakes in the 2008 print or in transcription.

- Embedded commentary text: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/230?lang=ar, https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/231?lang=ar, https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/232?lang=ar
- Separately reproduced Qūnawī text: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/267?lang=ar
- Comparative edition *available bibliographically but NOT collated*: Sayyid Jalāl al-Dīn Āshtiyānī (ed.), *Mashraʿ al-khuṣūṣ ilā maʿānī al-nuṣūṣ*, Qom, 1421 AH/2000–01, **335 pages**, ISBN 964424804X. Library catalogue: https://ge.nii.ac.jp/ncid/BA64748920 .

## Differences documented, not adjudicated

| Ref | Issue | Embedded lemma (2008 pp.230–232) | Independently reproduced original (2008 p.267) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| APP-01 | agreement of the verb | `توجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه` | `يوجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه` | morphological |
| APP-02 | non-manifestation | `ولم تظهر أبدا` | `ولم تظهر هي ، ولا تظهر أبدا` | semantic-emphasis |
| APP-03 | intrinsic incapacity | `لأنها ذاتها لا تقتضي الظهور` | `لأنها لذاتها لا تقتضي الظهور` | lexical |
| APP-04 | relative validity | `إنما يثبت صحتها بالنسبة` | `إنما تثبت صحتها بالنسبة` | morphological |
| APP-05 | locus of manifestation | `علمت أن الظهور في الوجود` | `علمت أن الظهور للوجود` | substantive |
| APP-06 | alternation wording | `بين الظهور ، وبطون غلبة ومغلوبية` | `بين ظهور وبطون لغلبة ومغلوبية` | syntactical |
| APP-07 | origin of relations | `صور أحوال وأحكام تنشأ بين المراتب` | `صور أحوال وأحكام تنشئ بين المراتب` | morphological |
| APP-08 | concealment | `ويخفى بعضها بعضا` | `ويخفي بعضها بعضا` | textual |
| APP-09 | ending | `فإذا ظهرت آثار الوجود بشرط . آخره والحمد لله رب العالمين` | `تمّ الكتاب والحمد لله وحده وصلّى الله` | lacuna |

### Explanation and editorial consequences

**APP-01 — agreement of the verb.** Embedded reading (p. 230–231): «توجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه». Separate Qūnawī (p. 267): «يوجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه». Different agreement (feminine vs masculine form); the plural subject is التعددات. No emendation made.

**APP-02 — non-manifestation.** Embedded reading (p. 231): «ولم تظهر أبدا». Separate Qūnawī (p. 267): «ولم تظهر هي ، ولا تظهر أبدا». Independent text adds the explicit pronoun and distinguishes past and future non-manifestation.

**APP-03 — intrinsic incapacity.** Embedded reading (p. 231): «لأنها ذاتها لا تقتضي الظهور». Separate Qūnawī (p. 267): «لأنها لذاتها لا تقتضي الظهور». The second specifies ‘in virtue of their own essence’ with a preposition.

**APP-04 — relative validity.** Embedded reading (p. 231): «إنما يثبت صحتها بالنسبة». Separate Qūnawī (p. 267): «إنما تثبت صحتها بالنسبة». Agreement differs; contextual reference is the validity of statements from restricted ranks.

**APP-05 — locus of manifestation.** Embedded reading (p. 232): «علمت أن الظهور في الوجود». Separate Qūnawī (p. 267): «علمت أن الظهور للوجود». Material distinction: “manifestation is in existence” vs “manifestation belongs to existence.” The latter accords with the commentary’s explicit gloss but must be checked against Āshtiyānī and manuscripts.

**APP-06 — alternation wording.** Embedded reading (p. 232): «بين الظهور ، وبطون غلبة ومغلوبية». Separate Qūnawī (p. 267): «بين ظهور وبطون لغلبة ومغلوبية». Definiteness and preposition in account of manifestation and hiddenness.

**APP-07 — origin of relations.** Embedded reading (p. 232): «صور أحوال وأحكام تنشأ بين المراتب». Separate Qūnawī (p. 267): «صور أحوال وأحكام تنشئ بين المراتب». Two printed forms of the verb; assess syntactic fit against a scan before vocalizing.

**APP-08 — concealment.** Embedded reading (p. 232): «ويخفى بعضها بعضا». Separate Qūnawī (p. 267): «ويخفي بعضها بعضا». Printed form differs by ya/hamza/vowel convention; the intended causative relation must be checked.

**APP-09 — ending.** Embedded reading (p. 232): «فإذا ظهرت آثار الوجود بشرط . آخره والحمد لله رب العالمين». Separate Qūnawī (p. 267): «تمّ الكتاب والحمد لله وحده وصلّى الله». The commentary sentence ends after an uncompleted prepositional construction; the standalone Qūnawī original ends normally. The latter cannot supply the missing Mahāʾimī commentary.


## Proposed reader treatment

1. Qūnawī lemma should carry a segment ID, a verse/page reference to **both** the embedded and independently reproduced locations, and a note explaining whether wording is normalized or diplomatic.
2. Al-Mahāʾimī commentary remains a separate authorial layer. When the commentary quotes the lemma, both are accessible without conflating the speakers.
3. Āshtiyānī readings belong in a distinct column **only after the text is consulted**. The word “variant” above refers to an internal printed divergence, NOT to a collated manuscript variant.
4. The p.232 truncated clause should be displayed exactly and tagged `witness_ends_mid_sentence`; do not add a conjectural completion.

## Full source text (the extracted medieval running text, excluding modern footnotes)

### Al-Mahāʾimī, 2008 printed p. 230

https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/230?lang=ar

[ ولهذا قال سبحانه وتعالى مبدئ سر هذا الأمر : لِمَنْ كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ أَوْ أَلْقَى السَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ [ ق : 37 ] ، إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ ( 12 ) إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ ( 13 ) وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ ( 14 ) ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ ( 15 ) فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ ( 16 ) [ البروج : 12 - 16 ] في مرتبتي الإطلاق والتقييد ، وقوله : فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [ البروج : 16 ] ، جواب سؤال مقدر ، علم أنه يبدو من معترض محجوب ] .

أي : لما ذكرنا من الترتيب ، قال سبحانه لإظهار سر هذا الترتيب بطريق الرمز بحيث يختص بالفهم من كان له قلب يستكشف المعاني الغامضة من القرآن ، أو ألقى السمع إلى المشايخ الكاشفة لها ، وهو حاضر كامل التوجه ، كأنه ينظر إلى ما يسمع أن بطش - أي قدرة - ربك لشديد يؤثر فيما شاء كيف شاء أنه هو يبدي من حيث كونه ودودا ، ويعيد من حيث كونه غفورا ودودا معا ، يفعل ذلك بالعرش المجيد الذي هو العقل الأول .

الإعادة إلى البطون ، والإبداء إلى الظهور ، في قوله تعالى : فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [ البروج : 16 ] ، إشارة إلى أنه لا يحتاج إلى الأسباب كما يتوهم من قوله تعالى : ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ [ البروج : 15 ] ، بل فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [ البروج : 16 ] ، بالأسباب وبدونها . وإنما الأسباب على مقتضى الحكمة ، وإلى أنه ليس موجبا بالذات ، كما يتوهم من أن الغفورية والودودية يوجبان الإعادة والإبداء ، فبيّن أن تجابيها أيضا بمشيئته واختياره لا بإيجاب ، كما يقول أهل الحجاب .

النص الثاني والعشرون : ولما فرغ عن تحقيق التوحد ، شرع في كشف ما يحجب عنه غالبا ، فذلك بما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ نص شريف ] هو آخر النصوص ؛ لأن كمال إيضاح التوحيد الذي هو أشرف المطالب حاصل به ، والحجب الباقية تيسر انكشافه عند انكشافه وآخريته لأن كمال اتضاح التوحيد في مقام أحدية الجمع والفرق ، وهو آخر المقامات فيما يتعارف .

قال الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه : [ اعلم أن أعظم الشبه والحجب أن التعدّدات الواقعة في الوجود الواحد توجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه ، فتوهم أن الأعيان ظهرت في الوجود وبالوجود ،

### Al-Mahāʾimī, 2008 printed p. 231

https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/231?lang=ar

وإنما ظهرت آثارها في الوجود ولم تظهر أبدا ؛ لأنها ذاتها لا تقتضي الظهور ] .

إنما كان هذا أعظم الشبه الحاجبة عن التوحيد ؛ لأن جميع الحجب من النقص والإمكان والتغييرات فرع هذا ، فإذا ارتفع ، فكأنه ارتفع الكل .

يعنى : أن هذه التعددات إنما هي آثار الأعيان الثابتة في الوجود الواحد الظاهر بها ، فتوهم أن الأعيان هي التي ظهرت في الوجود ، فهي المرئية ، وظهرت بوجود خاص لها غير وجود الواجب ، فرد ذلك بأن الظاهر هو الحق فيها وبها ، وإنما ظهرت آثار الأعيان في ذلك الوجود الواحد ، ولم تظهر تلك الأعيان ولا تظهر أبدا ؛ لأنها بالذات لا تقتضي ، أي : لا تقبل الظهور ؛ لأنها أمور عدمية ولا ظهور للعدم بل الوجود هو الظاهر والباطن .

ومن هنا قال الشيخ محيي الدين في « إنشاء الدوائر » : إن الوجود ليس بزائد على الوجود ؛ لأن الوجود هو الظاهر ، ولا ينافي كونه زائدا على الماهية في غير الواجب ، ثم ذكر تأويل ما يخالفه من أقوال المحققين ، بما قال الشيخ أعلى اللّه مقامه : [ ومتى أخبر محقق بغير هذا أو نسب إليها الوجود والظهور ، فإنما ذلك الإخبار بلسان بعض المراتب والأذواق النسبية ، أي : إنما يثبت صحتها بالنسبة إلى مقام معين ، أو مقامات مخصوصة دون ذوق مقام الكمال ، وأما النص الذي لا ينسخ حكمه ، فهو ما ذكرناه وهكذا كل ما ذكر في هذا الكتاب ، فإنه الحق الصريح الذي هو الأمر عليه ، وما سواه ، فقد يكون صحيحا مطلقا كهذا الذي ذكرنا ، وقد يكون صحيحا بالنسبة والإضافة إلي مقام ما ، كما سبقت الإشارة إليه ] .

أي : ومتى أخبر محقق عن كشفه بغير ما ذكرنا من أن الظهور للوجود ، بأن قال : الظهور لها والوجود محقق فيها ، أو نسب إليها الوجود والظهور جميعا ، وقال لها : الوجود الإضافي هو ظل الوجود الحق ، وهي الظاهرة بذلك الوجود ، فإنما ذلك الإخبار بلسان بعض مراتب الكشف وبلسان بعض الأذواق النسبية لا بمعنى أن المخبر المكاشف بجميع المقامات يخبر بذلك عن بعضها ، بل بمعنى أن هذا الكلام ، إنما يصح من المخبر بها إذا بلغ مقاما معينا ، أو مقامات مخصوصة وتقيد بها ، ولم يصل إلى مقام الكمال ، فإن الواصل إليه لا يعتد بظهورها ولا وجودها ، بل الظاهر هو الوجود الواحد فيها .

### Al-Mahāʾimī, 2008 printed p. 232

https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/232?lang=ar

هذا هو النص الذي لا ينسخ بما هو أعلى منه ، بخلاف تلك المقامات فإنها تنسخ بما هي أعلى منها ، ثم ذكر أن جميع نصوصه إنما هي على مقام الكمال وصحتها على الإطلاق ، بخلاف المذكور في غيره من كتبه وكتب غيره ، فإنه قيد يكون كذلك وقد لا يكون ، مع أنه لا بدّ وأن يكون صحيحا ، والإضافة إلى مقام ما سبقت الإشارة في التفريع الثالث من تفاريع النصوص الثلاثة : الأول من أن جميع الكشوف لا بدّ من صحتها بوجه .

فإن قيل : قد مر مرارا أن الأعيان ظاهرة ، قلنا : المراد ظهورها بظهور الحق فيها ، لا بذاتها ، كما أن وجودها كذلك ، وذلك الظهور والوجود عين الحق لا هي ، فهي معدومة أبدا . فإن قيل : فحينئذ لا يكون ذلك من النصوص . قلنا : إنما لا يكون من النصوص على تقدير أن يقال : أن الظهور إما بذاتها وإلا فهذا الكلام لا يقبل النسخ ، فافهم .

قال الشيخ : [ ومتى وضح لك ما ذكرته في هذا النص ، علمت أن الظهور في الوجود ؛ لكن بشرط التعدد مع آثار الأعيان فيه ، وأن البطون صفة ذاتية للأعيان ، والوجود أيضا من حيث تعقل وحدته ، والأمر دائر بين الظهور ، وبطون غلبة ومغلوبية ، بمعنى أنه ما نقص من الظاهر ، اندرج في الباطن ، وبالعكس والنسب والإضافات صور أحوال وأحكام تنشأ بين المراتب ، فيظهر بعضها بعضا ، ويخفى بعضها بعضا بحسب الغلبية والمغلوبية المشار إليها آنفا ، فافهم ] .

وصلّ اللهم على سيدنا محمد وآله وصحبه وسلّم ، أي : وما ظهر لك ما ذكرته من أن الظهور لآثار الأعيان في الوجود ، علمت أن الظهور للوجود ، إذ لا أثر للأعيان من حيث هي ؛ لأنها معدومة ، بل من حيث تعلق الوجود بها فالآثار في الحقيقة آثار الوجود بشرط الأعيان ، فإذا ظهرت آثار الوجود بشرط .

آخره والحمد لله رب العالمين

### Qūnawī, 2008 appendix p. 267

https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9637/267?lang=ar

نصّ شريف هو آخر النصوص :
اعلم أن أعظم الشبه والحجب أن التعددات الواقعة في الوجود الواحد يوجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه ، فتوهم أن الأعيان ظهرت في الوجود وبالوجود ، وإنما ظهرت آثارها في الوجود ولم تظهر هي ، ولا تظهر أبدا ؛ لأنها لذاتها لا تقتضي الظهور .
ومتى أخبر محقق بغير هذا أو نسب إليها الوجود والظهور ، فإنما ذلك الإخبار بلسان بعض المراتب والأذواق النسبية : أي إنما تثبت صحتها بالنسبة إلى مقام معين أو مقامات مخصوصة دون ذوق مقام الكمال .
وأما النص الذي لا ينسخ حكمه فهو ما ذكرناه ، وهكذا كل ما ذكر في هذا الكتاب ، فإنه الحق الصريح الذي هو الأمر عليه ، وما سواه فقد يكون صحيحا مطلقا كهذا الذي ذكرنا ، وقد يكون صحيحا بالنسبة والإضافة إلى مقام ما ، كما سبقت الإشارة إليه .
ومتى وضح لك ما ذكرته في هذا النص علمت أن الظهور للوجود ، لكن بشرط التعدّد مع آثار الأعيان فيه ، وأن البطون صفة ذاتية للأعيان ، والوجود أيضا من حيث تعقل وحدته ، والأمر دائر بين ظهور وبطون لغلبة ومغلوبية ، بمعنى أنه ما نقص من الظاهر اندرج في الباطن وبالعكس ، والنسب والإضافات صور أحوال وأحكام تنشئ بين المراتب ، فيظهر بعضها بعضا ، ويخفي بعضها بعضا ، بحسب الغلبة والمغلوبية المشار إليها آنفا فافهم .
تمّ الكتاب والحمد لله وحده وصلّى الله على سيّدنا محمد وآله وصحبه وسلم

### English translation of p. 267 (checked passage only)

**Qūnawī, final text (source-checked translation of printed p. 267).**

Know that the greatest doubts and veils arise when the multiplicities occurring in the one existence produce effects belonging to the fixed entities therein. One then imagines that the entities themselves have appeared in existence and through existence. Yet what appears in existence is their effects; **they themselves neither appeared nor will ever appear**, because their very nature does not demand manifestation.

When a realized knower reports otherwise, or attributes existence and manifestation to them, this report is in the idiom of certain ranks and relative tastes: it is valid only in relation to one determinate station or several stations, not according to the experiential knowledge of the station of perfection.

The definitive statement, whose ruling cannot be superseded, is what we have stated; so too every statement in this book. This is the unqualified truth about the matter. What is said elsewhere may be true unqualifiedly, as this is, or may be true only relatively and in connection with some station, as already indicated.

When what I have explained in this text becomes clear, you will know that manifestation belongs **to existence**, but under the condition of multiplicity together with the effects of the entities within it. Hiddenness is an intrinsic attribute of the entities, and likewise of existence insofar as its unity is conceived. The matter alternates between manifestation and hiddenness through predominance and subordination: whatever diminishes from the manifest falls within the hidden, and conversely. Relations and attributions are forms of states and judgments arising among ranks: some make others manifest and hide others according to the predominance and subordination already indicated. Understand.

*The book is complete; praise is to God alone, and may God bless our master Muḥammad, his family and companions and grant them peace.*

### Integrity and restrictions

The page transcriptions are checked against online **textual transcriptions**, not against photographic scans of the printed pages. The materials in this apparatus do not claim independent manuscript variants, verified punctuation, or diplomatic edition status. Modern editorial footnotes of the 2008 volume are not adopted as part of either medieval author’s text.

## Preserved file: editorial/COMPARATIVE_FINDINGS_STAGE04.md

# GNAMMA | Al-Mahāʾimī Stage 04 — Comparative Findings from printed pp.89–138

**Evidence:** The original Arabic and first-pass translation are in the cumulative file. Page references cite the al-Mazīdī 2008 page-indexed transcription; independent manuscripts, Āshtiyānī’s edition, and parallel critical readings are not yet collated. The comparison below is consequently a structured working interpretation, not a definitive assessment.

## A. Station-relative truth is not “anything goes”

At p.89, Qūnawī and al-Mahāʾimī distinguish a taste primarily related to a particular divine name from the distinctive taste of the most comprehensive station. The latter aspires to correspondence with the truth from a more inclusive horizon. P.116 then explicitly says a contrary formulation can nevertheless be *ṣawāb nisbī*—right in a relative sense. The relationship is not an easy verbal relativism. A restricted statement must be tested for (i) what reality is under consideration, (ii) what names or determinations are operative, (iii) the knower’s station, and (iv) what is suppressed as irrelevant under that restricted aspect. A more comprehensive statement explains rather than simply negates the earlier one. On this criterion, “God alone acts” and “effects are referred to creatures” can be ordered as different attributions, not both accepted as equally exhaustive. The causal model used to support the stronger claim remains philosophically debatable.

## B. Discriminate four operations called “difference”

**First, a conceptual consideration (*iʿtibār*).** Pp.102 and 121–122 mark names and predicates as determinate points of view on the Real; the negative unrestrictedness of the Essence cannot itself be predicated through the ordinary logical forms. Even *absolute existence* predicated as one and necessary occurs under a determinate relation. This is not the same as creating a world or acquiring a new attribute.

**Second, principial determination (*taʿayyun*).** The first determinate principle is the source of further names, and the levels of essential and act-related attributes are ordered by dependence without temporal succession (pp.121–123). The consequence is stronger than saying that humans happen to use different words, but weaker than treating each name as a separately subsisting entity.

**Third, relation (*nisba*) and conditioning.** Mirrors of fixed entities are said not to alter an intrinsically undetermined source. They furnish relations in which concealed plurality becomes manifest (pp.112–116). The particular relation is not the source’s essential constitution, and the reported absence of intrinsic causal efficacy is qualified by the account of conditions.

**Fourth, manifested effect.** Pp.117–130 distinguish *sharṭ*, on which something depends without that condition operating as an efficient producer, from *sabab*, which supplies causal efficacy within the ordered manifestation. The first intelligible effusion does not acquire a separate contingency-form as it passes through loci; its *taʿayyun* becomes intelligible under their restrictions. This is an explicit response to the problem of intermediate causes, not a proof that all ordinary causal mechanisms are illusory.

## C. The brevity of essential self-disclosure: an important source-based answer

On pp.108–109, the special essential disclosure is characterized as *barqī*, shorter than the span of two breaths. Al-Mahāʾimī expressly states that the human faculties do **not cease to exist in reality** when they are withdrawn from attention. Human comprehensiveness (*jamʿiyya*) makes a general closure of other functions possible for a moment but also demands their return; this is why the experience cannot persist in the same exclusive mode. **P.137 supplies independent interpretive confirmation:** the initial flash itself ends, but complete cognition of the divine names, levels and aspects remains in the spirit of the realized knower. The briefness is therefore first of all a description of a *mode of disclosure and human apprehension*, not a measurement of divine reality changing. It remains open whether the word “breath” is entirely phenomenological, a temporal expression for the recipient, or has a further technical meaning in Qūnawī’s broader corpus. One should not settle that question by speculation.

## D. Comprehensiveness differs from absolute union

Pp.132 and 136–137 explicitly allow the Real to be apprehended through names while excluding confinement, *ḥulūl* and *ittiḥād*. An intermediate knower can possess correct yet restricted cognition, while the Perfect Human—having experienced essential disclosure—can grasp the names without letting the names occlude the Essence or vice versa. Thus higher realization does not entail that discursive theology or name-conditioned spirituality is wholly false. It reorders them. The register must retain the distinction between *absence of a separate image in witnessing*, *absence of independent ontological reality*, and *identity in the unqualified divine Essence*.

## E. The level of divine knowledge changes the explanation of possibility

The final pages (pp.137–138) differentiate events impossible in themselves from events rendered non-actual under the contents of prior divine knowledge. The accomplished knower does not seek something absolutely excluded by knowledge of the decree; some decrees are conditional upon prayer, volition or another means, while others are not. This introduces a genuine philosophical challenge: how can condition-dependent events be eternally known without collapsing their contingency, and how can the knower’s will be a real condition rather than merely an appearance? These are not resolved by asserting either Avicennian foreknowledge or Akbarian unity. They demand direct comparison with Avicenna, Ṭūsī, later kalām and Qūnawī's full account of knowledge.

## F. Comparative matrix: provisional tests, not doctrinal equivalences

| Problem | Textual finding in al-Mahāʾimī | Comparative question |
|---|---|---|
| One Being and many determinations | Pp.102, 121–130: predicates, names and recipient-rules belong to several orders | Does Turka’s *taʿayyun* offer the same first-principle relation, or a later explicit reconstruction? |
| Relations of effect | Pp.115–119, 128–129: real difference of conditional relations without change in the Real | Does a Thomistic doctrine of participated created *esse* require an extra ontological principle absent from this model? |
| Unity and degree | Pp.121–123: first determination and nontemporal dependence | How does this differ from Ṣadrā’s intrinsic *tashkīk* of existence? |
| Human realization and temporality | Pp.108–110, 137: lightning disclosure ends; understanding continues | Which rank of cognition is being narrated, and does *nafas* refer to actual time or the knower’s experiential horizon? |
| Unmanifested possibilities | Pp.112–115: fixed entities and their effects distinguished | This does **not** yet demonstrate entities whose manifestation is intrinsically impossible. What would count as such an entity? |
| Scriptural response and causality | Pp.131–138: name-conditioned response and conditional decree | Can the metaphysics make sense of prayer changing the contingent outcome while divine knowledge remains infallible? |

## G. Questions to carry forward

1. Are the categories of *iʿtibār*, *ḥaythiyya*, *nisba*, *taʿayyun*, *shuʾūn* and the *aʿyān* related by an explicit deductive chain, or are some shifts of register only clarified by taste?
2. Does a first effusion have reality distinguishable in thought or in being from the Real's absolute existence?
3. Does p.137's durable knowledge function as a *malaka* of the soul, a nonformal form of knowledge, or something sui generis?
4. What exact principles restrict a spiritual report to one station, and by what criterion can a knower recognize that another is more comprehensive?
5. How can the apparent correctness of competing causal attributions be tested without rendering the differences vacuous?
6. Do the apparently nonproduced fixed entities have a mode of ontic or noetic actuality, or are they only principially distinct from manifested effects?
7. Does the comparative inquiry gain precision by keeping Guénon’s Absolute / Infinite / Universal Possibility separate until each Arabic term is established rather than conflating them with “nothingness”?

**Research standard:** Any future cross-author agreement or contradiction must be established by an original-language, clause-level citation to *both* authors, not by resemblance of technical vocabulary alone.

## Caveats about original text numbering

The independent online transcription uses text labels that do **not** yet have a source-checked one-to-one mapping to all 22 numbered `naṣṣ` sections in the printed commentary. In particular its passage `QUN-NU-019-C` identifies the treatment of affinity while Stage07's commentary section labels were constructed under Text Twenty. Likewise forum passages labelled Text Twenty contain sections about quiddity and existence whose position relative to the printed final Texts Twenty-One and Twenty-Two needs an explicit concordance.

**Do not** create additional links by equating numbers. Match quoted lemma text against the actual 2008 commentary and appendix, keeping internal source text and al-Mahāʾimī's interpretation separate. Whenever an alignment involves the independently edited Qūnawī text, record which printed edition and page supplied it.

## Preserved file: editorial/EDITION_STATUS.md

# Complete bilingual working edition

**Edition date: 11 November 2026 · Stage 13.**

The continuous reader contains the full available Arabic and working English for al-Mahāʾimī’s commentary on Qūnawī, followed by Qūnawī’s separate original text as printed in the same 2008 volume.

| Component | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Al-Mahāʾimī commentary | Printed pp.11–232: 222 pages, represented by 221 entries because pp.18–19 remain one reading unit |
| Qūnawī original appendix | Printed pp.235–267: 33 pages, each with Arabic and a new page-bound English translation |
| Canonical reader | 254 entries; one current version of each reading unit |
| Earlier overlapping Qūnawī material | Preserved separately as 54 historical draft/excerpt entries |
| Commentary translation review against available Arabic | 222/222 pages; source uncertainties remain marked |
| Documented commentary print-image comparison | 98/222 pages; seven previously omitted Stage12 records recovered |
| Qūnawī appendix print-image inspection | 33/33 recorded in Stage12 |
| Independent manuscript collation | None claimed |

The full 2008 electronic transcription and a scan of the printing have been acquired. The scan itself is missing printed pp.113–114; their electronic text is included. Its final commentary page confirms that the unfinished sentence on p.232 is unfinished in the printing, so the edition leaves it unreconstructed.

Substantive review has addressed omitted text, page-boundary drift, reversals of meaning, speaker attribution, and modern footnotes mistakenly incorporated into the medieval body. The [current review ledger](../data/coverage-stage13.json) and [page review index](review-stage13/review-index.json) give the exact completed review coverage. Stage13 completed the remaining 57 commentary-page reviews and applied 85 English passage corrections, 30 editorial notes and three heading corrections. The first passage of p.43 still includes an explicitly marked synopsis of an unstable source argument; it is not certified as a full literal reconstruction. Several other readings remain flagged. The separate [textual notes](TEXTUAL_NOTES.md) explain consequential decisions and unresolved readings.

## Reading and downloads

The [full cumulative handoff and stage archive](../handoffs.html) preserves the entire text, editorial records, reader sources and downloads for reliable continuation. The current release was rebuilt from the working Stage 11 production base; its canonical text remains the recovered Stage 13 edition.

The reader offers English, Arabic, and bilingual views; separate commentary and original-text navigation; search that opens a passage in context; shared-wording cross-references; bookmarks; saved reading position; font and theme controls; and printing of the selected view.

- [English PDF](../downloads/mahaimi-english.pdf)
- [Arabic–English PDF](../downloads/mahaimi-bilingual.pdf)
- [Arabic PDF](../downloads/mahaimi-arabic.pdf)
- [Bilingual Markdown](../downloads/mahaimi-bilingual.md)
- [Structured corpus](../downloads/mahaimi-corpus.json)
- [Offline reader](../index.html)

The full 2008 scan is a primary source link, not one of the project’s republished downloads.

## Scholarly scope

“Complete” describes the available running text and its English translation. It does not certify a manuscript-critical edition, settle every difficult printed reading, or authenticate each quoted report. The commentary, quoted Qūnawī lemmata, separately printed original, and modern apparatus remain distinct. An internal parallel in the same modern volume is not counted as another manuscript witness.

The [source record](SOURCES_STAGE12.md), [terminology glossary](GLOSSARY.md), and earlier research apparatus remain available. The next independent textual task, if pursued, is comparison with actual manuscript images or another commentary edition, especially at the unfinished ending. That research is distinct from the completed bilingual reader and downloads.

## Preserved file: editorial/ENDING_PRINT_WITNESS_STAGE12.md

# Printed ending verified against a facsimile

## Witness acquired

Al-Mahāʾimī, *Mashraʿ al-khuṣūṣ ilā maʿānī al-nuṣūṣ*, edited by Aḥmad Farīd al-Mazīdī (Beirut: Dār al-Kutub al-ʿIlmiyya, 2008). Public Internet Archive item `machra3-khosous`, uploaded 21 April 2014, 269 PDF pages. This is a scan of the same printed edition used by the project's online transcriptions, **not an independent manuscript**.

- Item: https://archive.org/details/machra3-khosous
- PDF: https://archive.org/download/machra3-khosous/machra3-khosous.pdf
- Acquired through the content server advertised in the item's public metadata: https://ia800504.us.archive.org/0/items/machra3-khosous/machra3-khosous.pdf
- SHA-256: `2e4b896446d82bbd877a8c0657e69976a25c366a2d97559194b7ed96c1749b0e`
- Size: 9,738,668 bytes.
- Local source: `machra3-khosous.pdf` in this directory.

## Directly inspected images

| Printed page | PDF page (one-based) | Archive leaf (zero-based) | Observation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 230 | 229 | 228 | End of Text Twenty-One; heading and opening of Text Twenty-Two on this same page. |
| 231 | 230 | 229 | Continuation of Text Twenty-Two and discussion of station-relative disclosures. |
| 232 | 231 | 230 | Final commentary page, syntactically interrupted, followed by an explicit ending formula. |
| 233 | 232 | 231 | Separate title page for Qūnawī's *al-Nuṣūṣ fī taḥqīq al-ṭawr al-makhṣūṣ*. |
| 234 | 233 | 232 | Blank separator. |
| 235 | 234 | 233 | Beginning of the separately printed Qūnawī text. |

The printed commentary p.232 ends its last explanatory sentence:

> بشرط الأعيان، فإذا ظهرت آثار الوجود بشرط.

It then prints, in a separate bold line:

> آخره والحمد لله رب العالمين

**Conclusion:** the interruption is already present in the printed 2008 edition. It is not merely a truncation introduced by the project's online extraction. The scan contains the end of that printed commentary followed by the separate Qūnawī work; it provides no missing complement to the interrupted sentence. The cause of the printed interruption remains undetermined. It could arise at an earlier stage of textual transmission or editing; this scan alone cannot determine which. No conjectural continuation should be supplied as authorial text.

## Readings that must remain distinct

The embedded Qūnawī lemma on printed p.232 reads **أن الظهور في الوجود**, "that manifestation is in existence." Al-Mahāʾimī's explanation later on the same page reads **علمت أن الظهور للوجود**, "you know that manifestation belongs to existence." The separate appendix p.267 has **للوجود** in Qūnawī's text. A translation must retain the difference rather than silently normalizing all three to the same English phrase.

Printed p.230 has **توجب** in the opening final lemma. The previous project's apparatus records **يوجب** in appendix p.267 and **بموجب** in other transcriptions. Treat these as recorded readings of their respective sources; neither the new scan nor their doctrinal plausibility establishes a manuscript-based preferred reading.

## Editorial status

This advances the project from electronic-transcription-only knowledge to direct comparison with a scan of its printed copy-text. It does not establish a critical text against historical manuscripts. The Āshtiyānī edition and Leiden Or.5675 remain independent comparison targets; no new manuscript folio has been inspected in this work. The ending should be labelled **"The 2008 printed commentary breaks off here"**, while retaining the printed closing formula separately.

The page-specific English revisions for pp.230–232 remove material displaced from adjacent pages, restore the final text's opening to p.230, preserve the printed variants, and mark the interrupted ending without completing it.

## Preserved file: editorial/GLOSSARY.md

> **Current edition:** full commentary pp.11–232 and Qūnawī appendix pp.235–267. This context-indexed glossary retains its earlier page-specific research entries; the historical section headings are not coverage limits. New terms and corrections from the complete edition appear at the end.

# Akbarī technical glossary — al-Mahāʾimī and Qūnawī
**Status:** context-sensitive working lexicon. “Attested” means that a term or its explicit construction occurs in the **consulted working text**, *Mashraʿ*, ed. al-Mazīdī, pp.11–72, unless a different source is named. It does not imply an exhaustive count. **Prospective** entries are not retroactively ascribed to pp.11–72. Exact lexical usage and authorial ownership (cited earlier authority vs al-Mahāʾimī) matter.

## A. Metaphysical and logical operations: never translate as one undifferentiated “aspect”

| Arabic | Transliteration | Principal translation; important alternative | Status/context | Required distinction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| الوجود | *al-wujūd* | being, existence; sometimes the unrestricted reality of Being | Attested pp.11,14–19,29,36–38 | The abstract predicative *concept*, independent existence, dependent created existence, and the divine Reality cannot be swapped without local argument |
| وجود الحقّ | *wujūd al-Ḥaqq* | existence/Being of the Real | Attested, e.g. pp.14,18–19,36–37 | Check whether identity, divine self-existence, causal dependence, or phenomenological exclusivity is asserted |
| الوجود المطلق | *al-wujūd al-muṭlaq* | unrestricted Being | **Attested p.39**, and central in p.47; again in commentary proper, M-01 | “Unrestrictedness” is not necessarily an added positive restriction (*bi-sharṭ al-iṭlāq*) |
| الماهيّة / الماهيات | *māhiyya / māhiyyāt* | quiddity/ies; what-it-is | Attested p.19 | Distinguish a possible essence from independently existent substance and from an *ʿayn thābita* |
| العين / الأعيان | *ʿayn / aʿyān* | entity, determination, individual, “fixed entity” where *thābita* is explicit | Attested p.11 and cited passages later | Never translate every *ʿayn* as a *manifest corporeal object* or automatically as a fixed entity |
| الأعيان الثابتة | *al-aʿyān al-thābita* | fixed entities | Examined independently in M-22, now additionally attested in translated pp.61, 77–78; not attested in the *initial* pp.11–38 | Their effects' appearing is not identical with their own appearing; separate ontological from modal claims |
| الإيجاد | *al-ījād* | bringing into existence, existentiation | Attested p.19 and p.29 | A productive/causal relation; not ipso facto the divine Essence. Mahāʾimī objects to al-Rāzī's inference from it to proximity to the Essence at p.19 |
| الموجود | *al-mawjūd* | existent, what exists | Attested | May refer to a real individual or be used under a qualifying relation to God; *mawjūd* ≠ *wujūd* |
| الموجِد / الموجَد | *al-mūjid / al-mūjad* | cause who brings into being / what has been brought into being | Problematic unvowelled transmitted wording p.15 | Explicitly distinguish agent and product; no silent vocalization where grammatically unsecure |
| اعتبار | *iʿtibār* | consideration; an intentional way of regarding a subject | **Attested p.16** in cited Ghazālī; pp.36 elsewhere | A cognitive or philosophical consideration may track an objective foundation; not thereby an extramental object or an arbitrary fiction |
| حيثيّة / من حيث | *ḥaythiyya / min ḥayth* | respect, aspect, insofar as | Attested construction **p.29** (“insofar as existence / insofar as bringing into being”) | Specifies the scope of the predication; does not automatically posit an additional ontic constituent |
| جهة | *jiha* | respect, orientation, aspect, direction | Attested pp.36–37 | May be metaphorical or relational; must not spatialize divine transcendence |
| نسبة / إضافة | *nisba / iḍāfa* | relation, attribution | Attested p.19, and M-22 online | A relation can be objectively grounded and still not be identical to its term, substance, or productive cause |
| تعيّن | *taʿayyun* | determination; becoming determinate | **Attested pp.47,50**, as determinations and explicitly the first determination; developed further in M-01 and M-22 | Must identify whether logical restriction, principial determination, rank of self-disclosure, name, or actual manifested individuation |
| تجلّي | *tajallī* | self-disclosure, disclosure | Attested p.11 and pp.28ff, and online M-20 | Distinguish divine act/reality, its effect in a locus, and the knower's unveiling of the effect |
| مظهر / مظاهر | *maẓhar / maẓāhir* | locus/loci of manifestation | Attested pp.11–12, 37 | The mirror does not become the source of light merely because light is seen in it |
| ظهور / بطون | *ẓuhūr / buṭūn* | manifestation / hiddenness | Attested pp.11,37–38, M-22 | Subject can differ: the Real becomes outward; the fixed entities remain intrinsically unmanifested according to M-22 |
| استعداد / قابلية | *istiʿdād / qābiliyya* | preparedness / receptivity | Attested p.11 and in testimonies p.28; M-20 | A limit in reception, not necessarily limitation of the divine Essence; objective status of preparedness requires argument |

## B. Modes of knowledge, states, and stations

| Arabic | Transliteration | Working rendering | Attestation and caution |
|---|---|---|---|
| نظر / استدلال | *naẓar / istidlāl* | discursive inquiry / inference | p.12, p.19, p.38; distinguishes the theologian's inference from the knower's apprehension; rational discourse is not simply declared false |
| الحدس | *ḥads* | intellectual intuition | p.12; not automatically *kashf* or a spiritual station; spelling of a similar term p.14 appears defective |
| كشف / مكاشفة | *kashf / mukāshafa* | unveiling / direct disclosure | pp.12,16–20, M-22; a true disclosed experience may have a restricted scope even when experientially certain |
| شهود / مشاهدة | *shuhūd / mushāhada* | witnessing / contemplative awareness | pp.16–23, 37; “one sees only God” must be read with its mode of apprehension and station |
| عين اليقين | *ʿayn al-yaqīn* | eye/certainty of direct vision | p.12; distinct from propositional certainty; the larger threefold hierarchy is not proved merely by this occurrence |
| حال / مقام | *ḥāl / maqām* | spiritual state / station | The discourse of maqām and ranks throughout pp.19–36; clarify whether temporary condition or stabilized rank in each cited author's terminology |
| ذوق | *dhawq* | taste, inward experiential realization | M-22 explicitly *al-adhwāq al-nisbiyya*; not a synonym for private opinion or discursive assent |
| جمع | *jamʿ* | gathering, unifying awareness | pp.22–23, 35,37; may be one mode of the knower's awareness rather than an absolute ontological denial of differentiation |
| فرق | *farq* | distinction, differentiation in awareness | pp.22–23; can coexist with gathering according to rank |
| فرق ثان | *farq thānī* | second differentiation | p.23 in cited al-Qushayrī; not simply a relapse into lowest differentiation; agency is apprehended “through God” |
| جمع الجمع | *jamʿ al-jamʿ* | gathering-of-gathering | p.23; its relation to *farq thānī* must be checked in Qushayrī's independent text |
| فناء | *fanāʾ* | effacement, passing-away | pp.19–21,30; distinguish extinction of perception of self from loss of a created hypostasis or true physical death |
| بقاء | *baqāʾ* | subsistence/remain-after-effacement | Relevant to pp.20–23 and further Nuṣūṣ; ascertain whether used literally or inferred from reported return to differentiated seeing |
| سكر / صحو | *sukr / ṣaḥw* | intoxication / sobriety | p.35 probable pair; received Arabic oddly reads «الشكر والصحو», not silently emended |
| تجريد | *tajrīd* | disengagement, abstraction, spiritual detachment | Context-dependent; can be noetic or ascetic, not inevitably a distinct cosmic level |
| التحقيق / محقق | *taḥqīq / muḥaqqiq* | realization, verification / realizer | pp.14,16, etc.; in an Akbarī usage may involve direct realization; not equivalent simply to “scholar” |
| الجمعية | *jamʿiyya* | comprehensiveness / synthetic human integration | p.11 combines *ijmāl* and *tafṣīl*; p.58 describes the Perfect Human; M-20 explicitly links *jamʿiyya* to differing preparedness of the Perfect Human | 
| وحدة / توحيد | *waḥda / tawḥīd* | unity / affirming divine unity | p.14; *tawḥīd* names a judgment, a disciplined form of witnessing, or a realized station depending on context |
| أحدية الجمع والفرق | *aḥadiyyat al-jamʿ wa-l-farq* | integral oneness of gathering and differentiation | M-22 heading/gloss; do not assume the perfected rank simply negates differentiation |

## C. Terms now established by consecutive pp.60–72, and still-open terms

| Arabic | Transliteration | Working translation | Page-specific register and caution |
|---|---|---|---|
| الأسماء الذاتية / الفعلية | *al-asmāʾ al-dhātiyya / al-fiʿliyya* | essential / act-related names | **p.60** distinguishes names indicating nontransitive meanings (e.g. life, knowledge) from names indicating activity beyond the subject (e.g. creation, sustenance); alternative definitions are reported and must remain alternatives |
| الأحدية / الواحدية | *aḥadiyya / wāḥidiyya* | nondifferentiated oneness / all-inclusiveness of differentiated Names | **pp.61–62**: the status of undifferentiated *shuʾūn* differs from distinct fixed entities at the level of knowledge; do not assign independent external existence to every rank |
| التعين الأول / الثاني | *al-taʿayyun al-awwal / al-thānī* | first / second determination | **p.62**: a principial hierarchy of disclosure and knowledge, not an assertion of two separately created things; quoted phrase around *intifāʾ/intiqāʾ al-taʿaddud* textually uncertain |
| الوجود الخارجي / الوجود العقلي / الوجود المطلق | *al-wujūd al-khārijī / al-ʿaqlī / al-muṭlaq* | extramental / intelligible / unrestricted existence | **p.64** explicitly distinguishes the *natural subjects* of three kinds of determinations. The claim is about the determination’s respective context, not that these are three equal substances |
| سراية | *sarāya / sarayān* | pervasion, diffusion, permeation | **pp.63–64** directly rejects *ḥulūl* and physical migration; described by sunlight manifesting in glass. Never translate as material indwelling |
| الحلول | *ḥulūl* | indwelling | **p.63** expressly rejected in the sense of one thing entering another or something confined in space |
| صفاء / استعداد | *ṣafāʾ / istiʿdād* | purity / receptivity | **pp.65–70**: relevant to station-specific ability to receive disclosure, not a limitation of the unrestricted Reality |
| الإنسان الكامل | *al-insān al-kāmil* | Perfect Human | **pp.65–67**: full development of bodily, intellectual and spiritual capacities, not their abolition; counts as a concrete philosophical-psychological argument for comprehensiveness |
| الحقيقة المحمدية | *al-ḥaqīqa al-Muḥammadiyya* | Muhammadan Reality | **pp.68–69**: operative comprehensive name/universal mediation contrasted expressly with the Prophet as created servant; avoid claims of independent divinity |
| الشهود / الجمعية | *al-shuhūd / al-jamʿiyya* | witnessing / integral comprehensiveness | **p.67**: reciprocal seeing of unity in plurality and plurality in unity is a more expansive station than exclusive attention to one alone |
| الحقيقة / الماهية / الهوية | *al-ḥaqīqa / al-māhiyya / al-huwiyya* | reality, quiddity, identity | **p.71**: explicitly differentiated definitions; not three automatic English synonyms for “essence” |
| الإطلاق الذاتي | *al-iṭlāq al-dhātī* | essential unrestrictedness | **p.72, M-01**: no qualified predication (even unity or necessity) under **that respect**; does not mean the Real is simply non-necessary under other respects |

**Still requiring systematic source evidence:** explicit *tajalliyāt dhātiyya barqiyya* (lightning-like essential self-disclosures), the Muhammadan *lā-maqām* (station of no station), whether there are fixed possibilities unable to produce any effects, the full taxonomy of nonformal apprehension, and the precise meanings of *Non-Being* relative to divine possibilities. These are research questions, not retroactive doctrines of pp.11–72.

## Contrast pairs for the definitive edition

- *Wujūd* in first-intentional ontology vs the mental *concept* “existence”; neither entails the other without premise.
- *Min ḥayth al-wujūd* vs *min ḥayth al-ījād*: **p.29**, explicit qualification by al-Nahrajūrī as transmitted by al-Mahāʾimī.
- **One underlying reality** vs **many true attributions** (pp.16,32); these do not eliminate differentiation within scriptural discourse.
- **Phenomenological non-seeing** of creatures (pp.16,19–23) vs **ontological lack of independent existence** (pp.19,25,36–37); neither alone proves literal identity of Creator and creature.
- **Validity in a station** vs **unqualified validity** (M-22 online), with the author's claimed hierarchy itself subject to investigation.

## Related GNAMMA working texts located, not conflated

Existing repository draft: `https://github.com/gnamma-research/booksite/blob/master/texts/al-turka/qawaid-al-tawhid/data/parallel-commentary.md`. It lists 40 introductory, 64 main, and six concluding commentary units. This is a **working edition** with edition N introductory and A main pagination; it is **not** a verified manuscript apparatus. Potential comparative loci recorded in earlier handoff: SH-015, SH-017, SH-035, SH-037, SH-049–052; these are navigation leads, not independently collated al-Mahāʾimī parallels.

## D. Additional contexts newly translated in pp.39–59

| Arabic | Transliteration | Local translation and evidence | Important qualification |
|---|---|---|---|
| الوجود المطلق | *al-wujūd al-muṭlaq* | unrestricted existence, explicitly at p.39, with subsequent metaphysical defence | “Unrestricted” is not equivalent to “a universal in the mind” or to “a genus instantiated in many separate existential subjects” |
| وجوب الوجود بالذات | *wujūb al-wujūd bi-l-dhāt* | necessity of existence in itself; logical target of p.39–49 arguments | Conceptual truth about “existent” must not be mistaken for a syllogistic demonstration of one necessary extramental reality without the argument's added premises |
| المعقولات الثانية | *al-maʿqūlāt al-thāniya* | second intelligibles, p.39 opponent's account | Can be used to deny that the *concept* of existence is an extramental constituent; this is not necessarily denial of real things |
| الاعتبارات العقلية | *al-iʿtibārāt al-ʿaqliyya* | mental considerations, pp.39,47–49 | For al-Mahāʾimī these can indicate real determinations without multiplying Being itself. Distinguish operation of intellection from its object |
| الوجود العيني | *al-wujūd al-ʿaynī* | extramental / concrete existence, p.41 and p.47 | Do not treat this as univocally identical with *wujūd* in all appearances; object/subject distinction disputed in argument |
| التعيّن الأول | *al-taʿayyun al-awwal* | first determination, p.50 symbolic unpacking of letters in the divine Name | The current **source context is letter symbolism**, not a fully defined technical scheme of first/second taʿayyun |
| العلم اليقين / علم اليقين | *ʿilm al-yaqīn* | knowledge of certainty, pp.50–56 | Author differentiates species of demonstrations, calmness, and modes of knowing |
| عين اليقين | *ʿayn al-yaqīn* | eye of certainty, pp.50,55–56 | Different disclosures by imagination, spirits, intellect, and divine knowledge are listed; check exact taxonomy |
| حق اليقين | *ḥaqq al-yaqīn* | reality of certainty, pp.50,55–56 | Can refer to acts, names, attributes, self-effacement and survival; do not flatten stages |
| الهمّة / الهمم | *himma / himam* | spiritual aspiration; pp.50–54 | Spiritual directing of resolve, not merely subjective desire |
| سكينة / طمأنينة | *sakīna / ṭumaʾnīna* | stillness / tranquillity, pp.54–56 | Distinct signs of attained certitude; do not convert to truth conditions of all propositions |
| الأسفار | *al-asfār* | journeys, p.57 | p.57 explicitly describes four journeys, including the return to creatures; not simply three ontological levels |
| النفس | *al-nafs* | soul/self; p.57 in one passage “subtle animal vapour” | The same word can denote appetite and psychologically mediating spirit, not the entire immortal rational soul in every author's usage |
| المعرفة | *maʿrifa* | recognition or gnosis, p.58 explicitly two meanings | (i) knowledge of hidden by outward sign; (ii) recognition of what was formerly witnessed. Do not translate both without gloss |
| مراتب الوجود | *marātib al-wujūd* | ranks of existence, p.58 | Transcription says **six** but visibly enumerates **seven** including the all-comprehensive human; no correction until textual collation |
| الإنسان الكامل | *al-insān al-kāmil* | Perfect Human, p.58, M-20 online | Human comprehensiveness is not the same as a quantitative aggregate of distinct bodies |
| المظاهر | *al-maẓāhir* | manifestation sites, p.58–59 | Mirror-language needs independent grounding for what is objectively actual vs manifest to a knower |

## Stage 3 additions: exact local senses and philosophical operations, pp.70–78

| Expression | Working English | Location | Doctrinal restriction |
|---|---|---|---|
| الحقيقة / الماهية / الهوية | extramental reality / what-it-is / individuating identity | p.71, al-Mahāʾimī’s three definitions | These are distinct terms and are not all “essence”; compare his usage to Ibn Turka rather than silently importing it |
| الحال / المقام | passing spiritual state / settled spiritual station | p.70 | Station is a stabilized condition; distinguish doctrinal truth from the knower's relative perception |
| الحظ الاختصاصي | singular personally allotted share | pp.70–71 | Unrepeatability of a self-disclosure is not a general claim that general species of disclosure never recur |
| الإطلاق الذاتي | intrinsic unrestrictedness | pp.72–75, Naṣṣ 1 | Not the ordinary binary predicate “unrestricted rather than restricted”; it is free from that binary too |
| التعين الأول | first determination | pp.73,75–77 | Aḥadiyya and intrinsic knowledge relation; do not conflate with manifest separate being |
| التعين الثاني | second determination | p.75 | Influence and productive attribution as understood here; no independent created object entailed by this label alone |
| الامتياز النسبي | relational distinction | p.75 | Qūnawī explicitly denies *real* distinction in the first determination |
| الامتياز الحقيقي | real distinction | p.75 | Used of wāḥidiyya; **do not** assume univocal equivalence with scholastic *distinctio realis* |
| النسبة العلمية الذاتية | intrinsic knowledge relation | pp.75–76 | Intellectually first relation, distinct from life-relation as first actual prerequisite |
| تعقل كلي / تعقل تفصيلي | universal / detailed cognition | pp.75–78 | Modes of understanding, not unqualified temporal parts in divine knowing |
| التقدم الطبيعي / تأخر الرتبة | natural priority / posterior rank | p.78 | Order of dependence distinguished explicitly from efficient causal production or temporal succession |
| التعلق | intentional relation of knowledge to object | p.78 | Change in the object's temporal qualification need not entail change in eternal knowing |
| المفصل في المجمل | differentiated within the undifferentiated | p.78 | Like potential fruit in a seed: a cognitive/manifestational analogy, not proof of numerical identity of seed and every actual fruit |
| الشهود العلمي / العيني | witnessing in knowledge / witnessing in concrete existence | p.78 | Fixed entities remain unmanifest *as fixed entities*, even where actual manifestations have effects |

**Caution:** The terms above are attested in the *online 2008 working Arabic*, not verified in the 2000–01 Āshtiyānī edition or a manuscript.


## New evidence from pp.79–88 (attested source, uncollated working translation)

| Arabic | Transliteration | Working rendering | Location and specific meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| استهلاك الوحدة في الكثرة | *istihlāk al-waḥda fī l-kathra* | absorption of unity into multiplicity | **p.79**: one existence is hidden in many extramental quiddities; the plurality of loci is real, yet the original existence is not multiplied in itself |
| الماهيات الخارجية | *al-māhiyyāt al-khārijiyya* | extramental quiddities | **p.79**: outwardly different mirrors of the one existence; contrast mental quiddities and the divine known entities |
| الإطلاق المقابل للتقييد | *al-iṭlāq al-muqābil li-l-taqyīd* | unrestrictedness opposed to restriction | **p.80**: narrower *iʿtibār* distinct from essential unrestrictedness transcending the pair altogether (p.74) |
| الاقتضاء / اللا اقتضاء | *al-iqtiḍāʾ / al-lā-iqtiḍāʾ* | demand or necessitating requirement / non-demand | **pp.80–83**: neither may exclusively qualify the Real under unrestrictedness; one effusion receives three conditional descriptions by rank |
| الفيض الذاتي / الأقدس | *al-fayḍ al-dhātī / al-aqdas* | essential / Most Holy Effusion | **pp.81–82**: prior in intelligibility to recipient and preparedness; does not itself imply externally prior time |
| الشرط / السبب / الواسطة | *al-sharṭ / al-sabab / al-wāsiṭa* | condition / cause or necessitating factor / intermediary | **pp.81–82**: a condition does not itself create; some causes are described as non-efficient; not interchangeable with true originating divine agency |
| العقل الأول | *al-ʿaql al-awwal* | First Intellect | **pp.81–83**: identified as the single positive condition mediating one rank of the effusion; doctrinally not the “general existence” itself |
| الوجود العام | *al-wujūd al-ʿāmm* | general existence | **p.83**: al-Mahāʾimī identifies universal effusion with this, while explicitly distinguishing the philosophical and theological causal accounts |
| التعلق | *al-taʿalluq* | relation / intentional connection | **pp.83–84**: what changes according to the known object, without change in intrinsic divine knowledge |
| الحكم / الحاكم / المحكوم عليه | *al-ḥukm / al-ḥākim / al-maḥkūm ʿalayh* | judgement or ruling / judging agent / recipient of judgement | **pp.84–86**: qualified relations depend on the state of both sides; neither subjective whim nor a temporal alteration of the Essence |
| العلم يتبع الوجود | *al-ʿilm yatbaʿ al-wujūd* | knowledge follows existence | **pp.86–88**: inseparable concomitance at its most universal level; degrees of manifestation of knowledge depend on receptivity |
| غلبة أحكام الإمكان / الوجوب | *ghalabat aḥkām al-imkān / al-wujūb* | dominance of rulings of possibility / necessity | **p.88**: character of manifestation in contingent recipients, **not** independent necessity belonging to minerals, plants or animals |

The glossary is cumulative and context-indexed: the same transliteration may require different English in another ontological or epistemic register. Existing terms remain subject to collation.


## D. Stage 04 lexicon — source-anchored, perspective-conditioned senses (pp.89–138)

| Arabic term | Transliteration | Local meaning | Printed page(s) | Distinction / caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| إطلاق سلبي / إطلاق ذاتي | *iṭlāq salbī / iṭlāq dhātī* | negative / essential unrestrictedness | pp.102,121–122 | Pure absence of predicates under a specific negative respect; not a temporal or spatial emptiness. |
| التعين الأول | *al-taʿayyun al-awwal* | first principial determination | pp.98–103,121–122 | Principle of intelligible ordering; not the pure unrestricted Essence nor an independent material thing. |
| التعين الثاني | *al-taʿayyun al-thānī* | second determination | pp.101–103 | Aspect under which necessary, one existence is predicated in a knowable relation. |
| الحيثية | *al-ḥaythiyya* | aspect or respect | pp.89–103,136–137 | Controls truth of a proposition and scope of cognition; not identical to a separate existent. |
| الاعتبار | *al-iʿtibār* | consideration | pp.89,102,115,129,137 | A warranted explanatory angle, possibly grounded in determinations, not merely a subjective fiction. |
| الحقيقة / العين الثابتة | *al-ḥaqīqa / al-ʿayn al-thābita* | reality / fixed entity | pp.112–115,130 | Fixed intelligible form versus its appearance/effects; do not equate its fixity with extramental actuality. |
| الشأن / الشؤون | *al-shaʾn / al-shuʾūn* | divine affair(s) | pp.115,130 | Relates fixed entities to inward divine affairs under the commentator’s exposition. |
| الأثر / التأثير | *al-athar / al-taʾthīr* | effect / exerting influence | pp.112–120 | Denied as extrinsic change in intrinsic reality in specific context; conditional and relational differences remain. |
| المرآة / المرائي | *al-mirʾāh / al-marāyā* | mirror / mirrors | pp.114–116 | A locus through which previously nonmanifest plurality is reflected; does not modify the intrinsic reality of the reflected. |
| النسبة / النسب | *al-nisba / al-nisab* | relation / relations | pp.115–116,129 | Relations of outward attribution may multiply without multiplication of the unrestricted source. |
| التجلي الذاتي البرقي | *al-tajallī al-dhātī al-barqī* | lightning-like essential disclosure | pp.108–111,136–137 | Brief distinctive witnessing of essential reality, not equivalent to the permanent understanding it subsequently produces. |
| الفراغ | *al-farāgh* | emptied awareness, disengagement | pp.108–109 | Withdrawal of attention from body/soul/attributes; expressly not the nonexistence of faculties. |
| الجمعية | *al-jamʿiyya* | comprehensiveness | pp.108–110,137 | Human synthetic completeness which both permits essential disclosure and requires a return to other faculties. |
| الحق النسبي | *al-ḥaqq al-nisbī* | relative / perspective-qualified truth | p.116 | What is correct according to one attribution but not exhaustive of the comprehensive station. |
| من حيث هو هو | *min ḥaythu huwa huwa* | in respect of what it is in itself | pp.117–119 | Key restricted causal consideration; excludes extrinsic conditions that alter outcomes. |
| الشرط / السبب | *al-sharṭ / al-sabab* | condition / cause | pp.118–119,128–129 | Condition: depends on it without efficacy. Cause: depends on it with efficacy (under this commentary’s definition). |
| المؤثر / المنفعل | *al-muʾaththir / al-munfaʿil* | agent / recipient | pp.118–120 | Subject of explanatory causal analogy, conditioned by appropriate relation or additional factor. |
| عدم التكرار في التجلي | *ʿadam al-tikrār fī al-tajallī* | nonrepetition of self-disclosure | pp.120–121 | No two identical appearances in all respects; argument classified as persuasive by the commentator. |
| برهان التطبيق | *burhān al-taṭbīq* | proof by correspondence / matching | pp.120–121 | Scholastic argument against endless regress; not to be mistaken for empirical infinity of chronological events. |
| حمل المواطأة / الاشتقاق | *ḥaml al-muwāṭaʾa / al-ishtiqāq* | direct predication / derivative predication | p.122 | Distinct logical forms of attributing names or properties, neither directly applied to pure negative unrestrictedness. |
| الحدوث الذاتي | *al-ḥudūth al-dhātī* | essential posteriority / dependent origination | p.123 | Hierarchy of dependence without temporal beginning; historical controversy with kalām remains. |
| العطاء الذاتي / الأسمائي | *al-ʿaṭāʾ al-dhātī / al-asmāʾī* | essential / name-related divine gift | pp.123–126 | Different predominant reference aspects, not literally gifts removed from all relations. |
| السؤال الاستعدادي / الحالي | *al-suʾāl al-istiʿdādī / al-ḥālī* | petition through preparedness / condition | p.127 | Nonverbal mode of asking through receptivity or spiritual state. |
| الفيض الأقدس | *al-fayḍ al-aqdas* | Most Holy Effusion | p.127 | Ground of receptive preparedness in the eternal intelligible order; not yet an extramental event. |
| الفيض المعنوي الأول | *al-fayḍ al-maʿnawī al-awwal* | first intelligible effusion | pp.128–130 | Unitary principial effusion, which becomes distinct under receptivities without superadded contingent rule. |
| القوابل | *al-qawābil* | recipients / receptive loci | pp.128–130 | Rulings of the Outward that correspond to fixed entities, according to context; not separate primordial creators. |
| الظاهر / الباطن | *al-Ẓāhir / al-Bāṭin* | Outward / Inward (divine names) | p.130 | Names or aspects of disclosure; unity of inwardness is not opposed to plurality under outward manifestation. |
| المطاوعة الإلهية | *al-muṭāwaʿa al-ilāhiyya* | divine responsive accommodation | pp.131–132 | Expressly called metaphorical; never divine subordination to a human command. |
| تصور / معرفة / شهود | *taṣawwur / maʿrifa / shuhūd* | apprehension / knowledge / direct witnessing | pp.131–137 | Correct representation of divine aspects must not confine the Real in an image; stations alter epistemic scope. |
| المعية الإلهية | *al-maʿiyya al-ilāhiyya* | divine accompaniment, withness | pp.134–135 | Relation of names/attributes to creation, not corporeal occupancy or identity of unrestricted Essence. |
| المضطر / الاضطرار | *al-muḍṭarr / al-iḍṭirār* | distressed petitioner / existential necessity | pp.133–135 | An immediate receptive state that may produce response without elaborate intellectual representation. |
| لوح محفوظ / مقام قلمي | *lawḥ maḥfūẓ / maqām qalamī* | Preserved Tablet / Pen-rank | pp.137–138 | Rank-relative knowing of divine determination, interpreted through Universal Soul / First Intellect. |
| المقدّر الجازم / المعلّق | *al-muqaddar al-jāzim / al-muʿallaq* | definitive / conditional decree | p.138 | Distinguishes what is fixed from what occurs under appointed conditions, including prayer or aspiration. |
| الاستحالة بالعلم | *al-istiḥāla bi-l-ʿilm* | impossibility relative to divine knowledge | p.138 | Not necessarily an intrinsic contradiction; cannot happen contrary to veridical antecedent divine knowledge. |

**Lexical qualification:** the definitions above are local to the cited printed passages and not asserted as univocal meanings across Qūnawī, Ibn ʿArabī, al-Farghānī and Ibn Turka. Manuscripts have not been inspected.

This is exact lexical overlap in the **same edition**, not evidence from an independent MS. `data/appendix-lemma-concordance-stage11.json`.

- **New manuscript identified:** Leiden University Libraries **Or. 5675**, 362 Arabic folios, dated 1142 AH (1729–30), once owned by Sultan Muḥammad Shifāʾ of Banten. Wittkam's *Inventory*, vol.6 (Leiden 2007), printed p.183. A.C.S. Peacock reports copyist Muḥyī al-Dīn b. Shaykh ʿAbd al-Shakūr b. ʿAbd al-Karīm b. al-Sulṭān Abū al-Mafākhir; his figure captions identify beginning and colophon imagery. The Gregorian conversion 1142/1749 in one figure caption is inconsistent: 1142 AH is 1729–30 CE. This is a **catalogue-authenticated acquisition target**, not a collated text.

DOI 10.5617/jais.12698. Record as interlinear teaching/reception evidence, distinct from the Arabic textual witness itself.
