      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī, reporting al-Rāzī (continuing):** —those things of it, its qualification by them, and its reception of them differ. The division just given returns, until it follows that only one thing can be denied of the one insofar as it is one, that it can be qualified by only one thing, and that it can receive only one thing.\n\n**Al-Ṭūsī, quoted in reply:** “Denying one thing of another, one thing's qualification by another, and one thing's reception of another are matters not realized by the existence of just one thing. They do not follow from the one insofar as it is one, but require more than one antecedent thing, so that these matters follow for those things under differing considerations. The proceeding of many things from many things is not impossible.\n\n“To explain: negation requires the prior establishment of both what is negated and that of which it is negated; the latter's establishment alone does not suffice. Qualification likewise requires a qualified subject and an attribute, and receptivity a recipient and something received. Difference in what is received, such as blackness and motion, requires a difference in the recipient's condition. A body receives blackness insofar as it is affected by another, and receives motion insofar as it has a condition that does not [prevent] its departure from it. But for the proceeding of one thing from another it suffices to posit a single thing, the cause. Otherwise it would be impossible for all effects to depend upon one principle.\n\n“Do not say that proceeding, too, is realized only after both a source and something proceeding are realized. We answer: ‘proceeding’ has two meanings. One is a relation accruing to cause and effect insofar as both are together; this is not our subject. The second is the cause's being such that an effect proceeds from it. In this sense it precedes the effect and then the relation accruing to both. This is our subject. It is one matter if the effect is one. That matter may be the very essence of the cause, if the cause causes through itself. Or it may be a state accruing to the cause, if it causes not through itself but according to another state. If the effects are more than one, that matter must differ, and multiplicity within the essence of the cause follows, as already stated.” End of quotation.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** It has also been objected that bringing into existence is impossible without two things proceeding: quiddity and existence. Again, the central point stands in relation to [many] points; the concept of its being opposite one point differs from the concept of its being opposite—",
      "ar": "تلك الأشياء عنه ، واتصافه بتلك الأشياء ، وقبوله لتلك الأشياء مختلفة ويعود التقسيم المذكور ، حتى يلزم الواحد من حيث هو واحد ، لا يسلب عنه إلا واحد ، ولا يوصف إلا بواحد ، ولا يقبل إلا واحدا . \n\nوأجاب الطوسي : إن سلب الشيء عن الشيء ، واتصاف الشيء بالشيء ، وقبول الشيء للشيء أمور لا يتحقق عن وجود شيء واحد لا غير ، فإنه لا يلزم الشيء الواحد من حيث هو واحد ، بل يستدعي وجود أشياء فوق واحد يتقدمه حتى تلزم تلك الأمور لتلك الأشياء باعتبارات مختلفة ، وصدور الأشياء الكثيرة عن الأشياء الكثيرة ليس بمحال . \n\nوبيانه : إن السلب يفتقر إلى ثبوت مسلوب ومسلوب عنه يتقدمانه ، ولا يكفي فيه ثبوت المسلوب عنه فقط ، وكذلك الاتصاف فيفتقر إلى ثبوت موصوف وصفة ، والقابلية إلى قابل ومقبول ، واختلاف المقبول كالسواد والحركة يفتقر إلى اختلاف حال القابل ، فإن الجسم يقبل السواد من حيث ينفعل عن غيره ، ويقبل الحركة من حيث يكون له حال لا ينفع خروجه عنها . \nوأما صدور الشيء عن الشيء أمر يكفي في تحققه في فرض شيء واحد هو العلة ، وإلا امتنع استناد جميع المعلولات إلى مبدأ واحد . \n\nلا يقال : الصدور أيضا لا يتحقق إلا بعد تحقق شيء يصدر عنه ، وشيء صادر ؛ لأنّا نقول : الصدور يطلق على معنيين : أحدهما أمر إضافي يعرض العلة والمعلول من حيث يكونان معا وكلامنا ليس فيه ، والثاني كون العلة بحيث يصدر عنها المعلول ، وهو بهذا المعنى متقدم على المعلول ، ثم على الإضافة العارضة لهما وكلامنا فيه ، وهو أمر واحد إن كان المعلول واحدا ، وذلك الأمر قد يكون هو ذات العلة بعينها إن كانت العلة علة لذاتها ، وقد يكون حالة يعرض لها ، إن كانت علة لا لذاتها ، بل بحسب حالة أخرى . \n\nأما إذا كان المعلول فوق واحد ، فلا محالة يكون ذلك الأمر مختلفا ، فيلزم منه التكثر في ذات العلة كما مر ، انتهى . \nوقد عورض بأن الإيجاد لا يمكن بدون صدور الاثنين : الماهية والوجود ، بأن النقطة المركزية محاذية للنقاط دون مفهوم كونها محاذية لنقطة غير مفهوم كونها محاذية",

      "printed_page": 205,
      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —another. If one or both of these [relations] were intrinsic to the central point, composition in it would follow. Otherwise the point would be their source, and either composition or an infinite regress would follow. Again, substantiality causes spatial occupancy and the reception of existent accidents: two effects of something simple. Do not say that one is in respect of a state and the other in respect of a place, for our discussion concerns its receptivity to both, which is among the accidents of its essence.\n\nThe answer is that quiddity is not made. Even if we grant that it is made, it is described as preceding existence, which is its attribute. Do not say that making it is precisely obtaining its existence; we answer that then the quiddity is not made. It remains as it was, but has been qualified by existence.\n\nThe central point's being opposite a point on the circumference is in respect of the relation between them; this differs from the relation between it and another point on the circumference. The two oppositions therefore do not arise from one aspect. The cause of each relation is the central point together with a point on the circumference. The argument about substance is complete only if its simplicity is established, both matters are established as existent, and the plurality of grounds and conditions is excluded: it receives spatial occupancy because it has position, and accidents because it is a substrate.\n\nIt may be said: if only one proceeds from the one, [one would produce one other], and so on to the last of existents. This is false: Zayd is plainly not the cause of ʿAmr, nor vice versa. Al-Ṭūsī answers in his treatise: more than one may proceed from the one when it is not considered [in isolation from] something else. For example, when one other proceeds from the one, another, B, may proceed from the two together; then another, C, from it together with B; then one other from every pair. Thus it does not follow that either of two things is the cause of the other: one may belong to one chain and the other to another.\n\nIt may be said: if one proceeds from Him and then another from Him together with the first, His effect upon the first is unconditional, while His effect upon the second is conditional upon the first. Being the source of the first unconditionally differs from being the source of the second conditionally; either composition or an infinite regress follows. We answer: we do not grant that the First alone acts upon the third. What acts is the aggregate, and the composition is in that aggregate.\n\nMoreover, we say that it would follow that one of two things caused the other only if the first effect—",
      "ar": "لأخرى ، فإن كان أحدهما أو كلاهما داخلا في النقطة المركزية لزم تركيبها ، وإلا لا تكون النقطة مصدرا لهما ، وللزم إما التركيب أو التسلسل ، وأيضا الجوهرية علة للتحيز والقبول للأعراض الوجودية ، فهما أثران لبسيط . \nلا يقال : أحدهما باعتبار الحال ، والآخر باعتبار الحيز ؛ لأنّا نقول الكلام في قابليته لهما ، وهو من عوارض ذاته . \nوالجواب : أن الماهية غير مجعولة ، ولو سلمنا أنها مجعولة ، فهي موصوفة بتقدم على الوجود الذي هو صفتها . \n\nلا يقال : جعلها عين تحصيل وجودها ، لأنا نقول : فليست الماهية مجعولة بل هي مستقرة على ما كانت لكنها وصفت بالوجود ، ومحاذاة نقطة المركز لنقطة من المحيط باعتبار ما بينهما من النسبة ، وهي غير النسبة التي بينهما وبين أخرى من المحيط ، فليس المحاذاتان من جهة واحدة ، وعلة كل نسبة نقطة المركز مع نقطة من المحيط ، وكون الجوهر لها إنما يتم ببيان بساطته ، وكون الأمرين وجودين ، وانتفاء تعدد الأدلة والشرط على قبول التحيز ، لكونه إذا وضع ، وللأعراض لكونه محلا . \n\nقيل : لو لم يصدر عن الواحد إلا الواحد يلزم أن لا يوجد الواحد واحدا آخر ، وعلى هذا إلى آخر الموجودات ، وذلك باطل ، ضرورة أن زيدا ليس علة عمرو وبالعكس . \nوأجاب عنه الطوسي في رسالته : إن الواحد الذي لا أعتبر معه شيئا آخر ، جاز أن يصدر عنه أكثر من واحد ، مثلا إذا صدر عن الواحد واحدا آخر ، يجوز أن يصدر مع واحد آخر - كب - وعنه مع - ب - آخر ( كج ) ، ثم مع كل اثنين واحد آخر ، وعلى هذا فلا يلزم كون كل واحد من الشيئين على الآخر لجواز أن يكون أحدهما من سلسلة ، والآخر من سلسلة أخرى . \n\nقيل : لو صدر عنه واحد ، ثم معه آخر له تأثير في الأول بلا شرط ، وفي الثانية بشرط الأول ، فكونه للأول بلا شرط غير كونه مصدرا للثاني بالشرط ، ويلزم إما التركيب والتسلسل . \n\nقلنا : لا نسلم أن الأول مؤثر في الثالث ، بل المؤثر هو المجموع والتركيب فيه . \nعلى أنّا نقول ، إنما يلزم أن يكون أحد الشيئين علة للآخر ، إن كان المعلول الأول",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —were one existent in every respect. But the effect must have an existence proceeding from the Necessary, and a quiddity receiving it through possibility. Something else may therefore proceed from the first effect in respect of each constituent.\n\nOnce you know this, we say that the author mentioned the impossibility of the one ‘manifesting’ [more than one] so that one should not suppose the prohibition to concern only origination and to exclude the Sufis' account of things as manifestations. [The printed sentence is defective.]\n\nThe view that more than one cannot proceed from what is one in every respect is subject to the scholars' denunciation because it entails things interposed between the Real and daily occurrences and other things, in such a way that He would be unable to originate them without [these intermediaries; the printed transition is defective]. For this reason they declared the philosophers who hold it unbelievers. The shaykh rejects what entails that consequence while accepting the principle. He says: for us that one is general, absolute, simple existence. Its multiplicity does not contradict its true unity; likewise the relations and subtle connections in the First Intellect.\n\nThis existence is effused upon all the entities of possible things and their realities fixed in eternal knowledge. Yet eternal knowledge concerns the existence of things. General existence is connected with them potentially from eternity, while their actual manifestation follows the order. This existence is also common to all the other existents, even daily occurrences, so that all depend upon God without an intermediary.       "ar": "موجودا واحدا من جميع الوجوه ، فإن المعلول لا بدّ من وجود صدر عن الواجب ، وماهية يقبله من إمكان ، فيجوز أن يصدر من المعلول الأول لكل جزء وشيء آخر . \nوإذا عرفت هذا ، \n\nفنقول : إنما قال المصنف رضي اللّه عنه :  “ لا استحالة إظهار الواحد ؛ لئلا يتوهم أن الواحد إنما يمتنع عنه صدور الواحد ، لإظهاره عن مذهب الصوفية في الأشياء ، فأشار إليه ليفهم العموم صريحا ، ثم لما كان هذا المذهب إلى امتناع صدور أكثر من واحد ، من الواحد من كل الوجوه محل تشنيع العلماء ؛ \n\nلاستلزامه وجود الأشياء المتوسطة بين الحق والحوادث اليومية ، وغيرها بحيث يعجز عن إيجاد بدون مشرب هذه الطائفة ، \nفلذلك كفّروا القائلين به من الفلاسفة ، منع الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه ما يستلزم ذلك من قبول الأصل ، فقال : لكن ذلك الواحد عندنا هو الوجود العالم المطلق البسيط ، وتكثره لا ينافي وحدته الحقيقية ، \nكذلك النسب والرقائق في العقل الأول ، فهذا الوجود فاض على جميع أعيان الممكنات ، والحقائق الثابتة لها في العلم الأزلي ، فأبعد منها في الحال والماضي لم توجد ، فإنه محال وإن كان بالغير ، وقد سبق العلم الأزلي بأنه لا يوجد ، ولكن العلم الأزلي يتعلق بوجود الأشياء ، وكذلك تعلق بذلك الوجود العام في الأزل بالقوة ، ولكن ظهورها بالفعل تابع للنظام ، ويتعلق العلم بكل شيء وعلى ما هو عليه . \n\nوهذا الوجود العام مشترك بين القلم الأعلى الذي هو أول موجود بذلك الوجود العام ، كما ورد في الحديث :  “ أول ما خلق اللّه القلم  “  “ 1  “ . \nوهو المسمى بالعقل الأول ، حيث قال صلى اللّه عليه وسلم :  “ أول ما خلق اللّه العقل  “  “ 2  “ ، وسمي قلما ؛ لأنه مبدأ التدوين والتسطير . \nوعقلا بكونه مجردا ، ولبيان سائر الموجودات حتى الحوادث اليومية حتى يستند الجميع إلى اللّه تعالى بلا واسطة وليس معلوله عزّ وجلّ منحصرا فيه ، كما يقوله أهل النظر من الفلاسفة  “ 3  “ . \nقيد أهل النظر لهم ؛ لأن سائر المتكلمين غير المعتزلة ينفون الفرع مع الأصل ؛",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —because in their view both necessarily entail an intermediary between Him and all other existents. The shaykh then rejects this intermediary because it would be between a thing and itself: in reality there is only the Real. The world is nothing additional to realities known to God. Initially they have nothing in existence apart from their establishment in His knowledge; then they are qualified by external existence. An intermediary would therefore be either between Him and His existence, which is His very self; between Him and other realities; or between Him and the aggregate of the world's existence and its realities.\n\nHe indicates the invalidity of the second possibility as follows:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “The realities, in respect of their being known and the determination of their forms in the Real's essential, eternal knowledge, cannot be made: originated things cannot subsist in the Essence of the Real, and the Real cannot be a container for another or be contained. There are other corrupt consequences that are evident to those with insight. Understand.\n\n“For this reason they are not described as made by realized people of unveiling, or by realized speculative thinkers. What is made is existence; what has no existence is not made. If it were otherwise, eternal knowledge would have an effect upon the determination of its objects within it from eternity, although they are not external to the one who knows them. To affirm that they are made would therefore require either their co-presence in existence with their knower, or that their knower be a locus receiving an effect from himself within himself, and also a container for another, as stated. All this is false, for it impugns the purity of His unity and entails that effused existence accrues as an accident to already existent things, not nonexistent ones. All this is impossible, because it obtains what is already obtained, and for other reasons there is no need to discuss at length. Understand.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** It is thus established that in the respect mentioned they are not made. There are not two existences, as we have said: existence is one, common to all of them and received from the Real. An intermediary between the Real and the realities of the world could be conceived only if those realities were made. But in respect of their being known to the Real—the determination of their forms in His essential, eternal knowledge—they cannot be made. The realities are realized in this respect, apart from existence, before the world. This respect has therefore belonged to them from eternity and is everlasting.\n\nIn respect of their being forms known to someone other than God, or known to Him through the manifestation of His knowledge in loci of manifestation, they may be made; but this is an incidental matter. Insofar as they are realities, they are not made. Their being made in the former respect is impossible because that knowledge does not differ from the Essence in any way. It shares the Essence's immunity from originated things subsisting within it. Moreover, what subsists in that knowledge, an attribute of the Real, subsists in the Real. If—",

      "printed_page": 208,
      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —they were made, they would be originated, and could not subsist in the Essence of the Real or in His inseparable, eternal attribute. If those realities did not subsist in the Real or in knowledge while being established there, they would either inhere [in Him] or be substrates for Him, and all of this is impossible. To make them made also entails other corrupt consequences evident to those with insight. For these reasons realized people of unveiling, and realized speculative philosophers, do not describe them as made.\n\nHe then explains those corrupt consequences, after indicating that they are so clear that every realized knower accepts them: what is made is external existence, and what is not external is not made. The entities have no existence, even though existence appears through them, upon them, and is attributed to them.\n\nMoreover, if quiddities were made—and there is no doubt that they are known to God, since His eternal knowledge encompasses all—they would first have originated in His eternal knowledge. They would not originate from the Essence as such, because of its independence of everything. Eternal knowledge would therefore have an effect upon the determination of its objects within it, although its objects are not external to their knower: they subsist in the knowledge that subsists in Him. Rather, they are nonexistent for themselves and have no existence except through the Real, since He is absolute existence. Their existence is not external, so it could only be within the essence of their knower.\n\nIf their being made were affirmed, they would either be originated from eternity, co-present in existence with their knower—but temporal origination from eternity is impossible—or not co-present, but originated within His Essence. Their knower would then either be His very self, making Him a locus receiving an effect from Himself in Himself, or be other than Him, making Him a container for another. He transcends being a container or something contained.\n\nHe then invalidates all of this by an argument suited to divine unity: God is one in every respect in His eternity. This would impugn the purity of His unity, since differing realities would exist alongside Him with independent existence [the following printed transition is unclear]. Furthermore, if they were made, they would be existent; existence effused upon them would then be an accident of things already existent. Existence would be repeated upon them: obtaining what is already obtained. This is impossible for that reason and for others that need not be discussed at length.\n\nFor example: the quiddities would then be realized by existence while it was absent. Or: if they were made, humanity would, when not made, be [not] humanity. It would therefore be denied of itself, which is—",
      "ar": "كانت مجعولة لكانت حادثة ، فيمتنع قيامها بذات الحق وصفته اللازمة القديمة أيضا . \nفإن لم تكن تلك الحقائق قائمة بالحق ، ولا يعلم وهي ثابتة هناك ، فهي إما حالة أو محال له ، والكل محال ، على أن في جعلها مجعولة ، مفاسد أخرى لا تخفى على المستبصر ، وتلك المفاسد لا توصف بالجعل عند المحققين من أهل الكشف ، ومن أهل النظر من الحكماء أيضا . \n\nثم بيّن تلك المفاسد بعد الإشارة إلى كونها في غاية الوضوح بحيث يسلمها كل محقق بأن المجعول هو الوجود الخارجي ، فما لا يكون في الخارج لا يكون مجعولا ، والأعيان لا وجود لها وإن ظهر بها الوجود ، وظهر عليها وأضيف إليها . \n\nوأيضا لو كانت الماهيات مجعولة ، ولا شك أنها معلومات للحق تعالى لشمول علمه الأزلي على الكل ، لكان أول حدثت في علمه الأزلي ، ولم يوجد عن الذات من حيث هي ؛ لغنائها عن الكل ، فكان للعلم القديم أثر في تعين معلوماته فيه ، مع أن المعلومات غير خارجة عن العالم بها ؛ لأنها قائمة بالعلم القائم به ، بل هي قائمة ؛ لأنها معدومة لأنفسها ، فلا وجود لها إلا بالحق إذ هو الوجود المطلق ووجودها ليس في الخارج ، فلا يكون إلا في ذات العالم بها . \n\nفلو قيل بجعلها ، فإما أن تكون حادثة في الأزل مساوقة للعالم بها في الوجود ، لكن الحدوث الزمني في الأزل محال ، أولا مساوقة لكنها حادثة في ذاته ، فالعالم بها إما عينه ، فيكون محلا لقبول الأثر من نفسه في نفسه ، أو غيره فيكون ظرفا لغيره ، وتعالى أن يكون ظرفا أو مظروفا . \n\nثم أبطل الكل بدليل تناسب التوحيد بأنه تعالى واحد من كل وجه من حيث أزليته ، وهذا قادح في صرافة وحدته إذ الحقائق المختلفة موجودة معه بوجود مستقل ، فلا يكون إلا بالترتيب معه على أنها لو كانت مجعولة ، لكانت موجودة والوجود الفائض عليها يكون عرضا لها ، وهي موجودة فيتكرر الوجود عليها ، فهو تحصيل الحاصل ، فهو محال من هذا الوجه ، ومن وجوه أخر لا حاجة إلى التطويل بها . \n\nمثل ما يقال : الماهيات حينئذ إنما تتحقق بالوجود حال عدمه ، مثل ما يقال ، لو كانت مجعولة ، لكانت الإنسانية عند عدم جعلها الإنسانية ، فيلزم سلبه عن نفسه ، وهو",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —impossible.\n\nOr it may be said that some concomitants accrue to quiddities as such, as evenness does to four. If four were supposed to be not even, it would not be four. The quiddities must therefore be established apart from individual existences—individual existence being existence itself. Were they made, their making would precede existence, but this priority is impossible. It is thus established that the realities, in respect of their being known to the Real, are not made, even though their being made under another consideration is possible. If they are not made in themselves, there are not two existences in reality. A plurality of existence would follow only if quiddities were existent in themselves and, because they differ intrinsically, existence differed intrinsically with their difference.\n\nExistence as such is one in the Real and in creation. It is common to all realities in respect of its manifestation in them and through them. Its source is the Real; it is effused from Him upon them as the sun's light pours upon what faces it. He indicates that the existence of the world has no need of an intermediary:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “This one existence accruing to created possibilities does not differ in reality from the hidden existence of the Real, detached from entities and loci of manifestation, except through relations and considerations such as manifestation, determination, the multiplicity arising through association and the acceptance of the ruling of commonality, and similar descriptions that accrue to it through its connection with loci of manifestation.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Since the existence accruing to created possibilities—he qualifies them this way because it does not accrue to anything else—is one, some possible things cannot serve as an intermediary for others, either for that existence to be obtained in itself or for its relations and considerations to be obtained.\n\nAs for the first: it does not differ in reality from the hidden existence of the Real, detached from entities and loci of manifestation, even though this is [manifest] and not detached from them. Difference in these matters does not entail difference in reality. It is therefore necessary through itself and has no need of an intermediary at all. Suppose we grant that it is not necessary: it is still one, and its occurrence in one possible thing differs from its occurrence in another only through attribution.\n\nAs for the second: those relations and considerations accrue to it through the loci of manifestation. These are nonexistent, so cannot be intermediaries. If their existence is considered, the First Intellect is not an intermediary for what is below it; rather, each locus is its own intermediary.       "ar": "محال . \n\nومثل ما يقال : أن بعض اللوازم تعرض الماهيات من حيث هي كالزوجية للأربعة ، فلو فرض أربعة غير زوج ، لم يكن أربعة ، فلا بدّ من تقررها مجردة عن الهويات ، والهوية هي الوجود ، ولو كانت مجعولة لكان ما جعلها قبل الوجود ، لكن هذه القبلية محالة ، فثبت أن الحقائق من حيث معلوميتها للحق غير مجعولة ، وإن كان جاز جعلها باعتبار آخر ، وإذا لم تكن مجعولة من حيث هي ، فليس في الواقع وجدان ، إذ تعدد الوجود إنما يلزم لو كانت الماهيات موجودة من حيث هي ، وهي مختلفة بذواتها حتى يختلف الوجود باختلافها اختلافا ذاتيّا . \n\nفالوجود من حيث هو واحد في الحق والخلق ، وهو مشترك بين جميع الحقائق باعتبار ظهوره فيها وبها ، وأصله الحق فاض منه عليها فيضان نور الشمس لمن يقابله . \nأشار إلى عدم احتياج وجود العالم إلى الواسطة ، \n\nبما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ ثم إن هذا الوجود الواحد العارض للممكنات المخلوقة ، ليس بمغاير في الحقيقة للوجود الحق الباطن المجرد عن الأعيان والمظاهر ، إلا بنسب واعتبارات كالظهور والتعين والتعدد الحاصل باقتران وقبول حكم الاشتراك ونحو ذلك من النعوت التي تلحقه بواسطة التعلق بالمظاهر ] . \n\nأي : لما كان الوجود العارض للمكنات المخلوقة قيد بذلك ؛ لأنه لا يعرض لغيرها واحد ، فلا يمكن الممكنات واسطة باعتبار البعض الآخر لحصول ذلك الوجود في نفسه ، ولا لحصول نسبه واعتباراته . \nأما الأول ؛ فلأنه ليس بمغاير في الحقيقة للوجود الحق الباطن المجرد عن الأعيان والمظاهر ، وإن كان هذا باطلا ظاهرا غير مجرد عن الأعيان والمظاهر ، فالاختلاف بهذه الأمور لا يستلزم الاختلاف بالحقيقة ، فهو واجب بالذات لا يفتقر إلى واسطة أصلا . \n\nسلمنا أنه ليس بواجب ، فهو واحد ، فحصوله في ممكن غير حصوله في الآخر إلا باعتبار الإضافة ، وأما الثاني ؛ فلأن تلك النسب والاعتبارات إنما حصلت له بواسطة المظاهر ، وهي معدومة ، فلا يكون واسطة ، فإن اعتبر وجودها فلا يكون العقل الأول واسطة بما دونه ، بل كل مظهر واسطة نفسه ، وذلك أن الاعتبارات الأصلية ثابتة الظهور",

      "printed_page": 210,
      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —in the loci of manifestation, determination through them, and multiplicity according to their number. The first two arise through its association with them; the third through its acceptance of the ruling of commonality, which follows from association. Likewise the other attributes accrue to it through connection with the loci of manifestation. Each locus is its own intermediary in these considerations and attributes, not in existence itself. There is therefore no intermediary between the Real and creation. What is thought to be an intermediary is so only because those considerations arise at its occurrence, not through it. If the world does not need an intermediary in respect of quiddity, existence, relation, or its attributes, it does not need one in respect of their aggregate, since nothing has arisen there that would require it.\n\nHe then states that an intermediary is needed between the Real and His association with the possible realities, because He is in Himself independent of the worlds. This intermediary cannot therefore belong to the world, whether its reality or existence, but must be from the Real, His names, and His attributes. He indicates this as follows:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “The wellspring of the loci of existence's manifestation, in respect of its association [with them], the presence of its self-disclosure, and the abode of its determination and descent, is the Cloud mentioned by the Prophet—God bless him and grant him peace. It is the station of lordly descent, the point from which the essential, all-merciful generosity issues from the unseen identity and the veil of the might of selfhood. In this Cloud is determined the rank of the first, unseen, eternal marriage, which opens the presences of the divine names through the essential, eternal orientations. We shall shortly unseal the key of its keys, if God—exalted is He—wills.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** That is, the source of the loci of manifestation, through which the realities of possible things become mirrors of the existence of the Real—not in respect of His Essence, independent of the worlds, but in respect of His association with those realities. This association is not like bodies' association with one another, an inhering thing's association with a substrate, or a substrate's association with an inhering thing. It is in respect of His self-disclosure in realities, so that He appears in the fixed entities, after His manifestation in His Essence to His Essence. Hence the abode of His determination is lower than the first determination, extending to the other determinations. This descent is not from a high place to a low one; it means drawing down toward the loci of manifestation.       "ar": "في المظاهر والتعين بها والتعدد بعددها ، والأولان يحصلان باقترانه بها ، والثالث لقبول حكم الاشتراك الذي هو فرع الاقتران ، وكذا سائر الصفات إنما تلحقه بواسطة التعلق بالمظاهر ، وكل مظهر واسطة نفسه في تلك الاعتبارات والصفات لا في نفس الوجود ، فلا واسطة بين الحق والخلق ، \nوما يظن أنه واسطة ، فلحصول تلك الاعتبارات عندها لا بها ، وإذا لم يفتقر العالم إلى الواسطة باعتبار الماهية والوجود والنسبة وصفاته ، لم يفتقر باعتبار المجموع ، إذ لم يحدث بما يوجب الافتقار إليها . \n\nثم ذكر أن الواسطة يحتاج إليها فيما بين الحق وبين اقترانه بالحقائق الممكنة ، لكونه بالذات غنيّا عن العالمين ، فلا تكون تلك الواسطة من العالم ، حقيقته أو وجوده ، بل من الحق وأسمائه وصفاته . \n\nوإليه أشار بما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وينبوع مظاهر الوجود باعتبار اقترانه حضرة تجليه ومنزل تعينه وتدلّيه العماء الذي ذكره النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ، وهو مقام التنزيل الرباني منبعث الجود الذاتي الرحماني من غيب الهوية وحجاب عز الإنيّة ، وفي هذا العمى يتعين مرتبة النكاح الأول الغيبي الأزلي الفاتح حضرات الأسماء الإلهية بالتوجهات الذاتية الأزلية ، وسنفك ختم مفتاح مفاتيحه عن قريب إن شاء اللّه تعالى ] . \n\nأي : وأصل مظاهر الوجود الذي به ، صارت حقائق الممكنات مرائي الوجود الحق - لا باعتبار ذاته الغنية عن العالمين - بل باعتبار اقترانه بهذه الحقائق . \nوليس ذلك الاقتران اقتران الأجسام بعضها ببعض ، ولا اقتران الحال بالمحال أو اقتران المحل بالحال ، بل باعتبار تجليه في حقائق بحيث يظهر في الأعيان الثابتة قربها بعد ظهوره في ذاته لذاته . فلذلك كان منزل تعينه أنزل عن التعين الأول إلى سائر التعينات ، وليس هذا التنزيل من مكان عال إلى سافل بل بمعنى التدلي إلى المظاهر ، والمتدلّي هو العماء الذي ذكره النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم :  “ إذا سئل أين كان ربنا قبل أن يخلق الخلق ؟ قال : كان في عماء ما فوقه هواء ، وما تحته هواء  “ ، فالعماء هو حضرة الواحدية بمنزلة الحجاب الرقيق بين الخلق",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —and the first determination.\n\nIt is the wellspring of the loci of manifestation and the intermediary in association because it is the station of lordly descent from the first determination to the second. These relations follow from the Essence's connection with the loci in the presence of the Cloud.       "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —existence, by manifesting actually in the locus of manifestation the possible attributes that are potentially within it.\n\nHe says, “We shall unseal the key of the keys”: this is the loving orientation. Perhaps that key is existence's inclusion of the many considerations and the exalted affairs potentially within it. Hence he says:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “If you understand, existence has two considerations. One is insofar as it is existence alone, which is the Real. From this aspect, as already indicated, there is in it no multiplicity, composition, attribute, characterization, name, trace, relation, or ruling. Rather, it is unalloyed existence. Our saying ‘existence’ conveys understanding; this is not a real name for Him. Rather, His name is His attribute itself, and His attribute His Essence itself.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** If the wellspring of the loci of manifestation is the presence of the Cloud—and this is among the ranks of the Real, since it precedes creation and there is something above it, the Cloud intervening between that and creation—then existence in the rank of the Real has two considerations, if you understand this meaning. One is insofar as it is existence alone, in the rank of oneness.\n\nIn this rank it is the Real without two considerations alongside it, since it is necessary existence through itself, as explained in the introduction. From this aspect, as already indicated, oneness has no actual multiplicity or composition of existence and quiddity or anything else. There is no non-established attribute or established characterization, no name differing from Him or trace making Him manifest. In this consideration He has no relation to a thing, nor a thing to Him, because of His independence of the worlds; nor any ruling that He is a principle or not a principle. Although He is not devoid of these, they are not distinguished under this consideration. In this consideration He is unalloyed—that is, pure—existence.\n\nHe then anticipates a question: ‘Existence is predicated of Him, and a predicate must differ from its subject in some respect; how, then, can He have no name differing from Him?’ He answers: our saying ‘existence’ conveys understanding. Because it is the most general of things, He is indicated by it; but there is no real name distinguished from Him there. In that rank His name is His attribute itself, and His attribute His Essence itself, since there is no distinction or duality there in any respect. That is, if a name were supposed for Him, it would not be distinct from the attribute, nor the attribute from the Essence: all, within existence itself, is existence itself.\n\nHe then anticipates another question: how can there be no characterization or attribute distinguished from Him, when He is qualified by perfection, knowledge, life, and power, whose concepts differ? How are they not distinguished there? He answers—",
      "ar": "الوجود باعتبار إظهار ما فيه من الصفات الممكنات بالقوة في المظهر بالفعل . \n\nقال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وسنفك ختم مفتاح مفاتيح الذي هو التوجه الحبي ، ولعل ذلك المفتاح هو اشتمال الوجود على الاعتبارات الكثيرة والشؤون الراقية بالقوة  “ ، فلذلك قال رضي اللّه عنه :  “ فللوجود إن فهمت اعتباران : أحدهما من كونه وجودا فحسب وهو الحق ، وأنه من هذا الوجه كما سبقت الإشارة إليه ، لا كثرة فيه ، ولا تركيب ، ولا صفة ، ولا نعت ، ولا اسم ، ولا رسم ، ولا نسبة ، ولا حكم ، بل هو وجود بحت ] . \n\nوقولنا : وجود هو للتفهيم ، لا أن ذلك اسم حقيقي له ، بل اسمه عين صفته ، وصفته عين ذاته ، أي وإذا كان ينبوع مظاهر الوجود وحضرة العماء - وهو من المراتب الحقيقية إذ هو قبل الخلق وفوقه شيء - إذ العماء حائل بين ذلك الشيء ، وبين الخلق فللوجود في الرتبة الحقيقية إن فهمت هذا المعنى اعتباران : أحدهما من كونه وجودا فحسب ، وذلك في المرتبة الأحدية . \n\nوفي هذه المرتبة هو الحق من غير اعتبارين معه ، إذ هو واجب الوجود بذاته لما مر في المقدمة ، وأنه من هذا الوجه كما سبقت الإشارة إليه من أن الأحدية لا كثرة فيها بالفعل ، ولا تركيب من وجود وماهية أو غيرهما ، ولا صفة غير راسخة ولا نعت راسخة ، ولا اسم يغايره ولا رسم يظهره ، إذ لا نسبة له بذلك الاعتبار إلى شيء ، ولا لشيء إليه لغنائه عن العالمين ، وحكم من كونه مبدأ أو غير مبدأ ، وإن لم يخل عنها ، لكنها لا تتميز بهذا الاعتبار ، بل هو بهذا الاعتبار وجود بحث أي : صرف . \n\nثم استشعر سؤالا بأنه : لا يقال عليته الوجود والمحمول لا بدّ وأن يغاير الموضوع من وجه ، فكيف لا يكون له اسم يغايره ؟ \nفقال : وقولنا وجود للتفهيم ؛ لأنه لما كان أعم الأشياء أشير به إليه إلا أنه لا اسم حقيقي متميز عنه هناك ، بل اسمه في ذلك المرتبة عين صفته وصفته عين ذاته ، إذ لا تميز ولا اثنينية هناك بوجه من الوجوه . \nأي : لو قدر له اسم ، لم يتميز عن الصفة ، وكذا الصفة عن الذات ، بل الكل في نفس الوجود عين الوجود . \n\nثم استشعر سؤالا آخر ، بأنه كيف لا نعت ، ولا صفة يتميز عنه مع أنه موصوف بالكمال ، وبالعلم والحياة والقدرة ومفهوماتها متغايرة ، فكيف لا يتميز هناك ، فأجاب عنه",

      "en": "**Qūnawī:** “His perfection is His very essential existence, established for Him from Himself, not from another. His life and power are His knowledge itself. His knowledge of things from eternity is His knowledge of Himself itself: He knows Himself through Himself, and knows every thing through His very knowledge of Himself.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The perfection established for Him in oneness and the first determination is His very existence, which His Essence requires. Perfection too is therefore established for Him from Himself. Deficiency is nonexistence, so perfection is existence. Existence is established for Him from Himself, not from another, because it is His very self. Were it other than Him, existence would be obtained from what is other than existence and would not be necessary through itself. Likewise His life and power are His knowledge of Himself. Everything that is aware of itself is called living, and what is not aware [the printed sentence stops here]. Power means doing what one wills; His act is known, so what He knows to exist He does, and what He does not, He does not. The reduction of will, hearing, sight, and speech to knowledge is evident. These attributes return to knowledge, and His knowledge of Himself is His very self, as already explained.\n\nIt remains to discuss His knowledge of things. He says, “His knowledge of things is also His very knowledge of Himself.” This is because He—mighty and majestic—knows Himself through Himself, not through a likeness additional to Himself, so that one might say He knows Himself through an additional knowledge. His eternal knowledge of things is His very knowledge of Himself because things consist of existence and realities. Existence is His very self, and realities are the forms of His knowledge. The forms of knowledge do not differ from knowledge in the eternal rank. Hence he specifies ‘from eternity’: all, within existence itself, is existence itself. Thus no characterization or attribute is distinguished there.\n\nHe then anticipates a question: how can He be identical with these differing, multiple things despite His utmost unity and simplicity? He indicates the answer:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “Differing things are united in Him, and multiple things issue from Him, without their containing Him or His containing them, or their bringing Him forth from a prior hiddenness, or His bringing them forth from Himself and making them appear. He has a unity that is the source of every multiplicity, and a simplicity that is identical with every composition. [He is] last and first [the printed transition is unstable]. Everything contradictory in the case of another is established for Him in the most perfect ways.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Things that differ in respect of quiddities are united in respect of existence, because it is common to them. Multiple things issue from Him, so their multiplicity has its source in His unity. Multiplicity was unity in the first rank, then became multiplicity attributed to its quiddities. But His many relations to those quiddities are not by His being a substrate—",
      "ar": "بما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وكما له نفس وجوده الذاتي الثابت له من نفسه لا من سواه ، وحياته وقدرته عين علمه ، وعلمه بالأشياء أزلا عين علمه بنفسه : بمعنى أنه علم نفسه بنفسه ، وعلم كل شيء بنفس علمه بنفسه ] . \n\nأي : والكمال الثابت له في الأحدية والتعين الأول ، وهو نفس وجوده الذي هو مقتضى ذاته ، فالكمال أيضا ثابت له من نفسه ؛ وذلك لأن النقص لما كان هو العدم ، كان الكمال هو الوجود والوجود ثابت له من نفسه لا من سواه ؛ لأنه عين نفسه ، إذ لو كان غيره ، لكان الوجود حاصلا مما هو سوى الوجود ، فلم يكن واجبا لذاته ، وكذا حياته وقدرته عين علمه بنفسه ؛ وذلك لأن كل ما يشعر بذاته ، يسمى حيّا ، وما لا يشعر . \nومعنى القدرة أن يفعل ما يشاء وفعله معلوم ، فما علم وجوده فعل ، وما لا ، فلا . \nوأما رجوع الإرادة والسمع والبصر والكلام إلى العلم فظاهر ، فهذه الصفات راجعة إلى العلم وعلمه بنفسه عين نفسه على ما مرّ بقي الكلام في علمه بالأشياء . \n\nفقال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وعلمه بالأشياء عين علمه بنفسه أيضا ] ؛ وذلك لأنه عزّ وجلّ علم نفسه بنفسه لا بمثال زائد على نفسه حتى يقال : علم نفسه بعلم زائد ، وعلمه بالأشياء أزلا عين علمه بنفسه ؛ لأن الأشياء عبارة عن الوجود والحقائق والوجود عين نفسه ، والحقائق صور علمه ، وصور العلم لا تغاير العلم في المرتبة الأزلية . \nولذلك قيد بقوله : أزلا ؛ وذلك لأن الكل في الوجود نفسه نفس الوجود ، وإذا كان كذلك ، فلا نعت ولا صفة تتميز هناك . \n\nثم استشعر سؤالا بأنه كيف يكون عين هذه الأشياء المختلفة المتكثرة مع غاية وحدته وبساطته ، \nفأشار إلى دفعه بما قال رضي اللّه عنه [ تتحد فيه المختلفات ، وتنبعث منه المتكثرات ، هي دون أن تحويه أو يحويها أو تبديه عن بطون متقدم أو هو من نفسه يبرزها ، فيبديها له وحدة هي محتد كل كثرة وبساطة هي عين كل تركيب آخر ، وأول مرة كل ما يتناقض في حق غيره ، فهو له على أكمل الوجوه ثابت ] . \n\nيعني : أن المختلفات من حيث الماهيات تتحد من حيث الوجود ؛ لاشتراكه فيها وتنبعث منه المتكثرات ، فأصل كثرتها وحدته ، فالكثرة في المرتبة الأولى كانت وحدة ، ثم صارت كثرة تنسب إلى ماهياتها ، لكن كثرة نسبته إلى تلك الماهيات ليس بطريق المحلية",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —for them, or by His inhering in them, so that He would be a substrate for originated things, their attribute, or situated within them. He is exalted beyond that. Rather, they manifest Him and are manifest through Him.\n\nThis does not mean that they bring Him forth from a hiddenness preceding this manifestation, for He has always been manifest to Himself. Rather, His manifestation in them follows His hiddenness relative to them. Likewise, their manifestation from Him does not mean that He brings them out from Himself and makes them appear. The entities remain as they are forever, never smelling the fragrance of existence, although existence appears through them and their forms. If they were qualified by existence, existence would be among their accidents and follow them, although it precedes them. This is why the question is obscure.\n\nHe then anticipates another question: these relations must be many, so how can He, together with them, be one in every respect and truly simple? He answers: He has a unity that is the source of every multiplicity, whether of relations or other things. All relations exist potentially within it, like the tree in the seed. In itself it is actually one in every respect; insofar as it is the source of multiplicity, there is potential multiplicity within it. Likewise, His simplicity is identical with every composition insofar as it is the source of compositions. In itself it is actual simplicity in every respect; insofar as it is the source of compositions, it is identical with all of them.\n\nHe then adduces the fact that God is called ‘First and Last’ together, because His attributes are eternal without beginning or end. His firstness is in respect of His unity and simplicity; His lastness in respect of His multiplicity and composition. They are therefore united in Him.\n\nHe anticipates another question: multiplicity and composition involve deficiency incompatible with eternity and intrinsic necessity. He answers that everything contradictory in the case of another is established for Him in the most perfect ways. Both are established in Him only in respect of the unity, simplicity, and necessity within them, not the aspects of deficiency, which are privative. We have already explained that every restricted thing has an aspect toward absoluteness, every absolute an aspect toward restriction, and everything in a locus is there only according to that locus. He then refutes the ordinary people who disagree with this.",
      "ar": "لها ، ولا الحالة فيها حتى يكون محلا للحوادث أو صفة لها أو متمكنا فيها ، تعالى عن ذلك ، بل مظهرة له وظاهرة به . \nوليس ذلك بمعنى أنها تبديه عن بطون متقدم على هذا الظهور ؛ لأنه لم يزل ظاهرا لنفسه ، بل ظهوره فيها بعد بطونه بالنسبة إليها ، وكذا ظهورها عنه ليس بمعنى أنه يخرجها من نفسه فيبديها إذ الأعيان لا تزال على ما هي عليه إلى الأبد لا تشم رائحة الوجود ، وإن ظهر الوجود بها وبصورها ، إذ لو اتصفت بالوجود ، لكان الوجود من عوارضها فيتأخر عنها ، وهو مقدم عليها ، فلهذا جعلت المسألة غامضة . \n\nثم استشعر سؤالا آخر بأن هذه النسب لا بدّ من تكثرها ، فكيف يكون معها واحدا من كل الوجوه ، وكيف يكون مع تحققها بسيطا حقيقيّا . \nفقال : له وحدة هي أصل كل كثرة من النسب وغيرها ، فجميع النسب فيها موجودة بالقوة ، كالشجرة في النّواة . \nفهي بالفعل بالنظر إلى ذاتها واحدة من كل وجه ، ومن جهة أنها محتد الكثرة فيها كثرة بالقوة ، وهكذا بساطته عين كل تركيب من حيث إنها محتد التركيبات ، فهي من حيث هي بساطة بالفعل من كل وجه ، ومن جهة أنها محتد التراكيب عين التراكيب كلها . \n\nثم استدل على ذلك بأنه يقال فيه تعالى :  “ أول وآخر  “ معا ؛ لأن صفاته قديمة أبدية وأوليته باعتبار وحدته وبساطته وآخريته باعتبار كثرته وتركيبه ، فهما يجتمعان فيه . \nثم استشعر سؤالا آخر ، بأن في الكثرة والتركيب نقصا ينافي القدم والوجوب الذاتي . فأجاب بأن : كل ما يتناقض في حق غيره ، وهو ثابت له على الوجوه فهما إنما يثبتان فيه من حيث ما فيها من الوحدة والبساطة والوجوب ، لا من جهات النقص ، إذ هي عدمية ، وقد مر أن كل مقيد له وجه إلى الإطلاق ، ولكل مطلق وجه إلى التقييد ، وإن كل كائن في محل لا يكون إلا بحسب المحل ، ثم رد على العوام المخالفين بهذا .  “ 1  “",

      "printed_page": 215,
      "en": "**Qūnawī:** “Everyone who speaks about Him but not through Him, denies of Him every ambiguous matter, and confines Him within his own apprehension is mute and silent, ignorant and confounded, until he sees through Him every opposite within its very opposite—indeed, as identical with it—while distinguishing its reality from Him.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** That is, everyone among the scholars who imagines he speaks about Him, but does not speak through Him, because he claims complete distinction in order to affirm his own self; who denies of Him every matter whose reality is ambiguous to his intellect, not knowing that his existence is the Real Himself, while the other is only his reality, which has no existence; and who confines the Real within what he apprehends as the Necessary Existent, the Eternal, free of deficiencies—such a person is mute and silent concerning the realities of things, ignorant and confounded concerning them. He does not know the Real as He is until he sees every opposite within its very opposite: the eternal in the originated, the originated in the eternal, the intrinsically necessary in the possible, and the possible in the intrinsically necessary. Indeed, he sees each as identical with the other in respect of existence, while distinguishing the reality of each opposite from the one, necessary Real, without believing in indwelling or union.\n\nHe then explains this in detail:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “His unity is His multiplicity itself; His simplicity His composition itself; His manifestation His hiddenness itself; His lastness His firstness itself. He is not confined within the concept of unity or existence, and is not delimited—”",
      "ar": "وقال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وكل من نطق عنه لا به ونفى عنه كل أمر مشتبه وحصره في مدركه ، فهو أبكم ساكت ، وجاهل مباهت ، حتى يرى به كل ضدّ في نفس ضده ، بل عينه مع تميزه بين حقيقته وبينه ] \nأي : كل ما نطق عنه من العلماء بزعمه لا به ، لدعوى التمييز الكلي لثبات نفسه ، ونفى عنه كل أمر مشتبه على عقله حقيقة ، فلم يعلم أن وجوده عين الحق والغير ، إنما هو حقيقة التي لا وجود لها . \nوحصر الحق في مدركه من الواجب الوجود القديم البريء عن النقائص ، فهو أبكم ساكت عن حقائق الأمور ، وجاهل بالحقائق مباهت فيها ، لا يعرف الحق على ما هو عليه حتى يرى كل ضد في نفس ضده ، فيرى القديم في الحادث والحادث في القديم ، والواجب بالذات في الممكن ، والممكن في الواجب بالذات ، بل يرى الكل عين الآخر من جهة الوجود مع تمييزه بين حقيقته ، كل ضد ، وبين الحق الواحد الواجب من غير اعتقاد حلول أو اتحاد . \n\nثم فصّل ذلك فقال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وحدته عين كثرته ، وبساطته عين تركيبه ، وظهوره نفس بطونه ، وآخريته عين أوليته ، لا ينحصر في المفهوم من الوحدة أو الوجود ، ولا ينضبط",

      "en": "**Qūnawī (continuing):** “—by a witness or within something witnessed. It is His to be as He has said, and to appear as He wills, without confinement to absoluteness or restriction. His is the meaning encompassing every letter, and the perfection embracing every attribute. Everything whose beauty is hidden from the veiled, in which blemish and deficiency are imagined—whenever its inner reality is uncovered so that its attribution to Him is understood to be sound, the form of perfection is found within it, and it is seen as a platform for the self-disclosure of majesty or beauty. All the names and attributes are multiple with Him within His very unity; they are His very self. He does not transcend what is established for Him, and is not veiled from what He has displayed in order to perfect it.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** His true unity is identical with its opposite, multiplicity, because multiplicity is not in existence itself but in its forms, which are identical with it insofar as they have no existence without it. They are therefore one in respect of existence, which requires unity and is coextensive with it. Unity is thus identical with multiplicity in respect of existence. Likewise His true simplicity is identical with its opposite, composition: this is not in existence itself but among its forms, which are identical with it, and so forth.\n\nLikewise His manifestation is His hiddenness itself, because the manifest is the form of the hidden. Lastness, a concomitant of manifestation, is firstness itself, a concomitant of hiddenness. The identity of what is entailed in its referent entails the identity of the concomitant in that respect. He then explains why two opposites can be united in Him: their union is impossible in something confined within a single concept. The Real is not confined within any concept—not unity, such that He would oppose the many, nor existence, such that He would oppose nonexistence. Hence He is realized in multiplicity and in possible realities, which are nonexistent. Absolute nonexistence is not intended, for it is not established. Understand.\n\nHe therefore has no opposite, just as He has no equal. He then says that although the witness of reason indicates confinement to unity and existence, making Him necessary existence, He is not delimited by it according to the proofs of unveiling. Those indicate His manifestation in multiplicity and in possible realities. Yet He is not delimited within that which is witnessed either.\n\nHe says that it is His to be as He has said: ‘They encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills’ [Q 2:255]. This concerns oneness. ‘And to appear as He wills’ concerns oneness-with-multiplicity, according to the preparednesses in the fixed entities for receiving manifestation in particular forms, at particular times and places. Yet He is not confined to either oneness or oneness-with-multiplicity. How could He be confined, when His is the meaning encompassing—",
      "ar": "لشاهد ولا في مشهود له ، أن يكون كما قال ، وظهر كما يريد دون الحصر في الإطلاق ، والتقييد له المعنى المحيط بكل حرف ، والكمال المستوعب بكل وصف ، كل ما خفي عن المحجوبين حسنه ، مما يتوهم فيه شين ونقص ، فإنه متى كشف عن ساقه بحيث يدرك صحة انضيافه إليه ألقى فيه صورة الكمال ، ورأى أنه منصة لتجلي الجلال أو الجمال ، سائر الأسماء والصفات عنده متكثرة في عين وحدته هي عينه لا يتنزه عما هو ثابت له ، ولا يحتجب عما أبداه ليكمله ] . \nأي : وحدته الحقيقية عين ضدها الذي هو الكثرة ؛ لأن الكثرة ليست في نفس الوجود ، بل في صورة عينه من حيث لا وجود لها بدونه ، فهي من حيث الوجود الذي يقتضي الوحدة ويساوقها واحدة . \nفالوحدة عين الكثرة باعتبار الوجود ، كذا بساطته الحقيقية عين ضدها الذي هو التركيب ؛ لأنه ليس في نفس الوجود ، بل بين صورة ، وهي عينه . . إلخ . \n\nوكذا ظهوره نفس بطونه ؛ لأن الظاهر صورة الباطن ، وكذا الآخرية التي هي من لوازم الظهور عين الأولية التي هي من لوازم البطون ، واتحاد اللزوم بحسب الصدق ، يستلزم اتحاد اللازم بحسبه ، ثم اعتذر عن سبب اجتماع الضدين فيه ، بأنه يمتنع اجتماعهما فيما ينحصر في مفهوم واحد ، والحق لا ينحصر في مفهوم أصلا ، لا في الوحدة ، حتى يقابل الكثير ، ولا في الوجود حتى يقابل العدم ، فلذلك يتحقق في الكثرة ، وفي الحقائق الممكنة التي هي أعدام ، وليس المراد العدم المطلق ، فإنه ليس بثابت ، فافهم . \n\nفلذلك لا ضد له كما أنه لا ند له ، ثم ذكر : أن شاهد العقل ، وإن دل على انحصاره في الوحدة والوجود - إذ جعله واجب الوجود - فلا ينضبط فيه بحسب الأدلة الكشفية ، فإنها دلت على ظهوره في الكثرة ، وفي الحقائق الممكنة ، لكنه لا ينضبط في ذلك المشهود أيضا . \n\nثم قال : له أن يكون كما قال من أنهم :وَلا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِما شاءَ[ البقرة : 255 ] هذا في الأحدية وظهر كما يريد هذا في الواحدية بحسب الاستعدادات التي في الأعيان الثابتة من قبولها الظهور بصور معينة في أزمنة معينة وأمكنة مخصوصة ، ومع ذلك لا ينحصر في الأحدية والواحدية ، وكيف ينحصر وله المعنى المحيط",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —every letter among necessary and possible existents, and the perfection embracing every attribute of absoluteness and restriction?\n\nHe then answers the difficulty posed by deficiency and blemish in restricted things: how could He be qualified by these when they oppose perfections? He says, “Everything whose beauty is hidden”: the imagination of blemish and deficiency comes only from the hiddenness of beauty, which belongs to the self-disclosure of beauty and majesty.\n\nWe say this because whenever the inner reality of the matter—expressed by ‘the shin’—is uncovered, so that existence, intrinsically perfect and combining the attributes of majesty and beauty, may rightly be attributed to it, the form of existential perfection is found within it. It appears to the extent of its preparedness and is hidden where its preparedness cannot manifest it. Despite its limited preparedness to manifest existence as it is, it is a platform—that is, a complete, clear locus—for the self-disclosure of majesty and beauty. These are among the concomitants of existence; its existence makes what is within it a platform for the disclosure of both together.\n\nHaving said that multiplicity in existence is unity itself, he explains where multiplicity is established and how it coexists with unity: it is in the names and attributes. These are many in their concepts and necessary rulings, yet all are within the very unity in respect of their referent. That unity itself is the Essence in respect of its referent, so all are the Essence itself. Unity and multiplicity are therefore together within it.\n\nHe then answers the supposition that multiplicity in Him entails many gods, although God transcends a partner by the agreement of those rational people and people of unveiling whose views carry weight. His answer is that, according to some of them, He does not transcend multiplicity in attributes, since those are established for Him in their view. He transcends multiplicity in subjects possessing those attributes, which are not established. This is precisely the position of the Sunnis, including the Ashʿarīs and others.\n\nHe then answers the question of how multiple attributes are affirmed in unveiling, when they would otherwise be veils from the Essence. He answers: He first discloses the attributes to them; when they are perfected, He discloses the Essence, thereby completing for them the disclosure of the attributes as well. The perfected person is not veiled by one thing from another: creation does not veil him from the Real, so how could the Real's attributes veil him from Him?\n\nHaving mentioned veiling and sanctity, he digresses. Since it was said that everything by which He is described is identical with its opposite, veiling in His case would be disclosure itself, might abasement itself, independence need itself, and sanctity deficiency itself. Yet these—",
      "ar": "بكل حرف من الموجودات الواجبة والممكنة ، والكمال المستوعب كل وصف من الإطلاق والتقييد . \n\nثم اعتذر عما يلزم من النقص والشين في المقيدات ، فكيف يتصف بذلك ، وهي منافية للكمالات ، فقال : كل ما خفي يعنى : إن توهم الشين والنقص ، إنما هو من خفاء الحسن الذي هو من تجلي الجمال والجلال . \n\nوإنما قلنا بذلك ؛ لأنه متى كشف عن باطن الأمر الذي عبر عنه بالساق ، حتى يصح كونه يضاف إليه الوجود الذي هو كامل بالذات ، جامع بصفتي الجلال والجمال ، ألفي أي : وجد فيه صورة الكمال الوجودي ، ظهر بقدر استعداده ، وخفي بما ليس في استعداده ، إظهاره ومع قصور استعداده لإظهار الوجود على ما هو عليه منصة ، أي مظهر كامل واضح لتجلي الجلال والجمال ؛ فلأنه من لوازم الوجود ، ووجوده أظهر ما فيه منصة تجليها معا . \n\nولما ذكر أن الكثرة في الوجود عين الوحدة ، ذكر أن الكثرة ثبتت في الوجود ، وكيف يجامع وحدته ، فقال : ذلك في الأسماء والصفات ، فإنها متكثرة بالمفهومات والأحكام اللازمة ، وكلها في عين الوحدة من حيث الصدق ، حتى أن تلك الوحدة عين الذات من جهة الصدق ، فالكل عين الذات ، ففيها الوحدة والكثرة معا ، ثم اعتذر عما يتوهم أنه يستلزم وجود الكثرة فيه بعدد الإله ، وهو تعالى منزّه عن الشريك باتفاق من يعتد به من العقلاء وأهل المكاشفة ، فأجاب بأنه عند بعضهم غير منزّه عن كثرة في الصفات ؛ لأنها أيضا ثابتة له عندهم ، وإنما يتنزه عن الكثرة في الموصوفين بتلك الصفات ، وليسوا بثابتين ، فهذا عين مذهب أهل السنة من الأشاعرة وغيرهم ، ثم اعتذر عما يقال يثبت تعدد الصفات في الكشف ، وإلا كانت حجبا عن الذّات . \n\nفأجاب : أنه يبدأ لهم بتجلي الصفات أيضا ، حتى إذا كملوا ، تجلى لهم بالذات ، فيكمل لهم تجلي الصفات أيضا ؛ لأن الكامل لا يحجبه شيء عن شيء ، حتى أنه لا يحجبه الخلق عن الحق ، فكيف يحجبه صفات الحق عنه ، ولما وقع الكلام في الحجاب والتقديس استطرد على أنه لما قيل أن جميع ما وصف به عين أضدادها ، فالحجاب في حقه عين الكشف ، والعزة عين الذل والغني عين الافتقار ، والتقديس عين النقص ، مع ثبوت هذه",

      "printed_page": 218,
      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —matters are affirmed by consensus, and their opposites denied by it. An explanation is therefore needed. It is what he says:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “His veil, might, independence, and sanctity signify His reality's distinction from everything that opposes it, His lack of connection with anything, and His lack of need for anything in the establishment and continuance of His existence. Nothing is realized through itself or through anything except Him. Take heed.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** His veil signifies His reality's distinction from everything opposing it. There is no opposition except in respect of existence [the printed formulation is difficult], so there is no veil in that respect. His reality's distinction is a veil because it produces the separation that brings ignorance of Him. If you say, ‘There is no reality and existence there; His reality is existence itself,’ we answer: what is intended is the reality of existence through which existence is existence. Although existence is most evident in its actuality, it is most hidden in respect of its reality, since it cannot be defined by an essential or descriptive definition.\n\nHis might signifies His lack of connection with anything, because connection with what is lower [the printed expression is defective]. In respect of the absoluteness of the Essence He is mighty. But because He has an aspect toward restriction, He becomes connected with created things, so that they appear and exist.\n\nHis independence signifies His lack of need for anything in the establishment and continuance of His existence. This is in respect of the Essence. In respect of the names, however, their appearance in loci of manifestation requires the fixed entities through which and in which they appear.\n\nHis sanctity signifies all of this, likewise in respect of the Essence, not the names. The proof is that nothing is realized through itself or through anything else except Him. He is therefore neither veiled from it, nor unconnected with it, nor independent of it in His manifestation in loci of manifestation, nor sanctified beyond that.\n\nHe says, “Take heed”: attend to this subtle point when applying the expressions veil, might, independence, and sanctity. He then begins the rulings of existence insofar as it is existence alone:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “In this respect, intellects and thoughts do not apprehend Him—glory be to Him. Directions and regions do not contain Him. Inner sights and eyes do not encompass witnessing or knowing Him. He transcends formal and intelligible restrictions, is sanctified beyond receiving any determination concerning quantity or quality, and is exalted beyond being encompassed by intuition, understanding, supposition, or knowledge. Through the perfection of His might He is veiled from all His creatures, the perfected among them—”",
      "ar": "الأمور بالإجماع ، وانتفاء أضدادها به احتاج إلى بيان ذلك ، \n\nفهو ما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وحجابه وعزته وغناه وقدسه ، عبارة عن امتياز حقيقته عن كل شيء يضادّها ، وعن عدم تعلقه بشيء ، أو عدم احتياجه في صبوته وجوده له وبقائه إلى ذلك ، لا تحقق لشيء بنفسه ولا بشيء إلا به ، فانتبه ] . \nأي : حجابه عبارة عن امتياز حقيقته عن كل شيء يضادّها ، ولا ضدية إلا بحسب الوجود ، فلا حجاب من تلك الجهة ، وإنما كان امتياز حقيقته حجابا ؛ لأنه تحصل به المباينة الموجبة للجهل به . \nفإن قلت : ليس ثمّة حقيقة ووجد ، بل حقيقته عين الوجود . \nقلنا : المراد حقيقة الوجود التي بها الوجود وجود ، فالوجود وإن كان أظهر بالإنيّة ، أخفى باعتبار الحقيقة ؛ لأنه لا يمكن تعريفه بحد ولا رسم . \n\nوعزته عبارة عن عدم تعلقه بشيء ؛ وذلك لأن التعلق بالدون ذاته ، وهو من حيث إطلاق الذات عزيزة إلا أنه لما كان له وجه على التقييد ، صار متعلقا بالأكوان ، حتى ظهرت ووجدت . \n\nوغناؤه عبارة عن عدم احتياجه في ثبوت وجوده وبقائه إلى شيء ، وهذا من حيث الذات ، وأما من حيث الأسماء ، فلا بدّ لظهورها في المظاهر من الأعيان الثابتة التي يظهر بها وفيها . \n\nوقدسه عبارة عن جميع ذلك ، وذلك أيضا بحسب الذات لا بحسب الأسماء ، بدليل أنه لا يتحقق الشيء بنفسه ولا بشيء آخر إلا به ، فليس محتجب عنه ولا غير متعلق به ، ولا غير محتاج في ظهوره في المظاهر إليه ، ولا مقدس عن ذلك . \n\nثم قال :  “ فانتبه  “ أي : عند إطلاق الحجاب العزة والغنى والقدس لهذه الدقيقة ، ثم شرع في أحكام الوجود من حيث كونه وجودا فحسب ،\n \nفهو ما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ لا تدركه سبحانه من حيث الحيثية العقول والأفكار ، ولا تحويه الجهات والأقطار ، ولا تحيط بمشاهدته ومعرفته البصائر والأبصار ، ومنزه عن القيود الصورية والمعنوية ، مقدس عن قبول كل تقدير متعلق بكمية أو كيفية متعال عن الإحاطات الحدسية والفهمية والظنية والعلمية ، متحجب بكمال عزته عن جميع بريته الكامل منه",

      "en": "**Qūnawī (continuing):** “—and the deficient.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Insofar as He is existence alone, neither immediate intellects nor discursive thoughts apprehend Him. Directions and regions do not contain Him, so outward senses do not apprehend Him. Inward insights and all eyes do not encompass unseen witnessing and certain knowledge of Him. He explains this by His transcendence of formal and intelligible restrictions: how could senses, intellects, and thoughts—which are restricted—apprehend Him? He explains His transcendence of formal restrictions by His sanctity beyond every determination of quantity or quality, and His transcendence of intelligible restrictions by His exaltation beyond being encompassed by intuition, understanding, supposition, or knowledge.\n\nHe explains the inability of inner sights and eyes to encompass Him by His being veiled through the perfection of His might from all His creatures: the perfected possessor of insight and the deficient person limited to outward sight. He describes the perfected as the one turning toward Him, and the deficient as the one turning back from Him. He qualifies the one turning toward Him by ‘in his supposition,’ indicating that, since He is veiled from him and he has not apprehended Him, how could he truly turn toward Him? It is an imagined turning, even if it gives him a station or state. He then anticipates the question: if intellects and insights do not apprehend Him, they have nevertheless apprehended His transcendence. He answers:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “All the intellects' declarations of transcendence, whether through their thoughts or their insights, are negative judgments that convey no real knowledge. Even so, they fall short of what His majesty requires and His sanctity and perfection deserve. The source of His knowledge's connection with the world is His very knowledge of Himself. This connection appears through the appearance of the relations of His knowledge, which are His objects of knowledge. He knows what is without end through the encompassing character of His knowledge and His being the source of every thing. He knows His Essence, its concomitant, and the concomitant of that concomitant, collectively and separately, generally and in detail, and so on without end. Whatever He determines, or knows to have its rank determined, under a condition and cause, He knows with its condition and cause. His prior knowledge of it [the printed construction is unstable] entails its determination. Otherwise He knows it through Himself—glory be to Him—and however He wills. No knowledge arises newly for Him, and no matter or ruling is determined in His case that confines Him.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Since He is existence alone, He does not differ from existents in this respect. When His knowledge connects with Himself, it connects with the world as distinguished from the Real. “The appearance of this connection”—that of His knowledge with the world—is through the appearance of the relations of His knowledge. Since those relations are the objects known and have appeared, the connection with them appears, just as existence's connection with them appears when its relations—the realities of existents—appear. And since—",
      "ar": "والناقص. ]\nأي : لا يدركه سبحانه وتعالى من حيث كونه وجودا فحسب ، العقول البديهية والأفكار النظرية ، ولا تحويه الجهات والأقطار ، فلا تدركه الحواس الظاهرة ، ولا يحيط بمشاهدته الغيبية ، ومعرفته اليقينية البصائر الباطنة ، ولا جميع الأبصار ، \nثم علل ذلك بأنه منزّه عن القيود الصورية والمعنوية ، فكيف تدركه الحواس والعقول والأفكار التي هي مقيدة ، ثم بين تنزيهه تعالى عن القيود الصورية ، بأنه مقدس عن قبول كل تقديره متعلق بكمية أو كيفية ، وعن القيود المعنوية بأنه متعال عن الإحاطات الحدسية والفهمية والظنية والعلمية ، \nثم علل عدم إحاطة البصائر والأبصار ، بأنه محتجب بكمال عزته عن جميع بريته للكامل صاحب البصيرة ، والناقص المقتصر على ظاهر البصر ، وبين الكامل بأنه المقبل إليه ، والناقص بأنه النّاكص عنه . \n\nوقيد المقبل بقوله : في زعمه إشعارا بأنه لما احتجب عنه ، فلم يدركه ، فكيف يقبل إليه إقبالا حقيقيّا ، بل هو إقبال وهمي وإن أفاده مقاما أو حالا ، ثم استشعر سؤالا بأنه لا تدركه العقول والبصائر ، وقد أدركت تنزيهه ، \n\nفأخبر بما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ جميع تنزيهات العقول من حيث أفكارها ومن حيث بصائرها ، أحكام سلبية لا تفيد معرفة حقيقية ، وهي مع ذلك دون ما يقتضيه جلاله ويستحقه قدسه وكماله ، ومنشأ تعلق علمه بالعالم من عين علمه بنفسه ، وظهور هذا التعلق بظهور نسب علمه التي هي معلوماته ، وإنما هو عالم بما لا يتناهى من حيث إحاطة علمه وكونه مصدرا لكل شيء ، فيعلم ذاته ولازم ذاته ، ولازم اللازم جمعا وفرادى ، وإجمالا وتفصيلا ، هكذا إلى ما لا يتناهى وما عينه أو علم تعين مرتبته عند شرط وسبب ، فإنه يعلمه بشرط وسببه ، ولازمة أن سبق علمه بذلك تعينه ، وإلا فيعلمه بنفسه سبحانه وكيف شاء ، غير أنه لا يتجدد له علم ، ولا يتعين في حقه أمر ينحصر فيه ولا حكم ] . \n\nأي : لما كان وجودا فحسب ، لم يغاير الموجودات من هذا الوجه ، فلما تعلق علمه بنفسه ، تعلق بالعالم متميزا عن الحق ، \nقال : ( وظهور هذا التعلق ) أي : تعلق علمه بالعالم ، سبب ظهور نسب علمه ، فإن تلك النسب لما كانت هي المعلومات وقد ظهرت ، ظهر التعلق بها كما ظهر تعلق الوجود بها عند ظهور نسبه التي هي حقائق الموجودات ، ولما كان",

The unstable ولازمة أن سبق علمه بذلك تعينه is rendered with an explicit notice, not treated as secure Arabic. The final explanatory sentence is kept open at the page boundary.",
      "source_url": "https://archive.org/download/machra3-khosous/machra3-khosous.pdf",

    {
      "id": "MSH-P220",
      "printed_page": 220,
      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —this implies that His knowledge is one, it might seem that He could not know the many through it, although He knows endlessly many things.\n\nHe says: He knows what is without end because His knowledge encompasses His Essence, and His Essence encompasses things, since their realities are His affairs. This concerns the realities. As for existence's connection with them, He knows through being the source of every thing. This is among the attributes of the Essence that do not differ from it in its own rank, and is one of its concomitants. When He knows the Essence wholly, He knows this attribute, because knowledge of what entails entails knowledge of its concomitant. He therefore knows the Essence's being a source and what follows from this: existence's connection with things—that is, the realities that are affairs within the Essence and fixed entities in knowledge. He knows them collectively and generally in respect of the Essence, and individually and in detail in respect of the attributes and existential connection. His one essential knowledge thus extends to endless objects of knowledge.\n\nIt might follow that He does not know temporal occurrences: in the first respect, because that is not the respect of their identity with Him; in the second, because they are not necessary concomitants of His being a source, but contingent matters. He therefore says, ‘Whatever He determines ... under a condition or cause,’ without the Essence depending upon it; or whatever He knows to have its rank determined under one of these, because it depends upon it in respect of its reality—He knows that thing through knowledge of its condition and cause. Even when it does not depend upon these so that they are necessary for it, He knows it through knowledge of its concomitant condition or cause, if His knowledge has preceded that it has a cause and condition and is determined only in their presence. That condition and cause must return to what is a concomitant of His Essence, or what He is intrinsically a source of. A concomitant has identity with the Essence in one respect, so He knows it in both respects. If it is connected with no condition or cause, necessary or otherwise, He knows it through Himself, because it follows from His being the source of things. However He wills a thing—whether connected with a condition and cause or not—He must know it eternally.\n\nIt might be imagined that when He knows a thing through its condition, cause, or concomitant, His knowledge is renewed. Furthermore, from eternity He knows Zayd's existence as future; when Zayd exists, He knows his existence; when he perishes, He knows it as past. How could knowledge not arise newly for Him? The answer is that from eternity He knows Zayd's existence at a particular time, its being present at that time, future in relation to eternity, and past in relation to what follows it. He thus knows what He has known—",
      "ar": "مقتضاه أن يكون علمه واحدا ، فلا يعلم المتعدد به ، مع أنه عالم بما لا يتناهى من المتعددات . \n\nقال : وإنما هو عالم بما لا يتناهى من حيث علمه ، محيط بذاته وذاته شاملة على الأشياء ؛ لأن حقائقها شؤونه هذه من جهة الحقائق ، وأما من جهة تعلق الوجود بها ، فمن حيث كونه مصدرا لكل شيء ؛ لأن هذه من جملة صفات الذات التي لا يغايرها في مرتبة الذات ، فهي من لوازمها ، فإذا علم الذات بالكلية علم هذه الصفة ؛ لأن العلم بالملزوم يستلزم العلم باللازم ، فيعلم مصدرية الذات ، \nوما يلزم مصدريتها من تعلق الوجود بالأشياء ، أعني الحقائق التي هي شؤون في الذات وأعيان ثابتة في العلم ، فيعلمها من حيث الذات جمعا وإجمالا ، ومن حيث الصفات والتعلق الوجودي ، فرادى وتفصيلا ، فسرى علمه الواحد الذاتي إلى ما لا يتناهى من المعلومات . \n\nولما كان مقتضاه ألا يعلم الحوادث الزمانية إما من جهة الأولى ؛ فلأنها غير جهة الاتحاد ، وإما من الجهة الثانية ؛ فلأنها ليست من لوازم مصدريته ؛ لأنها أمور جائزة . \n\nقال : ( وما عينه . . . عند شرط أو سبب ) من غير أن يتوقف عليها الذات ، أو علم تعين مرتبته عند أحدهما لتوقفه من حيث الحقيقة على ذلك ، فإنه تعالى يعلم ذلك الشيء بسبب علمه بشرطه وسببه ، وإن لم يتوقف عليها ، فلم يلزماه ، ويعلم سبب علمه بلازمة من الشرط ؛ والسبب أن سبق علمه بأن له سببا وشرطا ، \nهو إنما يتعين عندهما لا دونهما ؛ لأن ذلك الشرط ، والسبب لا بدّ وأن يرجعا إلى ما هو من لوازم ذاته ، أو بالذات مصدرا له ، واللازم له اتحاد بالذات من وجهة ، فيعلمه من الجهتين ، وإن لم يكن متعلقا بشرط وسبب لازم ولا غير لازم ، يعلمه سبحانه بنفسه ؛ لأنه من لوازم مصدريته للأشياء ، فكيف ما شاء الشيء من تعليقه على الشرط والسبب ، ولا تعليقه بهما لا بدّ وأن يعلمه علما أزليّا . \n\nولما توهم أنه إذا علم الشيء بشرطه أو بسببه أو لازمه ، فهو على متجدد ، على أنه يعلم وجود زيد في الأزل مستقبلا ، فإذا وجد علم وجوده ، فإذا فني علمه ماضيا ، فكيف لا يتجدد له علم بذلك ، فإنه علم في الأزل وجود زيد في الزمان الفلاني ، وحاليته لذلك الزمان ، واستقباله بالنسبة إلى الأزل ، ومضيه بالنسبة إلى ما بعده فيعلم بذلك ما علم ،",
      "review_status": "retranslated_against_print_and_transcription",

      "editorial_note_append": "Full page retranslation compared with scan. The compressed conditional-knowledge discussion is translated as a sequence of the author’s distinctions, without importing a modern theory of time. The final temporal example continues on p. 221.",

    {
      "id": "MSH-P221",
      "printed_page": 221,
      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —and likewise its dependence upon cause and condition does not entail its origination. He knows from eternity its ordering upon them. His knowledge of them entails His knowledge of it without knowledge of the cause temporally preceding knowledge of the effect.\n\nHe then states that knowledge is renewed through renewal of the known only for one in whose case a matter is determined that confines him. If he is confined within a time, he knows what is relative to that time, not another. Since God is not restricted by these times—His being from eternity is His very being for eternity—no knowledge arises newly for Him. Nor is a ruling determined in His case such that one could say He knows only Zayd's existence at a particular time, without knowing its futurity relative to eternity or its pastness relative to what follows his passing away. Rather, He knows all states through one knowledge. Likewise He knows what originated beings know, because their knowledges are shadows of His knowledge.\n\nHence God says, ‘Until We know’ [Q 47:31; the edition cites 47:32]. He encompasses things completely through all knowledges, but these are not renewed in His case, although their manifestation in loci of manifestation is renewed. Understand.\n\nHe then mentions a third ruling of existence insofar as it is existence alone:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “His perfection is through Himself. His existence is actual, not potential; necessary, not possible. He transcends known change and origination. Originated things do not contain Him so as to display or preserve Him. He does not bring them into being through need of another, nor do they bring Him into being. Things are connected with Him in respect of what is determined from Him; He is not connected with them in respect of their distinction from Him through multiplicity. Their existence for themselves depends upon Him, while He does not depend upon them. Through His reality He is independent of every thing, while every thing needs Him for its existence.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** His essential perfection is through Himself, not through His names, attributes, or loci of manifestation, because it is His Essence itself. The names, attributes, and their loci are only among its lights. His manifestation in what is outward is the reflection of His light within Himself. Hence His existence is actual, not potential, for what is potential is deficient.\n\nThis concerns His existence in His Essence, not the attributes of acts, which are sheer relations, or the loci of manifestation. Likewise His existence through Himself is necessary, not possible, even though His manifestation in the loci—",
      "ar": "وكذا توقفه على السبب والشرط لا يستلزم حدوثه ، بل يعلم في الأزل ترتبه عليه واستلزم علمه به ، علمه إياه من غير سبق ، علم بالسبب ، على العلم المسبب سببا زمانيّا . \n\nثم ذكر أنه إنما يتجدد العلم بتجدد المعلوم ، فمن يتعين في حقه أمر ينحصر فيه ، فإذا انحصر في زمان ، يعلم ما يكون بالنسبة إليه دون غيره ، ولما لم يتقيد سبحانه بهذه الأزمنة حتى أن كونه في الأزل عين كونه في الأبد ، لم يتجدد له شيء من العلم . \nثم ذكر أنه لا يتعين في حقه حكم حتى يقال إنه يعلم وجود زيد في الزمان الفلاني لا غير ، ولا يعلم استقباله بالنسبة إلى الأزل ومضيه بالنسبة إلى ما بعد فنائه ، بل يعلم جميع الأحوال بعلم واحد ، وهكذا يعلم ما تعلمه المحادثات الحادثة من حيث أن علومهم ظلال علمه تعالى . \n\nومن هنا يقول اللّه تعالى :حَتَّى نَعْلَمَ[ محمد : 32 ] ، فله الإحاطة الكلية بالأشياء بجميع العلوم ، لكنها لا تتجدد في حقه ، وإن تجدد ظهورها في المظاهر ، فافهم . \nثم ذكر حكما ثالثا للوجود من حيث هو وجود فحسب ، \n\nفقال رضي اللّه عنه :  [ كماله بنفسه ووجوده بالفعل لا بالقوة ، وبالوجوب لا بالإمكان ، منزّه عن التغير المعلوم والحدثان ، لا تحويه المحدثات لتبديه أو تصونه ، ولا يكونها لحاجة إلى سواه ولا تكونه ، ترتبط الأشياء به من حيث ما تعين منه ، ولا يرتبط بها من حيث امتيازها بتعدد عنه ، فيتوقف وجودها لها عليه ، ولا يتوقف عليه ، مستغن بحقيقته عن كل شيء مفتقر إليه في وجوده كل شيء] . \n\nأي : كماله الذاتي  “ 1  “ بنفسه ، لا بأسمائه وصفاته ومظاهره ؛ لأنه عين ذاته ، وإنما الأسماء والصفات ومظاهرها من أنوارها ، وظهوره في الظاهر عكس نوره في نفسه ؛ ولذلك كان وجوده بالفعل لا بالقوة ؛ لأن ما بالقوة ناقص . \n\nهذا بالنسبة إلى وجوده في ذاته ، لا بالنسبة إلى الصفات الفعلية التي هي نسب محضة ، والمظاهر وكذا وجوده لذاته بالوجوب لا بالإمكان ، وإن كان ظهوره في المظاهر",

The modern editor’s footnote defining essential perfection is not included as the author’s prose. The page’s final distinction continues on p. 222.",
