    {
      "id": "MSH-P222",
      "printed_page": 222,
      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —is through possibility, because perfection belongs to the Necessary, not the possible. The possible is deficient; if it is perfect, that perfection is not through itself. Since He is intrinsically necessary, He transcends known change, which would require the loss of a state within Himself. Only His relations to the loci of manifestation change.\n\nSince He transcends change, He transcends origination, because the origination of something within Him would entail His changing from what He was. Yet He is related to originated things through His connections with the realities of possible things, to appear in and through them, not in respect of the Essence or the essential and divine attributes. Because of His essential perfection and transcendence of changes, originated things do not contain Him by becoming His accidents so as to display Him as colours, lights, and dimensions display bodily substances. Nor do they contain Him as receptacles preserving Him from appearing, for that would entail essential change and deficiency: His manifestation and hiddenness would then not be through Himself. Certainly, His manifestation and hiddenness here, in the loci of manifestation, are through them. In relation to His Essence He is manifest; in respect of independence from the worlds He is hidden.\n\nSince His perfection is through His Essence, He does not bring originated things into being out of need for another. He brings them into being only to appear in loci of manifestation after His complete manifestation in His Essence. The perfection accruing to existence in respect of its inclusion of the affairs of possible things is completed only through them. The affairs within the Essence are the Essence itself, so this is no need for another. Neither do originated things bring Him into being, for He exists through Himself; His existence is not repeated through them. Rather, they appear and are connected through Him, and their manifesting reality acquires actual attributes that were potential through Him. What is brought into being is His connection with them. Those attributes appear upon Him through that connection after their hiddenness.\n\nHe then anticipates a question: since His perfection is through Himself and He has no need of originated things, in what respect are things connected with Him, so that He brings them into being? The answer is that their connection is [not] in respect of their otherness and distinction, but insofar as they are His determinations in manifestation, through which the perfection that is not essential to Him appears. Their existence is [His] existence with the restriction of His determination through them.\n\nTheir distinction concerns their multiplicity through their realities, unlike the aspect of existence: the effusion is one and becomes multiple according to the multiplicity of realities. Since their connection is through existence, their existence for themselves depends upon Him, without reciprocity. He is independent of everything through His reality, which is the reality of existence, although He is not independent of the loci in respect of His manifestation in them. Every thing needs Him for its existence, since nothing has existence from itself. Otherwise every thing would be intrinsically necessary, and there would be many things intrinsically eternal.",
      "ar": "بالإمكان ؛ لأن الكمال للواجب دون الممكن ، فإنه ناقص ، فإن كان كاملا فليس بنفسه . \nولما كان واجبا بالذات كان منزها عن التغيير المعلوم لاستلزامه زوال حاله بذاته ، وإنما يتغير نسبه إلى المظاهر . \n\nولما تنزّه عن التغيير ، تنزه عن الحدثان ؛ لأن حدوث شيء فيه ، يستلزم تغيره عما كان عليه ، إلا أنه ينتسب إليها بحسب تعلقاته بحقائق الممكنات ، للظهور فيها وبها ، لا بحسب الذات والصفات الذاتية والإلهية ، ولكماله الذاتي وتنزهه عن التغيرات لا تحويه المحدثات بأن تصير أعراضه لتبديه إبداء الألوان والأضواء ، والمقادير والجواهر الجسمانية ، ولا تحويه أيضا بأن تصير ظروفه لتصونه عن الظهور ؛ لأنه يستلزم التغيير والنقص بالذات ، إذ ظهوره بطونه حينئذ ليس بذاته . نعم ظهوره في المظاهر وبطونه هاهنا بها . وأما بالنسبة إلى ذاته فظاهرة ، ومن حيث الغناء عن العالمين باطن . \n\nولما كان كماله بذاته ، لا تكون المحادثات لحاجة له إلى سواه ، بل إنما كونها لظهوره في المظاهر بعد الظهور الكامل في ذاته ؛ لأن الكمال العارض للوجود من حيث اشتماله على شؤون الممكنات لا يتم إلا بها ، والشؤون في الذات عينها ، فليس ذلك حاجة إلى الغير ولا المحدثات تكونه ؛ لأنه موجود بذاته ، فلا يتكرر وجوده بها ، بل تظهر به وتتعلق ، ويحصل لظاهرها صفات بالفعل كانت لها القوة بسببه . \nفالمكون إنما هو تعلقه لها ، وتلك الصفات ظهرت عليه بذلك التعلق بعد بطونها . \nثم استشعر سؤالا بأنه لما كان كماله بنفسه ، ولا حاجة له إلى المحدثات ، فما من وجه ارتباط الأشياء به حتى كونها ، \n\nفقال : [ ارتباط الأشياء به من حيث غيريتها وامتيازها ، بل من حيث إنها تعيناته المظهرية يظهر بها الكمال الذي ليس بذاتي له ، ووجودها غير وجود مع قيد تعينه بها ] . \nوأما امتيازها فمن حيث تعددها بحقائقها ، بخلاف جهة الوجود ، فإن الفيض واحد تعدد بحسب تعدد الحقائق ، ولما ارتبطت من جهة الوجود ، توقف وجودها لأنفسها عليه من غير عكس ، فهو مستغن بحقيقته التي هي حقيقة الوجود عن كل شيء ، \nوإن لم يستغن باعتبار ظهوره في المظاهر عنها ، مفتقر إليه في وجوده كل شيء ، إذ كل شيء ، ليس له وجود من ذاته ، وإلا لكان كل واجبا بالذات ، فيتعدد القدماء بالذّات .",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Having stated that things are connected with Him through their existence, he explains what causes existence to be connected with them:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “Between Him and things there is no relation except providence, as has been said; and no veil except ignorance, confusion, and imagination, because of His utmost proximity and nearness, and the excess of His might and exaltation. His providence is, in reality, the effusion of His existential light upon what is imprinted in the mirror of its entity—which is the relation of its being known—and is prepared to receive the ruling of His bringing it into existence and being a locus of His manifestation. He is exalted: ‘Nothing is like His likeness’ from the first aspect, while ‘He is the Hearing, the Seeing’ from the second.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Here begins the second consideration; what preceded concerned pure existence. Although discussions of connection were mentioned, they were digressions. The primary purpose was to explain existence as such and its rulings in that respect. Rulings concerning its connections were introduced because explaining the essential rulings depended upon them: things are made clear by their opposites.\n\nThat is, between the Real as such and things there is no relation of His existence's connection with them—despite His essential independence of them—except providence, which is prior knowledge, as the philosophers say. Otherwise He would need them to perfect His Essence, or act in vain, which is a deficiency.\n\nSince things exist through His existence because of His providence for them as forms of His affairs, there is no veil between them and Him, owing to His utmost proximity and nearness, except their ignorance and the confusion of imagining their multiplicities. Owing to the excess of His might and exaltation, all these loci together cannot encompass Him, still less one of them.\n\nHe then explains that providence, although interpreted as prior knowledge of all things, is in reality the effusion of existential light. Prior knowledge does not suffice for things to occur externally without effusion—that is, the determination of His existence in respect of its luminosity and manifestation, not in respect of the Essence. Providence is completed only through this effusion, which is therefore its reality, as though the greatest of its intrinsic constituents.\n\nHe then identifies that upon which effusion occurs: what is imprinted and inscribed in the mirror of its fixed entity. He does not make it the fixed entity itself, since the entity's nonexistence continues. What is imprinted is its form; effused existence attaches to that form. That reality is a relation of its being known to God. But what is imprinted must be prepared to receive the ruling of God's bringing it into existence and appearing within it. Otherwise it does not exist, even if it is intrinsically possible.\n\nHe then states that rational transcendence concerns the first aspect: a likeness is what can take the place of another of its kind—",
      "ar": "ولما ذكر أن ارتباط الأشياء به من حيث وجودها ، ثم ذكر ما هو سبب تعلق الوجود بها ، \nفهو كما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ ليس بينه وبين الأشياء نسبة إلى العناية كما قيل ، ولا حجاب إلا الجهل والتلبيس والتخيّل لغاية قربه ودنوه وفرط عزه وعلوه ، وعنايته في الحقيقة إفاضة نوره الوجودي على من انطبع في مرآة عينه التي هي نسب معلوميته ، واستعد لقبول حكم إيجاده ومظهريته سبحانه ، ليس كمثله شيء من الوجه الأول ، وهو السميع البصير من الوجه الثاني ] . \n\nمن هنا شروع في الثاني إذ ما قبله جهة الوجود المحض ، وإن ذكر فيه أبحاث من التعلق على طريق الاستطراد ؛ لأن المقصود بالذات بيان الوجود من حيث هو ، وبيان أحكامه من تلك الحيثية ، واستطرد بالأحكام التي تتعلقها لتوقف بيان الأحكام الذاتية عليها ، إذ الأشياء تتبين بأضدادها ، أي : ليس بين الحق من حيث هو وبين الأشياء نسبة تعلق وجوده بها مع غنائه عنها بحسب الذات إلا العناية التي هي العلم السابق ، كما قاله الفلاسفة ، وإلا لكان مفتقرا إليها في استكمال ذاته بها ، أو كان عابثا وهو من النقائص . \n\nولما كانت الأشياء موجودة بوجوده لعنايته بها من حيث أنها صور شؤونه ، فلا حجاب بينها وبينه ، لغاية قربه منها ودنوه إلا الجهل منها ، والتلبيس تخيل تعداداتها لفرط عزه وعلوه ، فلا يحاط به هذه المظاهر كلها فضلا عن مظهر واحد منها . \nثم ذكر أن العناية وإن فسرت بسبق العلم بالأشياء كلها في الحقيقة هي إفاضة النور الوجودي إذ سبق العلم لا يكفي لحصول الأشياء في الخارج بدون الإفاضة ، أي تعين وجوده من حيث نوريته وظهوره ، لا من حيث الذات ، فالعناية إنما كملت بهذه الإفاضة ، فهي حقيقة تلك العناية ، كأنه أعظم أجزائه الذاتية . \n\nثم ذكر المفاض عليه بأنه من انطبع وانتقش في مرآة عينه الثابتة ، ولم يجعل نفس العين الثابتة لاستمرار عدمها والمنطبع صورته والوجود المفاض لا حق بتلك الصورة ، وتلك الحقيقة نسبة معلوميته تعالى ؛ لكن شرط المنطبع أن يكون مستعدا لقبول حكم إيجاده تعالى إياه وظهوره فيه ، وإلا لا يوجد وإن كان في ذاته ممكنا . \nثم ذكر أن التنزيه العقلي  “ 1  “ يختص بالوجه الأول إذ المثل ما يقوم مقام آخر من نوعه",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —but existence has no plurality, so it has no likeness. ‘The Hearing, the Seeing’ concerns the second aspect. Yet this includes a transcendence disclosed by unveiling when expressed exclusively. He indicates this by first saying, ‘He is exalted.’ He then states that this transcendence continues always, even when He appears in loci of manifestation:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “Whenever He is apprehended or witnessed, addresses or is addressed, this is from behind the veil of His might in the rank of His self just mentioned, through the relation of His outwardness and the ruling of His self-disclosure in the abode of His descent: the association of His general existence with possible things, and the shining of His light upon the entities of existents. It is nothing other than this.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Whenever the Real is apprehended through certain knowledge, witnessed with the eye of certainty in loci of manifestation or elsewhere, addresses any creature—angel, prophet, or saint—or is addressed, He must then be behind the veil of His might in the rank of oneness. He remains in His original rational transcendence.\n\nApprehension and the other acts mentioned occur through the relation of His outwardness to things. This relation is the ruling of His self-disclosure to them in the abode of His descent toward nearness to them. That nearness is through the association of His general existence with possible things. His association is not by contact, but by His light's shining upon the entities of existents. None of these acts occurs except through outwardness; oneness retains its rational transcendence.\n\nHe then explains why what exists and appears in them is called creation, although it is the transcendent Real in every rank, always:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “From this aspect, when the determination of His existence is considered as restricted by the attributes inseparable from each determinate possible entity—which are in reality the relations of His knowledge, collectively and separately—and by what follows from those attributes, the matters called affairs, properties, accidents, and the effects following the rulings of the name ‘Time,’ called times, ranks, and abodes, that determination and individuation is called ‘creation’ and ‘other.’ You will shortly learn its secret, if God—exalted is He—wills.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The transcendent Real is called ‘creation’ and ‘other’ from the second aspect when the determination of His existence is considered as restricted by the attributes inseparable from each determinate possible entity. The first qualification excludes Him in respect of the first determination; the second excludes His determination through the attributes of divinity and lordship. ‘Possible entities’ excludes impossibilities, which are called neither creation nor the Real.",
      "ar": "ولا تعدد للوجود فلا مثل ، وأما السميع والبصير فهو من الوجه الثاني ؛ لكن فيه تنزيه كشفي إذا أورده بطريق الحصر ، وإليه أشار رضي اللّه عنه لقوله :  “ أولا سبحانه  “ ، ثم ذكر أن ذلك التنزيه دائم مستمر ، وإن ظهر في المظاهر\n\nبما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ ومتى أدرك أو شوهد أو خاطب أو خوطب ، فمن وراء حجاب عزته في مرتبة نفسه المذكورة ، بنسبة ظاهريته ، وحكم تجليه في منزل تدليه من حيث اقتران وجوده العام بالممكنات ، وشروق نوره على أعيان الموجودات ليس غير ذلك].\n\nأي : متى أدرك الحق بالعلم اليقيني أو شوهد بعين اليقين في المظاهر ، أو غيرها أو خاطب أحدا من خلقه ملكا أو نبيّا أو وليّا أو خوطب ، فلا بدّ وأن يكون الحق حينئذ من وراء حجاب عزته في المرتبة الأحدية ، فيكون على تنزيهه الأصلي العقلي . \n\nوإنما وقع الإدراك ، وما عطف عليه بنسبة ظاهريته للأشياء ، وهذه النسبة هي حكم تجليه لها في منزل تدليه إلى قربة منها ، وذلك القرب من حيث اقتران وجوده العام بالممكنات ، وليس اقترانه بطريقة اتصال بل بشروق نوره على أعيان الموجودات ، ولا يقع شيء منها إلا بالظاهرية والأحدية على نزاهته العقلية  “ . \nثم ذكر سبب كون ذلك الموجود الظاهر فيها خلف ، مع أنه الحق المنزه في كل مرتبة \n\nدائما بما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ فهو سبحانه من حيث هذا الوجه إذا لومح تعين وجوده متقيدا بالصفات اللازمة لكل متعين من الأعيان الممكنة التي هي في الحقيقة نسب علمه جمعا وفرادى ، وما يتبع تلك الصفات من الأمور المسماة شئونا والخواص والعوارض ، والآثار التابعة لأحكام الاسم الدهر المسماة بالأوقات والمراتب أيضا والمواطن ، فإن ذلك التعين والتشخص يسمى خلقا وسوى ، كما ستعرف عن قريب سره إن شاء اللّه تعالى ] . \n\nأي : والحق المنزه يسمى خلقا وسوى من الوجه الثاني إذا لو محيي تعين وجوده مقيدا بالصفات اللازمة لكل متعين من الأعيان الممكنة بالقيد الأول ، خرج من حيث التعين الأول وبالقيد الثاني خرج من حيث تعينه بصفات الإلهية والربوبية ، وبقيد الأعيان الممكنة خرجت الممتنعات ، فإنها لا تسمّى خلقا كما لا تسمّى حقّا .",

      "id": "MSH-P225",
      "printed_page": 225,
      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī:** He then states that those entities are, in reality, relations of His knowledge, indicating that their basis is nonexistence. They have no attribute apart from considering existence's determination through them. Hence we said that existence is restricted by those attributes.\n\nHe states that there is no difference between the attributes collectively and separately, lest one suppose that when those attributes are gathered together they are not called creation, since comprehensiveness belongs especially to divinity. The comprehensiveness meant here, however, is that of all the inseparable attributes accruing through determination according to possible entities. These are essential attributes of those things, further restricted by what follows from them. Through these concomitants distance from necessity and proximity to possibility increase, confirming their created character.\n\nHe mentions them lest one suppose that these incidental matters do not bring about createdness, since the basis of existence is necessity. It should not be said that the basis is altered merely through the accession of these attributes. This supposition is removed because their accession follows the establishment of createdness; they do not oppose or confront that basis. These concomitants include the matters called ‘affairs’: things' receptivities to existent attributes; properties peculiar to some things rather than others; and general accidents accruing to a thing without being peculiar to it. Although these attributes are not essential constituents, they endure in their subjects.\n\nLikewise there are effects following the rulings of the name ‘Time,’ one of God's names, as in the report: ‘The son of Adam hurts Me: he reviles Time, while I am Time; I turn night and day.’ Those rulings are called times, and their effects are temporal changes. There are also effects accruing through ranks, from the highest world [the printed formulation is compressed], and through abodes, such as what accrues to the elements through their reception of composition and transformation from one form to another.\n\nHe mentions these matters to indicate that created things must possess all these forms. The list does not exclude anything, but discloses the full created reality and its attributes. He then states that its secret will soon be known: he will say, ‘Through His permeation of every thing,’ and so forth. You will understand it, if God—exalted is He—wills.\n\nHe then mentions the rulings of existence from this aspect:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “Every attribute is then ascribed to Him—”",
      "ar": "ثم ذكر أن تلك الأعيان في الحقيقة نسب علمه إشعارا بأن أصلها عدم ليس لها صفة لاعتبار تعين الوجود بها ؛ فلذلك قلنا : أن الوجود تقيد بتلك الصفات . \n\nثم ذكر أنه لا فرق بين الصفات جمعا وفرادى ؛ لئلا يتوهم إن تلك الصفات إذا كانت على الجمعية ، لا تسمى خلقا من حيث أن الجمعية من خواص الإلهية ، وذلك إن تلك جمعية جميع الصفات اللازمة اللاحقة باعتبار التعين بحسب الأعيان الممكنة ، وهذه الصفات ذاتية تلك الأشياء ، ومقيدة بما يتبع تلك الصفات ، إذ بهذه التوابع يزداد البعد عن الوجوب ، والقرب من الإمكان ، فهي مؤكّدة للخلقية . \n\nوإنما ذكرها ؛ لئلا يتوهم إن هذه الأمور العارضة لا تجعل من الخلقية ، إذ أصل الوجود الوجوب ، فلا يقال : هذا الأصل من قبيل عروض هذه الصفات ، لكن الوهم يندفع بأن عروضها بعد ثبوت الخلقية ، فليس في معارضية الأصل ومقابلته في شيء ، وتلك التوابع من الأمور المسماة شئونا ، أي : قابليات الأشياء للاتصاف بصفات وجودية ، وخواص تختص ببعض الأشياء دون بعض . \n\nوعوارض تمامه تعرض للشيء من غير اختصاص به ، وهذه الصفات وإن لم تكن من الذاتيات ، فهي دائمة لموصوفاتها ، وهكذا الآثار التابعة لأحكام الاسم الدهر الذي هو من أسماء اللّه تعالى ، كما ورد في الحديث :  “ يؤذيني ابن آدم ، يسب الدهر ، وأنا الدهر أقلب الليل والنهار  “  “ 1  “ ، وتلك الأحكام المسماة بالأوقات ، وآثارها هي التغيرات الزمانية وكذا العارضة باعتبار المراتب من عالم الأعلى ، والعارضة باعتبار المواطن كالعارض للعناصر من جهة قبول التركيب ، والانقلاب من صورة إلى صورة . \nوإنما ذكر هذه الأشياء ؛ إشعارا بأن المخلوقات لا بدّ وأن تتصف بهذه الصور كلها ، فذكر هذه الأمور ليس لإخراج شيء ، بل للاطلاع على كمال الحقيقة الخلقية وصفاتها . \nثم ذكر أن سر ذلك سيعرف عن قريب ، وذلك أنه سيذكر :  “ أنه بسريانه في كل شيء . . . إلى آخره  “ ، وستعرفه إن شاء اللّه تعالى . \n\nثم ذكر أحكام الوجود بهذا الوجه بما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وينضاف إليه إذ ذاك  “ 2  “ كل وصف",

      "id": "MSH-P226",
      "printed_page": 226,
      "en": "**Qūnawī (continuing):** “—He is named by every name, appears through every trace, receives every ruling, is restricted in every place by every trace, and is apprehended by every faculty: sight, hearing, intellect, understanding, and the other powers and organs of perception. Remember.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** When existence is restricted by what has been mentioned, every originated attribute is ascribed to it. It is named by every name of originated things, appears through every trace of theirs, and receives every ruling of change. In each place it is restricted by the trace suited to that place, whether the place is intelligible or sensible. It is then apprehended by every outward faculty, such as hearing and sight, and every inward faculty, such as intellect and understanding, and other powers: common sense, imagination, estimation, memory, and reflection; and organs of perception such as the soul, heart, and spirit. Remember this matter, lest the Real veil you from creation or creation veil you from the Real.\n\nHe then states the secret of its restriction by these descriptions despite its transcendence of them:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “Know that this is through His permeation of every thing by His essential light, sanctified beyond partition, division, and indwelling in spirits and bodies. Understand.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** But all this is whenever He loves and however He wills. He is restricted by these attributes through His permeation—that is, His manifestation in such a way that His light flows through every thing. This is the essential, existential light that manifests all, while transcending partition within itself. Its division through the loci of manifestation is impossible; it appears in each locus according to the preparedness He has given it. This permeation is not indwelling, whether in immaterial spirits or in bodies as such. Although His manifestation in them accords with their preparedness, it is not by necessity, but whenever He loves and however He wills. Preparedness comes to it through His love and will, and self-disclosure accords with it. When He permeates them, He is restricted by their restrictions, which accrue to them through this permeation.\n\nHe then states that during permeation He is not confined by what He permeates:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “At every time and in every state, He receives these two opposing universal rulings through Himself, not through an additional matter, and unites every two differing things, absent and present, outgoing and incoming. If He wills, He appears in every form; if He does not will, no form is ascribed to Him.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** He receives through Himself at a temporal time and in a changing state. He specifies this because in respect of eternity He does not receive all—",
      "ar": "ويسمى بكل اسم ، ويظهر بكل رسم ، ويقبل كل حكم ، ويتقيد في كل مكان بكل رسم ، ويدرك لكل مشعر من بصر وسمع وعقل وفهم ، وغير ذلك من القوى والمدارك ، فاذكر ] . \nأي : وينسب إلى الوجود عند التقييد لما ذكر كل وصف حادث ، ويسمى بكل اسم من أسماء المحدثات ، ويظهر بكل رسم من رسومها ، ويقبل كل حكم من التغييرات ، ويتقيد في كل مكان بكل رسم يليق بذلك المكان ، سواء كان المكان معنويّا أو حسيّا ، ويدرك عنه ذلك بكل مشعر ظاهر من سمع وبصر وباطن من عقل وفهم وغير ذلك من القوى ، كالحس المشترك والخيال والوهم والحافظة والمفكرة والمدارك من النفس والقلب والروح ، فاذكر هذه المسألة ؛ لئلا يحجبك الحق عن الخلق ، والخلق عن الحق . \n\nثم ذكر سر تقييده بهذه الأوصاف مع تنزهه عنها بما قال الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه : [ واعلم أن ذلك بسريانه في كل شيء بنوره الذاتي المقدس عن التجزيء والانقسام والحلول في الأرواح والأجسام ، فافهم ] . \nولكن كل ذلك متى أحب وكيف شاء ، أي إنما يقيد بهذه الصفات باعتبار سريانه ، أي ظهوره بحيث يسرى نوره في كل شيء ، وهو النور الذاتي الوجودي المظهر للكل مع تقدسه عن التجزّيء في نفسه ، يمتنع انقسامه بالمظاهر ، لكن ظهر في كل مظهر بقدر استعداده الذي أعطاه . \nوليس ذلك السريان بطريق الحلول لا في الأرواح المجردة ولا في الأجسام المطلقة ، وظهوره فيها وإن كان بحسب استعدادها ، فليس بطريق الوجوب ؛ ولكن متى أحب وكيف شاء فإن الاستعداد حاصل له من حبه ومشيئته والتجلي بحسبه ، فإذا سري فيها تقيد بقيودها اللاحقة لها باعتبار هذا السريان . \n\nثم ذكر أنه حال السريان لا يتقيد بما سوي فيها ، \nفذلك ما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ وهو في كل وقت وحال القابل لهذين الحكمين الكليين المذكورين المتضادين بذاته لا بأمر زائد ، والجامع بين كل أمرين مختلفين من غائب وحاضر وصادر ووارد . إذا شاء ظهر في كل صورة ، وإن لم يشأ ، لم ينضاف إليه صورة ] ، \nأي : وهو القابل بذاته في وقت من الأوقات الزمانية ، وحال من الأحوال المتغيرة ، قيد بذلك ؛ لأنه من حيث الأزل لا يقبل الجميع ،",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —otherwise originated things would be eternal. It may also be said that He is receptive through Himself, but eternity prevents the reception. He thus receives the two universal rulings, detachment and restriction: detachment from everything in the first, and restriction by everything in the second. They are opposites with the utmost difference between them. Opposition, however, is considered only with respect to particular subjects and individual determinations. His receptivity is through Himself, not an additional matter ascribed to Him, since there is nothing beyond absolute existence whose attribution to Him could be considered. Although the effect of His receptivity to restriction by some matters concerns an additional matter, that matter is conceptual in relation to existence itself. His gathering of opposites—indeed, of every two differing things, whether opposed or not—is in respect of His form, not His Essence alone.\n\nForms differ with the different matters appearing in them, and those matters differ through the will ascribed to Him. If He wills, He appears in every form; if He does not will, no form is ascribed to Him at all. This is as on the day when He says, ‘Whose is the dominion today? God's, the One, the Overpowering’ [Q 40:16]. He says ‘if He does not will’ to indicate that willing nonexistence and not willing are alike in the non-attribution of forms. What is intended is the absence of will's connection, for will is eternal and does not cease. He then states that these forms do not change Him from what He is in oneness:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “His determination and individuation through forms, and His qualification by their attributes, do not impair the perfection of His existence, His might, or His sanctity. His manifestation in things, His making them manifest, and His determination and restriction through them and their rulings, insofar as they are themselves, do not contradict His exaltation, freedom from restrictions, or essential independence of everything described as existent. Rather, He—glory be to Him—unites realities that resemble and differ so that they combine, and those that differ and stand apart so that they remain diverse.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** His determination through specific and individual forms, and qualification by their originated attributes, do not impair the perfection of His existence in oneness and oneness-with-multiplicity. These determinations and individuations concern the loci of manifestation, not the Essence. They therefore contradict neither the Essence's perfection, nor His might beyond connection with them, nor His sanctity beyond originated things. What happens to a form in a mirror when the mirror moves or breaks does not happen to the possessor of the form. Thus His manifestation in things, His making them manifest, His determination through their lowly ranks, and His restriction by their possible realities and originated attributes from this aspect do not contradict His exaltation from another aspect, oneness; nor His essential absoluteness—",
      "ar": "وإلا لكانت الحوادث أزلية ، ويمكن أن يقال قابل بذاته ، إلا أن الأزل يمنع من القبول ، فهذا قابل لهذين الحكمين التجرد والتقيد الكليين ؛ لأنه اعتبر التجرد عن الكل في الأول ، والتقيد بالكل في الثاني ، وهما متضادان ، بينهما غاية الخلاف إلا أن الضدية إنما تعتبر بالنظر إلى الموضوعات الخاصة والتعينات الشخصية ، وقبوله له بذاته لا بأمر زائد ينضاف إليه إذ ليس وراء الوجود المطلق شيء حتى يعتبر انضيافه إليه ، وإن كان أثر قابليته للتقيد ببعض الأمور باعتبار الأمر الزائد ، لكن ذلك الأمر اعتباري بالنظر إلى نفس الوجود . نعم جمعيته المتقابلين ، بل لكل مختلفين سواء كان بينهما تقابل أم لا ، باعتبار صورته لا باعتبار ذاته فقط . \n\nواختلاف الصور باختلاف ما ظهر فيها من الأمور المختلفة ، واختلاف تلك الأمور بما ينضاف إليه من المشيئة ، فإذا شاء ظهر في كل صورة ، وإن لم يشأ لا ينضاف إليه صورة أصلا ، كما يكون يوم يقول عز وجل :لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ الْواحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ[ غافر : 16 ] . \nوإنما قال : وإن لم يشأ ؛ ليشعر بأن مشيئة العدم ، وعدم المشيئة سواء في عدم انضياف الصور ، والمراد عدم تعلق المشيئة ، وإلا فالمشيئة قديمة لا تنعدم ، ثم ذكر أن هذه الصور لا تغيره عما كان عليه في الأحدية . \n\nفذلك قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ لا يقدح تعينه وتشخصه بالصور ، واتصافه بصفاتها في كمال وجوده وعزه وقدسه ، ولا ينافي ظهوره في الأشياء وإظهاره وتعينه وتقيده بها وبأحكامها من حيث هي علوه وإطلاقه من القيود وغناه بذاته عن جميع ما وصف بالوجود ، بل هو سبحانه الجامع بين ما تماثل من الحقائق وتخالف فيتألف ، وبين ما تغاير وتباين فيختلف ] . \n\nأي : لا يقدح تعينه بالصور النوعية والشخصية ، واتصافه بصفاته الحادثة في كمال وجوده الأحدية والواحدية ؛ لأن هذه التعيّنات والتشخّصات باعتبار المظاهر لا بالذات ، فلا ينافي كمال الذات ولا عزته عن التعلق بها ، ولا قدسه عن الحوادث لذلك ، فإن ما يلحق الصورة في المرآة عند تحريكها أو كسرها ، لا يلحق شيء ذا الصورة ، ولذلك لا ينافي ظهوره في الأشياء ، وإظهاره للأشياء ولا تعينه بمراتبها الدنيّة ، ولا تقيده بحقائقها الممكنة وبصفاتها الحادثة من هذه الحيثية ، علوه من حيثية أخرى هي الأحدية ، ولا إطلاقه الذاتي",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —nor His essential independence of all. Rather, while transcending all, He gathers realities that resemble one another and those that differ—that is, are proximate—and combines them. He makes them one, or gives them oneness, through the affinity between those realities, so that they accord with His unity accordingly.\n\nHe also gathers what is mutually incompatible and what stands apart, without a unifying affinity between them. They therefore do not accord with His unity and remain diverse, yet they come together through existence within existence. He does this to display receptivity through gathering and separation, because it encompasses all of them. He then mentions the names through which manifestation occurs at [origination] and concealment at annihilation:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “Through His existential self-disclosure hidden things appear, and blessings descend from the unseen into the witnessed, through His names the Expander and the Originator. Through the withdrawal of the ruling of His descent, existents become hidden and cease, through His names the Contractor and the Restorer.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Through His self-disclosure by general existence, according to the demand of the name the Expander upon the realities, and the Originator's making it manifest as restricted by them and their states, the realities and their attributes hidden in oneness-with-multiplicity appear. The blessings of those realities descend, through manifestation, from the unseen unity into the witnessed. These are the external self-disclosures upon them, actually complete after being potentially theirs. Then, through withdrawal of the ruling of His descent—that is, His nearness to the realities—what has become actual among them in external existence becomes hidden, indeed ceases externally, according to His names the Contractor and the Expander, concerning manifestation and hiddenness, and the Restorer, who returns what appeared to what it was at first.\n\nHe then explains why these names connect with origination and annihilation:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “He—exalted is He—was veiled by His might, and was Forgiving. When He loved to be known, He drew near and appeared in whatever He willed, however He willed, and was Loving. Through love, insofar as He is lover, He originates, and love makes Him manifest. Through love, insofar as He is lover and beloved, He restores every thing within His grasp and subdued beneath the force of His taking hold, because of the strength of His act and the weakness of what receives it.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** When He regards His exaltation and independence, He veils Himself from things through His might and is Forgiving—that is, concealing them. When He loves to be known, to perfect the world and existence through manifestation in loci and to bring what is potentially possible for both into actuality, [He draws near to] the realities and appears in whatever He wills through the eternal will that bestows preparedness upon them, however He wills there. He is thus Loving, through His appearing in them and making them appear. Through love, insofar as He is lover alone—there being no beloved from creation before origination—He originates—",
      "ar": "ولا غناه بذاته عن الجميع ، بل هو تعالى مع تنزهه عن الجميع ، يجمع بين الحقائق المتماثلة والمتخالفة أي المتقاربة ، فيؤلّف بينهما ، فيجعلها واحدة أو أحدية بسبب المناسبة التي بين تلك الحقائق ، حتى يناسب وحدته على حسب ذلك . \n\nويجمع أيضا بين ما ينافر أخرى تنافر ، وبين ما يباين ، فلا يكون بينهما مناسبة جامعة ، فلا يناسب وحدته فيختلف ، لكنها تجتمع بالوجود في الوجود . \nوإنما فعل ذلك إظهارا للقابلية على سبيل الاجتماع والافتراق ؛ لشموله لها جميعا ، ثم ذكر الأسماء التي بها الظهور عند الاتحاد والخفاء عند الإعدام . \n\nفلذلك قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ بتجليه الوجودي ظهرت الخفيّات ، وتنزلت من الغيب إلى الشهادة البركات ، من حيث أسمائه الباسط والمبديء ، وبارتفاع حكم تدلّيه تخفي وتنعدم الموجودات باسميه القابض والمعيد ] . \n\nأي : بتجليه بالوجود العام باقتضاء الاسم الباسط على الحقائق ، والمبديء إظهاره مقيدا بها وبأحوالها ، أظهرت الحقائق وأوصافها الخفيات في الواحدية ، وتنزلت بالظهور من غيب الوحدة إلى الشهادة بركات تلك الحقائق ، وهي التجليات عليها الخارجية الكاملة بالفعل بعد ما كانت لها بالقوة ، ثم بارتفاع حكم تدليه ، أي دنوه من الحقائق يخفي ما فعل منها في الوجود الخارجي ، بل ينعدم في الخارجي ، بمقتضى اسميه القابض والباسط للظهور والبطون ، والمعيد لما ظهر إلى ما كان عليه في الأول . \n\nثم بيّن سبب تعلق هذه الأسماء بالإيجاد والإعدام \nبما قال رضي اللّه عنه : [ إنه تعالى كان محتجبا بعزه ، فكان غفورا ، وإن أحب أن يعرف دنا وظهر فيما شاء كيف شاء ، فكان ودودا ، فبالمحبة يبدي من كونه محبّا ، وهي تبديه ، وبها من كونه محبّا ومحبوبّا يعيد كل شيء في قبضته ومقهور تحت قوة بطشه ؛ لقوة فعله وضعف المنفعل ] . \n\nأي : إن نظر سبحانه وتعالى علوه واستغنائه ، احتجب عن الأشياء بعزه فيكون غفورا ، أي : ساترا لها ، وإن أحب أن يعرف من جهة تكميل العالم والوجود بالظهور في المظاهر ، وإخراج ما لهما في الإمكان بالقوة إلى الفعل وما من الحقائق ، وظهر فيما شاء بالمشيئة الأزلية المفيضة عليها الاستعداد كيف شاء هناك ، فكان ودودا لظهوره فيها وإظهارها ، فبالمحبة من جهة كونه محبّا فقط ، إذ لا محبوب من الخلق قبل الإيجاد ، يبديء",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** —the realities by giving them existence, while love makes Him manifest by appearing in them after His manifestation through Himself within Himself. Through love, insofar as He is lover in created forms and beloved in respect of reality, He restores [them] to Himself. This includes the saying cited here as the Prophet's: ‘Love of homeland is part of faith.’\n\nHe then indicates that being lover and beloved does not suffice: every thing must also be in the grasp of His will and subdued beneath the force of His taking hold, which is His power. These are realized through the strength of His act, so that He is overpowering and grasping, and the weakness of [what receives] the act, so that it is grasped and overpowered. It is an instrument for His doing things as required by the wisdom that orders effects upon their causes, according to His customary way of bringing things into existence following the orientations of the universal intellects and souls.\n\nThe First Intellect is a locus of contraction in respect of its possibility, and expansion in respect of its necessity through its Lord; origination in respect of its existence, and concealment in respect of its immateriality; unseen in respect of belonging to the world of spirits, and witnessed in respect of its manifestation through its Lord; disclosure in respect of its recording unseen matters, and a veil in respect of its mediation between the Real and creation. It thus becomes a formal veil—that is, according to outward appearance, since in reality there is no agent except God. But because things are brought into existence upon its orientation, this is attributed to it as a cause, not as an agent.\n\nThrough this, the Real does what He does on the occasion of its orientation—not through its assistance or causality, but upon its orientation. This is as we say of our acts: they are the Real's creations, yet they occur upon our orientations toward them. All are therefore His acts without qualification. He then adduces evidence for this whole account in his following statement—",
      "ar": "الحقائق بإعطاء الوجود لها ، وتبديه بالظهور فيها بعد ظهوره بذاته في ذاته ، وبالمحبة من جهة كونه محبّا في الصور الخلقية ، ومحبوبا من جهة الحقيقة يعيد إليه ، ومنه قوله صلى اللّه عليه وسلم :  “ حب الوطن من الإيمان  “  “ 1  “ . \n\nثم أشار إلى أن المحبة والمحبوبية لا تكفيان في ذلك ، بل لا بد معها من كون كل شيء في قبضة مشيئته ، ومقهورا تحت قوة بطشه التي هو قدرته ، وهما يتمان بقوة فعله حتى يصير قاهرا قابضا ، وضعف الفعل حتى يصير مقبوضا مقهورا ؛ فلذلك لا يكون غيره فاعلا ، ولا يكون هو منفعلا . \nثم ذكر ما هو المظهر الأول الذي بواسطته ظهرت هذه الأشياء وأسبابها \n\nبما قال الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه : [ ومظهر قدرته ، وآلة حكمته في فعله بسنته ، ومحل ظهور سر القبض والبسط ، والإبداء والإخفاء ، والغيب الشهادة ، والكشف والحجاب الصوري السببي الذي به يفعل ما ذكره ولا مطلقا هو عرشه المجيد ] . \nأي : مظهر قدرته القاهرة ، العرش المجيد الذي هو العقل الأول على ما فسره الشيخ المحقق المحيى الحق والدين ابن العربي قدس اللّه روحه في رسالته المسماة بـ  “ العقلية  “ ، وهو آلة لفعله الأشياء على ما اقتضته الحكمة المرتبة للمسببات على أسبابها بسنته الجارية في إيجاد الأشياء ، عقيب توجهات العقول والنفوس الكلية ؛ \n\nوذلك لأن العقل الأول كان محلا لظهور القبض من حيث إمكانه ، والبسط من حيث وجوبه بربه ، والإبداء مكن حيث وجوده ، والإخفاء من حيث تجرده ، والغيب من حيث كونه من عالم الأرواح والشهادة من حيث ظهوره بربه ، والكشف من حيث تسطيره لأمور الغيبية ، والحجاب من حيث توسطه بين الحق والخلق ، فصار حجابا صوريّا ، أي بحسب الظاهر إذ لا فاعل في الحقيقة إلا اللّه ، لكنه لما كان إيجاد الأشياء عند توجهه نسب إليه لكونه سببا لا لكونه فاعلا \" . \n\nفهو الذي يفعل الحق ما يفعل بسبب توجهه لا بإعانته وسببيته ، بل عند توجهه كما نقول في أفعالنا أنها مخلوقات الحق ، لكنها توجد عند توجهاتنا إليها ؛ فلذلك كان الكل أفعاله مطلقا ، ثم استدل على هذا المجموع \n\nبما قال رضي اللّه عنه :",

      "en": "**Qūnawī (continuing):** “For this reason He—exalted is He—said, disclosing the secret of this matter: ‘For one who has a heart, or gives ear while present’ [Q 50:37]; ‘Your Lord's grasp is indeed mighty. It is He who originates and restores. He is the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Glorious Throne, Doer of whatever He wills’ [Q 85:12–16], in the two ranks of absoluteness and delimitation. His saying, ‘Doer of whatever He wills,’ answers an implicit question that He knew would arise from a veiled objector.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** That is, because of the ordering we have mentioned, He—exalted is He—spoke to disclose its secret by way of allusion, so that understanding it belongs specifically to one who has a heart that discovers the obscure meanings of the Qurʾān, or who gives ear to the shaykhs who disclose them, being present and wholly attentive, as though looking at what he hears. Your Lord's “grasp”—that is, His power—is mighty: it acts upon whatever He wills, however He wills. He originates insofar as He is Loving, and restores insofar as He is both Forgiving and Loving. He does this through the Glorious Throne, which is the First Intellect. Restoration is to hiddenness; origination is to manifestation.\n\nHis saying, “Doer of whatever He wills,” indicates that He has no need of causes, as one might suppose from His saying, “Lord of the Glorious Throne.” Rather, He does whatever He wills, with causes and without them. Causes accord with wisdom. The saying also indicates that He does not necessitate things by His essence, as one might suppose from the statement that forgiveness and lovingness necessitate restoration and origination. He therefore explains that their self-disclosure, too, is through His will and choice, not through necessitation, as the people of veiling maintain.\n\n**Text Twenty-Two**\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Having finished establishing unity, he begins to disclose what most often veils it. He explains this in his saying—may God be pleased with him—“A noble text.” It is the last of the texts because through it the clarification of divine unity, the noblest of the objects sought, attains completion. The remaining veils become easy to uncover once this is uncovered. Its position at the end is also because the complete clarification of divine unity occurs at the station of the oneness of gathering and distinction, which is the last of the stations as they are conventionally known.\n\n**Qūnawī:** “Know that the greatest doubt and veil is that the multiplicities occurring in the one existence necessitate the effects of the fixed entities within it, and thus give the impression that the entities have appeared in existence and through existence—”",
      "ar": "[ ولهذا قال سبحانه وتعالى مبدئ سر هذا الأمر : لِمَنْ كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ أَوْ أَلْقَى السَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ [ ق : 37 ] ، إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ ( 12 ) إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ ( 13 ) وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ ( 14 ) ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ ( 15 ) فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ ( 16 ) [ البروج : 12 - 16 ] في مرتبتي الإطلاق والتقييد ، وقوله : فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [ البروج : 16 ] ، جواب سؤال مقدر ، علم أنه يبدو من معترض محجوب]\n .\nأي : لما ذكرنا من الترتيب ، قال سبحانه لإظهار سر هذا الترتيب بطريق الرمز بحيث يختص بالفهم من كان له قلب يستكشف المعاني الغامضة من القرآن ، أو ألقى السمع إلى المشايخ الكاشفة لها ، وهو حاضر كامل التوجه ، كأنه ينظر إلى ما يسمع أن بطش - أي قدرة - ربك لشديد يؤثر فيما شاء كيف شاء أنه هو يبدي من حيث كونه ودودا ، ويعيد من حيث كونه غفورا ودودا معا ، يفعل ذلك بالعرش المجيد الذي هو العقل الأول . الإعادة إلى البطون ، والإبداء إلى الظهور ، \nفي قوله تعالى : فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [ البروج : 16 ] ، إشارة إلى أنه لا يحتاج إلى الأسباب كما يتوهم من قوله تعالى : ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ [ البروج : 15 ] ، بل فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [ البروج : 16 ] ، بالأسباب وبدونها . \nوإنما الأسباب على مقتضى الحكمة ، وإلى أنه ليس موجبا بالذات ، كما يتوهم من أن الغفورية والودودية يوجبان الإعادة والإبداء ، فبيّن أن تجليها أيضا بمشيئته واختياره لا بإيجاب ، كما يقول أهل الحجاب .\n\nالنص الثاني والعشرون \nولما فرغ عن تحقيق التوحد ، شرع في كشف ما يحجب عنه غالبا ، فذلك بما قال رضي اللّه عنه :\n[ نص شريف ] هو آخر النصوص ؛ لأن كمال إيضاح التوحيد الذي هو أشرف المطالب حاصل به ، والحجب الباقية تيسر انكشافه عند انكشافه وآخريته لأن كمال اتضاح التوحيد في مقام أحدية الجمع والفرق ، وهو آخر المقامات فيما يتعارف .\n\nقال الشيخ رضي اللّه عنه : [ اعلم أن أعظم الشبه والحجب أن التعدّدات الواقعة في الوجود الواحد توجب آثار الأعيان الثابتة فيه ، فتوهم  “ 1  “ أن الأعيان ظهرت في الوجود وبالوجود ،",

      "en": "**Qūnawī (continuing):** “—whereas only their effects have appeared in existence. They themselves have not appeared and never will appear, because their very selves do not entail manifestation.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** This is the greatest of the doubts that veil divine unity because all the veils of deficiency, possibility, and changes branch from this one. Once it is removed, it is as though all have been removed.\n\nHe means that these multiplicities are only the effects of the fixed entities within the one existence that is manifest through them. They therefore give the impression that it is the entities that have appeared in existence and are what is seen, and that they have appeared through an existence peculiar to them, other than the existence of the Necessary. He rejects this: what is manifest in them and through them is the Real. Only the effects of the entities have appeared within that one existence. Those entities have not appeared and never will appear, because in themselves they do not entail—that is, do not admit—manifestation. They are nonexistent things, and nonexistence has no manifestation. Rather, existence is the Manifest and the Hidden.\n\nHence Shaykh Muḥyī al-Dīn said in *Inshāʾ al-dawāʾir*: “Existence is not something additional to existence,” because existence is what is manifest. This does not contradict its being additional to quiddity in what is other than the Necessary. He then explains how to interpret statements of the realized knowers that differ from this, in the shaykh's words—may God exalt his station:\n\n**Qūnawī:** “Whenever a realized knower reports otherwise, or ascribes existence and manifestation to those entities, that report is in the language of certain ranks and relative tastes. That is, its correctness is established only in relation to a particular station, or particular stations, short of the taste of the station of perfection. As for the definitive text whose ruling is not abrogated, it is what we have stated. The same applies to everything mentioned in this book: it is the explicit truth according to which the matter is. What is said otherwise may be correct without qualification, as is what we have stated here; or it may be correct in relation and attribution to a certain station, as already indicated.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** That is, whenever a realized knower reports from his unveiling something other than our statement that manifestation belongs to existence—for example, saying that manifestation belongs to the entities and that existence is realized in them, or ascribing both existence and manifestation to them and saying that they possess relative existence, which is the shadow of true existence, and that they are what is manifest through it—he reports only in the language of certain ranks of unveiling and certain relative tastes. This does not mean that a reporter who has unveiled all the stations reports in this way from some of them. It means that these words are correct from their speaker only when he has reached a particular station, or particular stations, and is confined to them, without having reached the station of perfection. One who has reached it takes no account of the entities' manifestation or existence: rather, the one existence is what is manifest within them.",
      "ar": "وإنما ظهرت آثارها في الوجود ولم تظهر هي ، ولا تظهر أبدا ؛ لأنها ذاتها لا تقتضي الظهور ] . \n\nإنما كان هذا أعظم الشبه الحاجبة عن التوحيد ؛ لأن جميع الحجب من النقص والإمكان والتغييرات فرع هذا ، فإذا ارتفع ، فكأنه ارتفع الكل . \n\nيعنى : أن هذه التعددات إنما هي آثار الأعيان الثابتة في الوجود الواحد الظاهر بها ، فتوهم أن الأعيان هي التي ظهرت في الوجود ، فهي المرئية ، وظهرت بوجود خاص لها غير وجود الواجب ، فرد ذلك بأن الظاهر هو الحق فيها وبها ، وإنما ظهرت آثار الأعيان في ذلك الوجود الواحد ، ولم تظهر تلك الأعيان ولا تظهر أبدا ؛ لأنها بالذات لا تقتضي ، \nأي : لا تقبل الظهور ؛ لأنها أمور عدمية ولا ظهور للعدم بل الوجود هو الظاهر والباطن . \nومن هنا قال الشيخ محيي الدين في  “ إنشاء الدوائر  “  “ 1  “ : إن الوجود ليس بزائد على الوجود ؛ لأن الوجود هو الظاهر ، ولا ينافي كونه زائدا على الماهية في غير الواجب ، ثم ذكر تأويل ما يخالفه من أقوال المحققين ، \n\nبما قال الشيخ أعلى اللّه مقامه : [ ومتى أخبر محقق بغير هذا أو نسب إليها الوجود والظهور ، فإنما ذلك الإخبار بلسان بعض المراتب والأذواق النسبية ، أي : إنما يثبت صحتها بالنسبة إلى مقام معين ، أو مقامات مخصوصة دون ذوق مقام الكمال ، وأما النص الذي لا ينسخ حكمه ، فهو ما ذكرناه وهكذا كل ما ذكر في هذا الكتاب ، فإنه الحق الصريح الذي هو الأمر عليه ، وما سواه ، فقد يكون صحيحا مطلقا كهذا الذي ذكرنا ، وقد يكون صحيحا بالنسبة والإضافة إلي مقام ما ، كما سبقت الإشارة إليه ] . \nأي : ومتى أخبر محقق عن كشفه بغير ما ذكرنا من أن الظهور للوجود ، بأن قال : \nالظهور لها والوجود محقق فيها ، أو نسب إليها الوجود والظهور جميعا ، وقال لها : الوجود الإضافي هو ظل الوجود الحق ، وهي الظاهرة بذلك الوجود ، فإنما ذلك الإخبار بلسان بعض مراتب الكشف وبلسان بعض الأذواق النسبية لا بمعنى أن المخبر المكاشف بجميع المقامات يخبر بذلك عن بعضها ، بل بمعنى أن هذا الكلام ، إنما يصح من المخبر بها إذا بلغ مقاما معينا ، أو مقامات مخصوصة وتقيد بها ، ولم يصل إلى مقام الكمال ، فإن الواصل إليه لا يعتد بظهورها ولا وجودها ، بل الظاهر هو الوجود الواحد فيها .",

      "en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** This is the definitive text that nothing higher abrogates, unlike those stations, which are abrogated by what is higher than they are. He then states that all his definitive texts proceed from the station of perfection and are correct without qualification. This differs from what is mentioned in his other books and in the books of others: that may or may not be so, although it must be correct in relation and attribution to some station. The earlier indication, in the third subdivision of the first three texts, was that all unveilings must be correct in some respect.\n\nIf it is asked, “It has been stated repeatedly that the entities are manifest,” we answer: what is meant is their manifestation through the Real's manifestation within them, not through their own selves, just as their existence is in this way. That manifestation and existence are the Real Himself, not the entities; the entities are forever nonexistent.\n\nIf it is asked, “Then this would not be one of the definitive texts,” we answer: it would fail to be one of the definitive texts only on the assumption that manifestation [occurs] through their very selves. Otherwise, this statement admits no abrogation. Understand.\n\n**Qūnawī:** “When what I have mentioned in this text becomes clear to you, you will know that manifestation is in existence, but on condition of multiplicity together with the effects of the entities within it; and that hiddenness is an intrinsic attribute of the entities, and also of existence insofar as its unity is conceived. The matter turns between manifestation and hiddenness, predominance and subordination: what diminishes from the manifest is included in the hidden, and conversely. Relations and attributions are forms of states and rulings that arise among the ranks. Some make others manifest, and some conceal others, according to the predominance and subordination just indicated. Understand.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** O God, bless our master Muḥammad and his family and companions, and grant them peace. That is, [when] what I have mentioned becomes clear to you—that manifestation belongs to the effects of the entities within existence—you know that manifestation belongs to existence. For the entities have no effect insofar as they are themselves, because they are nonexistent, but only insofar as existence is connected with them. The effects are therefore, in reality, the effects of existence on condition of the entities. “Then, when the effects of existence become manifest on condition of—”\n\n**[The sentence ends at this point in the 2008 printed edition.]**\n\n“Its end; and praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.”",
      "ar": "هذا هو النص الذي لا ينسخ بما هو أعلى منه ، بخلاف تلك المقامات فإنها تنسخ بما هي أعلى منها ، ثم ذكر أن جميع نصوصه إنما هي على مقام الكمال وصحتها على الإطلاق ، بخلاف المذكور في غيره من كتبه وكتب غيره ، فإنه قيد يكون كذلك وقد لا يكون ، مع أنه لا بدّ وأن يكون صحيحا ، والإضافة إلى مقام ما سبقت الإشارة في التفريع الثالث من تفاريع النصوص الثلاثة : الأول من أن جميع الكشوف لا بدّ من صحتها بوجه . \nفإن قيل : قد مر مرارا أن الأعيان ظاهرة ، قلنا : المراد ظهورها بظهور الحق فيها ، لا بذاتها ، كما أن وجودها كذلك ، وذلك الظهور والوجود عين الحق لا هي ، فهي معدومة أبدا . \nفإن قيل : فحينئذ لا يكون ذلك من النصوص . \nقلنا : إنما لا يكون من النصوص على تقدير أن يقال : أن الظهور إما بذاتها وإلا فهذا الكلام لا يقبل النسخ ، فافهم . \n\nقال الشيخ : [ ومتى وضح لك ما ذكرته في هذا النص ، علمت أن الظهور في الوجود ؛ لكن بشرط التعدد مع آثار الأعيان فيه ، وأن البطون صفة ذاتية للأعيان ، والوجود أيضا من حيث تعقل وحدته  “ 1  “ ، والأمر دائر بين الظهور ، وبطون غلبة ومغلوبية ، بمعنى أنه ما نقص من الظاهر ، اندرج في الباطن ، وبالعكس والنسب والإضافات صور أحوال وأحكام تنشأ بين المراتب ، فيظهر بعضها بعضا ، ويخفى بعضها بعضا بحسب الغلبية والمغلوبية المشار إليها آنفا ، فافهم ] . \n\nوصلّ اللهم على سيدنا محمد وآله وصحبه وسلّم ، أي : وما ظهر لك ما ذكرته من أن الظهور لآثار الأعيان في الوجود ، علمت أن الظهور للوجود ، إذ لا أثر للأعيان من حيث هي ؛ لأنها معدومة ، بل من حيث تعلق الوجود بها فالآثار في الحقيقة آثار الوجود بشرط الأعيان ، فإذا ظهرت آثار الوجود بشرط . \nآخره والحمد لله رب العالمين \n\n* * *",

    {
      "page": 150,
      "entry_id": "MSH-P150",
      "old_english": "**[Continuation of al-Mahāʾimī from p. 149]**: These reflected forms are subordinate, in their order, to the original form that is known in itself.\n\n**Qūnawī:** Thus there arises a fresh knowledge of the kinds of manifestation and the rulings necessarily accompanying them. These rulings comprise the effects of things upon one another, whether through establishing or undoing, outwardly or inwardly, in higher or lower realms, within a determinate duration or without such duration, and in concordance or in discordance. All of this occurs through the connection brought about among them by the existential, immediately experienced self-disclosure, which gathers their dispersed elements together, as we explained.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** When the many determinate things make the One appear manifold in the kinds of manifestation proper to their various receptive capacities, the forms in which the One appears also differ. Accordingly, knowledge of those kinds of manifestation is said to be renewed, meaning that it follows knowledge of unity by an order of nature, not by a temporal succession. The manifested reality and the locus in which it is manifested are united with respect to existence; the manifest form is, in truth, that very reality, while its otherness concerns its status as an image. Therefore knowledge of the image follows knowledge of essential unity in rank.\n\nThese manifestations have determinate consequences. Something may affect another by bringing something about, as rain causes a crop to grow, or by undoing it, as fire burns wood. Such relations may be outward, as in those physical examples, or inward, as when two affirmative premises yield an affirmative conclusion and premises including a negative yield a negative conclusion. They may belong to higher orders, as with the influence of intellects upon souls and what lies below them, or to lower orders, as with the generation and corruption of elements acting upon one another. They may be time-bound, as in effects of intellects upon elements or elements upon one another, or not time-bound, as in the influence of intellects upon souls. They may be concordant, as good actions conduce to felicity, or discordant, as corrupt actions bring misery and punishment.\n\nAll these are diverse knowledges and are said to be renewed only in the sense that their order depends on the judgment of unity and the connection among the things themselves. Even when the things are contrary to one another, they are joined by the one existential disclosure common to them all, within eternal knowledge. What changes is the relational determination between that knowledge and the things, in view of the contrarieties belonging to them. Understand this carefully.",
      "new_english": "**[Continuation of al-Mahāʾimī from p. 149]**: These reflected forms are subordinate, in their order, to the original form that is known in itself.\n\n**Qūnawī:** Thus there arises a fresh knowledge of the kinds of manifestation and the rulings necessarily accompanying them. These rulings comprise the effects of things upon one another, whether through establishing or undoing, outwardly or inwardly, in higher or lower realms, within a determinate duration or without such duration, and in concordance or in discordance. All of this occurs through the connection brought about among them by the existential, immediately experienced self-disclosure, which gathers their dispersed elements together, as we explained.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** When the many determinate things make the One appear manifold in the kinds of manifestation proper to their various receptive capacities, the forms in which the One appears also differ. Accordingly, knowledge of those kinds of manifestation is said to be renewed, meaning that it follows knowledge of unity by an order of nature, not by a temporal succession. The manifest is united with the manifester in respect of existence. The manifest is an image of the manifester—al-Mahāʾimī expressly identifies “manifester” here as an active participle—and in reality it is identical with it; its otherness consists in being its image. Therefore knowledge of the image follows knowledge of essential unity in rank.\n\nThese manifestations have determinate consequences. Something may affect another by bringing something about, as rain causes a crop to grow, or by undoing it, as fire burns wood. Such relations may be outward, as in those physical examples, or inward, as when two affirmative premises yield an affirmative conclusion and premises including a negative yield a negative conclusion. They may belong to higher orders, as with the influence of intellects upon souls and what lies below them, or to lower orders, as with the generation and corruption of elements acting upon one another. They may be time-bound, as in effects of intellects upon elements or elements upon one another, or not time-bound, as in the influence of intellects upon souls. They may be concordant, as good actions conduce to felicity, or discordant, as corrupt actions bring misery and punishment.\n\nAll these are diverse knowledges and are said to be renewed only in the sense that their order depends on the judgment of unity and the connection among the things themselves. Even when the things are contrary to one another, they are joined by the one existential disclosure common to them all, within eternal knowledge. What changes is the relational determination between that knowledge and the things, in view of the contrarieties belonging to them. Understand this carefully.\n\n**Qūnawī:** Knowledge, delight and felicity, in all their different varieties, follow correspondence or affinity (*munāsaba*); ignorance, torment and wretchedness follow the strength of the rulings of separation and distinction. As for the intermingling of the rulings of union and those of distinction, its sway is perpetual. The source of each group of these rulings, through some kind of correspondence, and that to which it returns in respect of relation ... [continued on p. 151].",
      "reasons": [
        "Corrected المظهر اسم الفاعل: the manifester, not a locus of manifestation.",
        "Restored the Qūnawī lemma physically beginning at the foot of p.150; its continuation is on p.151.",
        "Rendered أبدي السلطنة as perpetual sway, replacing the inherited paraphrase about relative dominance."
      ],
      "source_printed_page": 150
    },
    {
      "page": 151,
      "entry_id": "MSH-P151",
      "old_english": "**Qūnawī:** Knowledge, delight and felicity, in all their different varieties, are in proportion to *munāsaba*—correspondence or affinity—while ignorance, pain and wretchedness are in proportion to the strength of the rulings of separation and distinction. Where the rulings of union are mingled with those of distinction, their relative dominance is displayed. The origin of each cluster of these rulings in a particular kind of affinity, and the point to which it returns as a relation, is what is called a *martaba*, a rank or level. Understand.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** If the highest degree of knowledge of a thing is union with the known, then knowledge of all degrees, together with the enjoyment and felicity corresponding to it, follows the degree of correspondence between knower and known, between the one enjoying and what is enjoyed, and between the felicitous person and what confers felicity. Gnosis, faith, virtuous character and good deeds bring about this correspondence. Conversely, ignorance, torment and misery occur according to the strength of the differences separating the ignorant person from what is unknown, the sufferer from what causes suffering, and the wretched person from what makes him wretched. One must therefore avoid unbelief, vicious dispositions and disobedience, lest these rulings of separation and difference predominate.\n\nSeparation has these effects because it opposes correspondence and therefore yields contrary effects. Where it is weak, it cannot overcome the original correspondence arising from the participation of all things in existence. But where the rulings of union—associated with the attributes of necessity—and those of separation—associated with the attributes of possibility—are mixed in approximately equal strength, each exercises its sway for as long as the mixture lasts. A person in whom both are present may be knowing, happy and enjoying under one aspect but not under another. Thus the people of the Paradise of Acts are felicitous insofar as they are delivered from the Fire, yet deficient in felicity relative to the people of the Paradises of the Attributes and of the Essence.\n\nSomeone who first enters the Fire and later Paradise is, on this account, governed at first by separation and afterwards by union. The power of faith belongs to the person's inward spirit, while the power of bad acts attaches to outward behaviour. What attaches to the outward can pass away, unlike what is rooted in the inward. It is also possible to state the governing principle more simply: ignorance, torment and misery arise only where separation and distinction become strong, for when weak they cannot defeat the original affinity of existence.\n\nNor should one imagine that union abolishes all distinction. Both determinations persist after manifestation: under the consideration of necessity there is the One, necessary Reality, present throughout; under the consideration of determinations and possible attributes there are always creatures. The origin of each cluster of the rulings of union and of distinction, through a particular affinity with real unity, is what is designated a rank (*martaba*).",
      "new_english": "**Qūnawī (continuing):** ...and its support is what is called a rank (*martaba*). Understand.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** If the highest degree of knowledge of a thing is union with the known, then knowledge of all degrees, together with the enjoyment and felicity corresponding to it, follows the degree of correspondence between knower and known, between the one enjoying and what is enjoyed, and between the felicitous person and what confers felicity. Gnosis, faith, virtuous character and good deeds bring about this correspondence. Conversely, ignorance, torment and misery occur according to the strength of the differences separating the ignorant person from what is unknown, the sufferer from what causes suffering, and the wretched person from what makes him wretched. One must therefore avoid unbelief, vicious dispositions and disobedience, lest these rulings of separation and difference predominate.\n\nSeparation has these effects because it opposes correspondence and therefore yields contrary effects. Where it is weak, it cannot overcome the original correspondence arising from the participation of all things in existence. But where the rulings of union—associated with the attributes of necessity—and those of separation—associated with the attributes of possibility—are mixed in approximately equal strength, each exercises its sway for as long as the mixture lasts. A person in whom both are present may be knowing, happy and enjoying under one aspect but not under another. Thus the people of the Paradise of Acts are felicitous insofar as they are delivered from the Fire, yet deficient in felicity relative to the people of the Paradises of the Attributes and of the Essence.\n\nSomeone who first enters the Fire and later Paradise is, on this account, governed at first by separation and afterwards by union. The power of faith belongs to the person's inward spirit, while the power of bad acts attaches to outward behaviour. What attaches to the outward can pass away, unlike what is rooted in the inward. It is also possible to state the governing principle more simply: ignorance, torment and misery arise only where separation and distinction become strong, for when weak they cannot defeat the original affinity of existence.\n\nNor should one imagine that union abolishes all distinction. Both determinations persist after manifestation: under the consideration of necessity there is the One, necessary Reality, present throughout; under the consideration of determinations and possible attributes there are always creatures. The origin of each cluster of the rulings of union and of distinction, through a particular affinity with real unity, is what is designated a rank (*martaba*).\n\nTherefore the Real, glorified and exalted, knows these things with complete knowledge. That correspondence has an effect upon them from His side because it is original in Him, whereas ... [continued on p. 152].",

    {
      "page": 152,
      "entry_id": "MSH-P152",
      "old_english": "**[Continuation of al-Mahāʾimī]**: God therefore knows all such things perfectly, and correspondence has an effect on them from His side, for in Him it is primordial. Their correspondence, however, does not make them attain that same knowledge, because it is derivative and weaker. Affinity may be common to two terms, but its power differs according to the rank of each. What the relationship between God and creation, or creation and God, ultimately refers to is precisely this rank. Its operation at the level of God, whose unity is original, is incomparably greater than at the level of creatures, whose unity is derivative through existence. Without this distinction, the two knowledges would be equal merely because both parties share a correspondence. Understand.\n\n**Qūnawī:** When I began composing this text, I was told inwardly, in the course of writing, that the rulings attributed to unity and to the one Real, expressed as the rulings of necessity, have, as viewed from unity, a single foundational ruling: the reality of *qaḍāʾ* (decree). The *maqādīr* (measures) are the effect of the manifold determinations of the objects of knowledge relative to that single ruling. The appearance of existence in accordance with those differentiations involves first a reception of influence and then an exercise of influence among the enumerated things, by restoring to them the effects proper to them. Know this, consider the strange matter to which I have drawn attention, and you will attain a rare knowledge. God is the guide.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** This expands the explanation of the perfection of divine knowledge in both its undifferentiated and detailed aspects. The former is called decree; the latter, measure or determination, without excluding either from the comprehensiveness of the divine Essence. The rulings attributed to unity—namely the first determination—and to the One Real—namely the second determination or degree of divinity—are called rulings of necessity. But their ultimate origin, when viewed from unity, is one ruling: the reality of decree, or the divine knowledge of His Essence in His Essence. In the degree of the first determination, these rulings are not actually multiple, so union with the objects of knowledge is most intense there. This is why one is obliged to accept the decree with contentment.\n\nAs for the measured determinations, their meaning is that each object of knowledge occurs in its apportioned measure of time, place and accompanying accidents. These measures result from the differentiations of the objects of knowledge originally embraced potentially by unity under the one ruling, insofar as that ruling relates to the objects after relating to the Essence that comprehends them. The result is that each object seeks what its own nature can receive, either immediately or through another. Union at this level is less intense than at the first, and this is the detailed knowledge that constitutes the domain of measure (*qadar*).\n\nFinally, the existence of the One Real appears, according to His names and the differences among those objects of knowledge, first with efficacy in the higher ranks of the intellects and souls, and again in the levels beneath them.",

      "old_english": "[Editorial heading: The dispositions of the fixed entities and the meaning of qadar]\n\n**[Continuation of al-Mahāʾimī]**: Those lower levels are bodies and corporeal things. Their existence appears through the return to the enumerated things of the determinate effects already proper to them in the state in which their fixed entities subsisted. Eternal knowledge of these things is thereby complete also in this respect: in their manifested state they do not differ from what they are in the sphere of measure. Under one consideration they are united with the single existence; even when their particular effects are considered, those effects belong to the objects of knowledge themselves, for they are restored to them rather than independently arising from every standpoint.\n\nQūnawī's injunction to 'know this' means that it is a subtle knowledge rarely found in books, disclosing the meaning of decree and predestination in a way not previously explained. God guides one to the verification of such sciences, which discursive thoughts cannot attain and ordinary sight does not perceive.\n\n[Editorial heading: Opening of Text Thirteen: the limit of knowledge of created things]\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī (introducing the next text):** This noble text explains the remaining secrets of the subject. It states the furthest attainable degree of knowledge of things other than God, and the degree of union possible with them. The utmost such union occurs in the mirror of eternal divine knowledge. Things are intrinsically different from one another; God cannot be known as He is in Himself, because what has no being of its own cannot become united with existence as such. He is unknowable from the aspect of unqualified absoluteness, for the conditioned qua conditioned cannot be united with the absolute qua absolute. Moreover, His determinations are without end, just as human states are without end. One therefore knows Him in relation to the correspondence between such states and His determinations, which are His names; knowledge of His names and intrinsic modalities is thereby conditioned. Within these limits one comes to know His decree and measure.\n\n**Qūnawī:** Know that the highest degree of knowledge of any thing whatsoever, **except the Real**, consists in knowing it through a knowledge arising from a complete vision of it in God's knowledge. This knowledge has two signs. The first is that what you have learned frees you from having to examine it again and again in the hope of increasing your understanding. For an increase in knowledge after a prior claim to know the thing indicates that the first knowledge was deficient. Had it been perfect from the outset, further acquisition would be unnecessary, as is the case with God's knowledge. Such completeness depends upon comprehensive intellectual knowledge of the known.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī (page breaks at this point):** The highest degree of knowledge available to created knowers, whether human beings or angels, concerns a thing other than the Real, whether immediately evident or reached by reasoning.       "page": 154,
      "entry_id": "MSH-P154",
      "old_english": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing from p. 153):** ...your heart, with all of its receptive powers, so that the thing is disclosed fully, without its being lost to awareness by reason of annihilation (*fanāʾ*). This differs from grasping a thing through discursive definitions, which, before complete purification, are usually accompanied by mistaken imagination and corrupt fancies. That is why one sees even accomplished rational investigators disagreeing about definitions despite their exertions.\n\nThe first of the two signs that this knowledge has been attained is that the certainty acquired by tasted experience (*dhawq*), with the purity of the heart and the keenness of the soul, makes further repeated inquiry unnecessary. Such repetition might otherwise occur through reason or unveiling, even if the original discovery had been achieved by inquiry after purification and the cultivation of these capacities. The repetition cannot be needed simply to impress the knowledge upon the heart, since it is already firmly established there, and the concomitant properties of the known can be deduced from it.\n\nAn attempt to increase one's knowledge after claiming already to possess complete knowledge is possible only where the first knowledge was deficient. Were the first knowledge exhaustive in every respect, an increase would seek an aspect already possessed. This would be the impossible acquisition of what is already acquired. Since divine knowledge is perfect in every respect, its supposed increase is impossible. One may, however, speak of an articulated determination of what is already known wholly in itself, so that it comes to be referred to in detail. The kind of knowledge which renders further inquiry unnecessary depends on encompassing everything about the known; since a conditioned knower cannot encompass the unconditioned Real, this cannot occur in any creature's knowledge of God.\n\n**Qūnawī:** The second sign indicating that this knowledge has been acquired and is sound is that the reach of one's knowledge extends throughout the thing and goes beyond its restriction, until one sees its furthest limit as connected to the absoluteness of the Real.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The second sign confirms both the acquisition of knowledge through wholly seeing the thing in God's knowledge and its validity. Unlike the first sign, which merely shows that the thing is known, this also permits knowledge of why it is so. Qūnawī says it is a sign *from which one draws an inference*: there is an evidential path here analogous to rational demonstration. It is that knowledge extends to all the thing's parts, accidental features and different respects; then it passes beyond it to what is above it, in the form of more fundamental characteristics and accidents; and in turn to what is above those, repeatedly, until the utmost horizon of the thing comes into sight ... [the argument continues on p. 155].",

      "page": 155,
      "entry_id": "MSH-P155",
      "old_english": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continued):** ...and the conceptions of everything above it, until its furthest conceivable boundary is seen as connected with the Real's absoluteness, beyond which there is nothing. Only then is the thing known with complete knowledge. This requires seeing the thing within God's knowledge, which comprehends the beginning, the end and every intermediate connection, without limit.\n\nThe first sign has already implied that one cannot possess such complete knowledge of God, because His determinations are without end and the finite cannot encompass that which has no limit. The first passage therefore left the point implicit; here it is stated expressly.\n\n**Qūnawī:** Knowledge of the Real is not of this sort. It attaches to Him only insofar as He becomes determined within a degree, a locus of manifestation, a state, an aspect, or a consideration. Whenever He is delimited for the knower through a determination under one of these heads, there becomes apparent and determinate to that knower, from the absolute Essence and according to the state of the recipient of disclosure, something that was not determined for that person before.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** No human knowledge of the Real can run through Him and then transcend Him in the way just described. Such knowledge concerns Him through some definite level, such as *aḥadiyya* or *wāḥidiyya*; through a manifesting locus, such as spirits or bodies; through the states of manifestation and hiddenness; through the considerations of absoluteness and restriction; or through the consideration that none of these restricts Him, without any contradiction. Each of these is a determination, whereas real absoluteness is a negative notion. At any given moment the knower receives from the absolute Essence a new determination appropriate to the state of the recipient, distinct from what was delimited previously. But where is the unconditioned absoluteness in such apprehensions?       "new_english": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continued):** ...and the conceptions of everything above it, until its furthest conceivable boundary is seen as connected with the Real's absoluteness, beyond which there is nothing.       "entry_id": "MSH-P156",
      "old_english": "**[Continuation of the discussion of Text Thirteen]**\n\n**Qūnawī:** By contrast, the Real displays Himself through states, as the Most High says, “Every day He is upon some affair” (Qurʾān 55:29). Understand; do not interpret the matter away. Endeavour instead first to see it directly. Believe, submit, and you will be safe. God alone gives success and inspiration.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Human states do not reach a final state after which none is possible. Their change and succession is a matter of observation. Since they are determinations of the absolute Essence and varieties in the appearances of that Essence, the Real's determinations and modes of disclosure to human beings have no final limit. A determination differs from a variety of manifestation: the former is a cause of manifestation insofar as it is surrounded by the qualifying attributes that bring the manifestation about; the latter is the diversity of appearances occasioned by diverse determinations. Because human states and attributes constitute loci in which the Essence appears under the consideration of attributes, their diversity occasions diversity of manifestation, and each manifestation entails a determinate relation of correspondence. Human states thus serve as qualifying conditions for such differentiations. The divine names, under which the Real becomes determined, are names in relation to those human states, which mediate the diversity of manifestation and hence of determinations.\n\nThe Qurʾānic statement that He is engaged in an affair each day (55:29) has elsewhere been used to indicate that these affairs are inexhaustible: the days do not terminate, so neither do the affairs. Since the divine affairs stand in relation to the fixed entities and the comprehensive human being includes all of these, the states of the human being are likewise inexhaustible, as are the resulting varieties of manifestation and determinations. It is therefore impossible to encompass them. How, then, could one reach their furthest end and proceed beyond them to circumscribe what lies beyond? Understand. Do not reinterpret this statement away, for it is intended as stated; seek to witness it. Believe first and submit, rather than mistakenly claim to know what cannot be known, namely the Real through every one of His determinations. God grants this realization, which is the realization of the limits of knowing; He inspires surrender where attainment has been found impossible. God knows best.\n\n**[Opening of Text Fourteen, on the same printed page.] Al-Mahāʾimī:** Qūnawī designates the following text an exalted text. The preceding discussion established that the Real is united with all things, and therefore knows them perfectly, whereas creatures cannot be united with Him in the same fashion and so cannot know Him through all His determinations, much less in absolute freedom from determination. The present text explains the majesty that both permits and veils this union. Under unconditioned absoluteness, unity so prevails that multiplicity does not appear, even though the absolute has a relation to determination. Under qualification, by contrast, there remains a relation to absoluteness, but it does not prevail: plurality is actually manifest. An apprehension of absoluteness is possible only to the degree that unity is manifest within the qualified, and it is not a knowledge of absoluteness in the manner that the Absolute knows it.",
      "new_english": "**[Continuation of the discussion of Text Thirteen]**\n\n**Qūnawī:** By contrast, the Real turns through the states, as the Most High says, “Every day He is upon some affair” (Qurʾān 55:29).
