````json
    },
    {
      "id": "MSH-031",
      "pair_sequence": 2,
      "old_en": "**Objection:** Unrestricted existence could be immune to nonexistence only if it were the very essence of a determinate existent. But that is false: the unrestricted can be predicated of what is determinate, whereas one self-subsistent essence cannot be predicated of another. Necessary reality is therefore a special nature necessarily accompanied by unrestricted existence. **Reply:** Such a nature cannot be made intelligible. If it has instances in the mind, and one instance exists while the others are impossible, despite all being [conceptually] possible, the necessity of the former and impossibility of the latter must come from something extrinsic; for what belongs to something through itself is not eliminated by what comes from another. If the nature has no such instances and differs from unrestricted existence, it cannot itself be existent, lest it become a composite with existence. If it is a quiddity, necessary existence would subsist in it; but being other than existence, it would need what is other and would have to be the agent that brings existence about—otherwise the Necessary's existence would come from another.",
      "new_en": "**Objection:** Unrestricted existence could be immune to nonexistence only if it were the very essence of a determinate existent. But that is false: the unrestricted can be predicated of what is determinate, whereas one self-subsistent essence cannot be predicated of another. Necessary reality is therefore a special nature necessarily accompanied by unrestricted existence. **Reply:** Such a nature cannot be made intelligible. If it has instances in the mind, and one instance exists while the others are impossible, despite all being [conceptually] possible, the necessity of the former and impossibility of the latter must come from something extrinsic; for what belongs to something through itself is not eliminated by what comes from another. If the nature has no such instances and differs from unrestricted existence, it cannot itself be existent, lest it become a composite with existence. If it is a quiddity, necessary existence would subsist in it and thus depend on something other than itself. That quiddity would have to be the agent producing this existence—otherwise the Necessary’s existence would come from another.",
      "reason": "Clarifies the dependence argument: the necessary existence that subsists in a distinct quiddity would depend on another; the inherited pronouns incorrectly made the quiddity the dependent subject."
    },

    {
      "id": "MSH-032",
      "pair_sequence": 3,
      "old_en": "**Reply:** Existence, whatever differences are alleged in its manifestations, does not admit nonexistence, as already established. Were another [independent existence] actual there would be multiple Necessary Existents, something the proponent of gradation wholly rejects. Arguments for gradation from priority, precedence, greater completeness and greater nobility presuppose the alleged nature that necessarily accompanies existence; but such properties accrue to existence only in relation to quiddities—for example, through having fewer or more intermediaries. Against the posited necessarily accompanying nature we add that it differs from the notion of every determination, for determination requires a subject, which conflicts with intrinsic necessity. Such a nature would therefore have possible instances: it is a universal in the mind, and if one instance obtained while the others were impossible, this would have to be through another. If the alleged inseparability is denied because the nature is unrestricted or the restriction is merely supposed, the conclusion follows if the determination is not independent of its subject.",

Were another [independent existence] actual there would be multiple Necessary Existents, something the proponent of gradation wholly rejects.       "old_en": "**Reply:** An appeal to self-evidence is inadmissible at the very point under dispute.     {
      "id": "MSH-036",
      "pair_sequence": 1,
      "old_en": "**Third objection:** Unrestricted existence is supposed to receive opposites. It would then need preparatory conditions external to itself, for if its receptivity for them came entirely from itself, there would be an intrinsic opposition in its very reality. **Reply:** It may be disposed for one thing through itself and for another through a mediating factor without an intrinsic opposition; besides, these preparatory conditions are attributes distinct from it. **Fourth:** If necessary, it must be one, yet it is the locus of attributes; a simple reality would consequently be both recipient and agent in relation to the same item, which the philosophers reject. **Reply:** That is impossible only when the two roles are asserted under one and the same aspect. It may therefore receive through its determination and act through its reality, or conversely.       "new_en": "**Third objection:** Unrestricted existence is supposed to receive opposites.       "reason": "Restores the antecedent of هي to كثرة (plurality); the inherited comparison of things to forms was not what the supplied clause says."
    },
    {
      "id": "MSH-037",
      "pair_sequence": 1,
      "old_en": "... if the essence entails detachment, this is contradicted by possibles; if it entails no detachment, it violates the hypothesis; and if it entails neither, every cause must be extrinsic. One cannot answer that detachment is privative and therefore requires only the absence of a cause, for an absence relative to something would presuppose the absence of the cause of conjunction; that cause would differ from the Necessary, bringing back dependence upon another. **Reply:** Sharing here means that multiple attributes are related to existence and considered together with it, so that it manifests through genera, species and individuals. There is no multiplication within existence itself, and therefore no intrinsic participation of several separate realities. Moreover, the condition of the Essence's disengagement is that it is not qualified by those attributes. We may indeed say that its essence entails neither [the disputed restriction nor its negation] while its inwardness entails disengagement and its outwardness entails relation. It has no need of another because it is itself the Inward and the Outward. We deny that a privative detachment needs an absence of a cause: needing the absence of a cause would be a positive relation, not established by something wholly without actuality. Even if conceded, relative nonexistence derives from existence, not from a distinct existence that would introduce need of another; besides, the supposed dependence would belong to detachment itself, not the Essence that is disengaged.",
      "new_en": "... if the essence entails detachment, this is contradicted by possibles; if it entails no detachment, it violates the hypothesis; and if it entails neither, every cause must be extrinsic. One cannot answer that detachment is privative and therefore requires only the absence of a cause, for an absence relative to something would presuppose the absence of the cause of conjunction; that cause would differ from the Necessary, bringing back dependence upon another. **Reply:** Sharing here means that multiple attributes are related to existence and considered together with it, so that it manifests through genera, species and individuals. There is no multiplication within existence itself, and therefore no intrinsic participation of several separate realities. Moreover, [on the present construal] the cause of disengagement is the Essence, on condition that it is not qualified by those attributes. We may indeed say that its essence entails neither [the disputed restriction nor its negation] while its inwardness entails disengagement and its outwardness entails relation. It has no need of another because it is itself the Inward and the Outward. We deny that a privative detachment needs an absence of a cause: needing the absence of a cause would be a positive relation, not established by something wholly without actuality.       "reason": "Restores علة (cause) rather than replacing it with condition, while flagging the compressed syntax; clarifies فلا تغاير نفس الوجود without inventing a second source-existence."

    {
      "id": "MSH-039",
      "pair_sequence": 4,
      "old_en": "**Objection:** Discursive reasoning must assist inspiration in order to distinguish it from satanic suggestion and the soul's internal speech. Inspiration is not subject to human control, and purification requires disciplines to which temperament and tranquillity rarely conform. If the outcome of purification is not immediately necessary knowledge, then it depends upon a state whose loss entails losing some of the knowledge; in this sense it is inferential. If no such dependency is found, the result may be no more reliable than unexamined imitation, and people holding false doctrines also experience such convictions; a discriminator is indispensable. **Reply:** The discriminator is agreement with the Book, Sunna and consensus of the community. It thereby excludes the experience of those holding false doctrines.",
      "new_en": "**Objection:** Discursive reasoning must assist inspiration in order to distinguish it from satanic suggestion and the soul's internal speech. Inspiration is not subject to human control, and purification requires struggles to which the bodily constitution rarely proves equal. Assurance is attained only through discursive reasoning. If the outcome of purification is not immediately necessary knowledge, then it depends upon a state whose loss entails losing some of the knowledge; in this sense it is inferential. If no such dependency is found, the result may be no more reliable than unexamined imitation, and people holding false doctrines also experience such convictions; a discriminator is indispensable. **Reply:** The discriminator is agreement with the Book, Sunna and consensus of the community. It thereby excludes the experience of those holding false doctrines.",
      "reason": "The inherited English incorrectly joined والطمأنينة to the constitution as what rarely supports disciplines. Restores الطمأنينة إنما هي بالنظر as the objector’s separate epistemic claim."

      "id": "MSH-041",
      "pair_sequence": 3,
      "old_en": "When one turns toward action the passing impulse to act is called intention (*qaṣd*), and the commencement of action is striving (*saʿy*).       "id": "MSH-043",

      "old_en": "In the technical definitions it is said: the *knowledge of certainty* (*ʿilm al-yaqīn*) is what demonstration yields; its *eye* (*ʿayn al-yaqīn*) is what witnessing yields; its *reality* (*ḥaqq al-yaqīn*) is what is obtained from knowing the reality made visible through that witnessing.       "old_en": "The author of the *Manāzil* says: knowledge of certainty consists in accepting what has become manifest of the Real, accepting what is unseen on the Real's authority, and standing by what is upheld through the Real.     {
      "id": "MSH-043",
      "pair_sequence": 4,
      "old_en": "Another says: knowledge of certainty is the state of gnosis; the eye of certainty is the state of gathering (*jamʿ*); and the reality of certainty is the gathering of gathering expressed in the language of unity. The first definition is closest to the present discussion. Knowledge received merely from outward scholars, by contrast, is imitation rather than direct knowledge.",

      "id": "MSH-047",
````

````json
      "new_en": "He then indicates that this is the first determination: ‘This intellection’—that is, self-intellection—‘and determinate apprehension, although it immediately follows the indicated unrestrictedness’, meaning unrestrictedness in the negative sense, would properly be qualified by unrestrictedness in ordinary usage and would thus not be a determination [in that respect]. Yet it combines both: determination in relation to what precedes it, and unrestrictedness in relation to what lies beneath it. Relative to the Real's determination in the intellection of every conceiver, whether the Real or creation, in every self-disclosure, in a locus of manifestation or otherwise, it is an unrestricted determination. In combining both it gathers the determinations [the connective wording here is uncertain], and it is that to which knowledge of Him relates. Hence it is the essential self-disclosure that falls upon the Muhammadan Reality directly, and upon others through an intermediary. It cannot disclose itself in loci of manifestation: if it shines upon them, it burns them up. It appears only to His Essence in His Essence; none sees Him thus except one who has been effaced in Him and subsists through Him. To it belongs the highest station of unification, essential unification above that of attributes and intellect. Unification cannot be considered in what lies above it, since the attribution of unity has no priority there at all. Understand.",
      "reason": "Restores omitted ordinary/negative unrestrictedness distinction, the two relative aspects and full disclosure logic; replaces interpretive softening with the actual burn-up image and flags uncertain connective."
    },
    {
      "id": "MSH-P103",

      "old_en": "**Text Eight. Qūnawī:** “A noble, universal text containing sublime mysteries.” The previous text established the Real as the end of any felicitous traveller.       "new_en": "**Text Eight. Qūnawī:** ‘A noble, universal text containing clear mysteries.’ **Al-Mahāʾimī:** Having stated in the preceding text that the traveller who receives some felicity from the Real must have the Real as his final end, he now explains the cause of that felicity and its details. The mysteries discussed here are the kinds of self-disclosure in loci of manifestation, the human being as the complete locus calling for these kinds of disclosure, what follows from each self-disclosure, and that temporally originated things are not other than the Real, since He has not exerted an effect upon their realities or upon ...",
      "reason": "Restores جلية as clear, and the actual causal claim لم يؤثر rather than adding ‘not simply an other opposed to’ or suppressing agency."

    {
      "id": "MSH-P125",
      "pair_sequence": 1,
      "old_en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continued):** Qūnawī speaks of a hidden secret in the degrees of reckoning because an apparently nominal relation may ultimately return to a more essential one. Al-Mahāʾimī argues that since names return to the Essence, even a severe reckoning under some names is not independent of mercy, though it may appear in a form of chastisement. A consequence can be fitting in a rational sense and manifest a perfection of wisdom while being painful to the recipient's natural disposition. He further conjectures that in the next world reason may come to predominate over bodily inclination; since the disclosures experienced by those undergoing punishment must be nominally determined, he proposes that punishment will in one respect come to an end. He attributes a corresponding doctrine to Ibn ʿArabī. This is a substantive theological claim of the commentator and should be indexed separately from Qūnawī's quoted formulation, not generalized without qualification to every Akbarian school.\n\nHe construes the phrase “if its outcome is a stronger relationship to the Presence of the Essence” as the necessary conclusion of a correctly formed argument, unlike relations under particular names, which can shift. Qūnawī uses restrictive language to assign freedom from reckoning to gifts with an effectively essential predominance, so as not to imply that every gift outside the first-mentioned class must be reckoned.\n\nThe reason given for absence of reckoning is essential proportionality between agent and recipient: an essential correspondence, unlike a contingent nominal condition, does not cease. Al-Mahāʾimī locates its governing character in mercy, arguing that the relation of mercy to the Essence is prior to that of wrath. A residual name-based aspect in a mixed gift may tempt one to expect reckoning, but a merely subordinate aspect does not override its governing essential correspondence.\n\n**Qūnawī:** “Whoever does not know this foundation does not understand the reality of the saying, ‘God provides for whom He wills without reckoning’ (Q 2:212), nor the secret of ‘This is Our gift; bestow it or withhold it without reckoning’ (Q 38:39), and similar passages repeated in the Mighty Book and in prophetic reports, such as the saying that seventy thousand of his community will enter Paradise without reckoning ...”",
      "new_en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continued):** ... reckoning while others do not. He emphasizes this because he is certain of it, and speaks of a great secret that cannot be divulged. Its explanation is that the names return to the Essence. Thus reckoning, even when difficult under some names, returns to that in which there is no reckoning: mercy, even if it takes the form of punishment. Since punishment is His judgment, it bears a rational appropriateness to their acts, and it contains a perfection of wisdom in which one takes pleasure as regards intellect, although one suffers as regards nature.\n\nPerhaps in the next world intellect will predominate in them over nature. Moreover, the disclosures to those undergoing punishment must be disclosures of the names; their punishment must therefore come to an end in some respect, namely the one we have described. Shaykh Muḥyī al-Dīn explicitly stated this. This relation has already been discussed because of its frequent occurrence in reality. If the outcome—that is, the effect of the prevailing and subordinated aspects—is a strong relation of those gifts to the Presence of the Essence, the expression used indicates that this outcome necessarily follows, just as the conclusion follows from a sound syllogism. This differs from relation to the names, which is not necessary, since it may change.\n\n‘That, then, is what [has no reckoning]’ uses a restrictive construction to indicate that, of these two classes, absence of reckoning belongs exclusively to this one. Had this restrictive formula been used of the essential gifts [mentioned first], it would have suggested that reckoning is necessary for everything else, including this class.\n\nHe then gives the reason for absence of reckoning in both places: ‘Because essential gifts’—those mentioned first—and what has a stronger relation to them, this last class, issue from the agent and are received by the recipient only through an essential correspondence in both. What belongs essentially never ceases or comes to a halt. This pertains specifically to mercy, since mercy's relation to the Essence precedes wrath's relation. Because the aspect of the names is evident in the last class, one might suppose that it is without reckoning from the side of the Essence but subject to reckoning from the side of the names. He rejects this: nothing necessitates the gifts except that correspondence; the subordinated aspect has no effect. Understand.\n\n**Qūnawī:** ‘Whoever does not know this foundation does not know the reality of God's saying, “God provides for whom He wills without reckoning” [Q 2:212], nor the secret of His saying, “This is Our gift; bestow it or withhold it without reckoning” [Q 38:39], and similar passages repeatedly mentioned in the Mighty Book, and also in prophetic reports, such as the saying that seventy thousand of his community will enter Paradise without reckoning ...’",
      "reason": "Restores continuous translation rather than summary; removes translator directives from running prose; preserves the strength and qualifications of the commentator's punishment argument and the restrictive-construction reasoning."
    },
    {
      "id": "MSH-P126",
      "pair_sequence": 1,
      "old_en": "**Qūnawī (concluding his report):** “... and with every thousand another seventy thousand.” These, he says, possess nominal gifts whose relationship to the Presence of the Essence is stronger than their relationship to the Presence of particular names and attributes; for that reason they follow those who possess essential correspondence and share in their states. Know this.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The foundation teaches that gifts essentially related to the divine Reality, and those in which that relation prevails, are without reckoning. Without it one cannot understand the explanatory ground of Q 2:212, “God provides whom He wills without reckoning.” Though the verse mentions divine willing and the comprehensive name “God,” which embrace named determinations, the essential aspect may predominate within the relevant bestowal. The comprehensive name includes Essence and attributes without lowering the Essence to the level of a particular name. Likewise divine will, here understood as distinct from restricted volition, has a more encompassing relation.\n\nThe expression “without reckoning” is taken to embrace the occurrence and timing of provision. The deeper mystery of Q 38:39, “This is Our gift: bestow it or retain it without reckoning,” refers to an essential gift not governed by a calculable rule of obligation or recompense—even the teaching or guidance through which realized people return from the Real to creatures can be transmitted or withheld without a corresponding numerical account.\n\nQūnawī uses the word “reality” for the first scriptural passage because its basis is accessible through names outwardly known, but “secret” for the second because it concerns the Essence, the deepest unseen mystery. The prophetic narration is then used to exemplify two groups entering Paradise without reckoning: the original seventy thousand, who are described as leaders with essential gifts, and the accompanying multitudes, whose gifts involve names but incline strongly toward the essential Presence. This is an interpretation of the report, not a hadith-critical authentication.\n\n[The modern footnotes on this page cite al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah and Aḥmad; they are excluded from the author's Arabic text and may serve as leads for an independent hadith check.]",
      "new_en": "**Qūnawī (continued):** ‘... and with every thousand, seventy thousand.’ These possess gifts of the names, but their relation to the Presence of the Essence is stronger than their relation to the Presence of the names and attributes. For this reason they follow those who possess essential correspondence and share in their states. Know this.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Whoever does not know that essential gifts, and those whose relation to the Essence predominates, have no reckoning does not know the reality of ‘God provides for whom He wills without reckoning’ [Q 2:212]—that is, the cause explaining it by a demonstration of the reason why. This is a gift of the names in which the relation to the Essence predominates, as shown by the fact that ‘God’ is a name encompassing the Essence and attributes, while the Essence is exalted within it. He is high in His nearness and near in His height. Likewise, mashīʾa is above irāda, so it too has a relation to the Essence. ‘Without reckoning’ means in occurrence and timing.\n\nNor does such a person know the secret of ‘This is Our gift’ [Q 38:39]: an essential gift that entails neither obligation nor recompense, even from the aspect of guidance for which the perfected are returned from the Real to creation. Bestow it by teaching whomever you wish, or withhold it, for it is ‘without reckoning’; that is why this phrase is placed last.\n\nHe first says ‘reality’, indicating something established in hearts because it concerns the manifest names; he then says ‘secret’, indicating that it concerns the Essence, which is the greatest of the unseen mysteries. He adds that the prophetic reports likewise state that these two classes of gifts are without reckoning: those related to the Essence alone, and those whose relation to the Essence predominates. The first class is the seventy thousand; the report indicates this by making them those who are followed.\n\nThe second class is those indicated by ‘with every thousand, seventy thousand’. These possess gifts of the names, but their relation to the Presence of the Essence is stronger because the aspect of necessity predominates.",
      "reason": "Restores omitted statements about nearness/height, mashīʾa above irāda, the placement of ‘without reckoning’, and predominance of necessity; removes invented qualifications and modern hadith notes from running translation."
    },
    {
      "id": "MSH-P127",
      "pair_sequence": 2,
      "old_en": "**Qūnawī:** “Having described the classes of gifts and their governing rules, let us describe the kinds of recipients. Those who receive fall into differing ranks according to the requests that their preparedness, actual state, rank, spiritual constitution, natural temperament, or adventitious natural conditions express—the latter finding expression through the speech of the requesting recipient.”",
      "new_en": "**Qūnawī:** ‘Having described the classes of gifts and their governing rules, let us describe the classes of their recipients. In receiving them they fall into levels, differentiated according to their requests of preparedness, state, rank, spirituality, natural temperament, or adventitious nature, which are expressed by the tongue of the seeking recipient.’ **Al-Mahāʾimī:** Having finished with the classes of gifts—essential gifts, gifts of the names, and those related to both—and what follows from them, he describes the classes of their recipients. Their reception differs in degree, so the gifts are also divided according to their classes. He explains that their levels multiply according to their requests.",
      "reason": "Restores the commentary actually present in this Arabic pair, previously displaced into the next English pair; preserves the list without collapsing preparedness into spoken petition."
    },
    {
      "id": "MSH-P127",
      "pair_sequence": 3,
      "old_en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Having divided gifts into essential, nominal and jointly related types, Qūnawī now divides recipients according to the different ways in which reception is possible. The word “request” (*suʾāl*) here is broader than a spoken petition. The first form includes a readiness or receptive condition arising through the Most Holy Effusion (*fayḍ aqdas*) at the level of divine affairs; a second concerns requests connected with the fixed entities; a third pertains to a rank of manifestation generally, under the ordered stages of descent. A fourth comprises requests specific to particular levels, such as the spiritual—spirit, heart and soul—natural temperaments resulting from bodily elemental constitution, and contingent bodily impulses and acquired conditions.",
      "new_en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The first class is requests of state; the receptive state [the wording here is uncertain] is preparedness, the receptivity bestowed by the Most Holy Effusion upon the divine affair. The second is requests described as ‘purified from the fixed entities’ [المقدسة عن الأعيان الثابتة: the construction is uncertain]. The third is requests of rank, encompassing every rank among the ranks of descent. The fourth is requests specific to certain ranks: spiritual requests, related to the spirit and what corresponds to it, such as heart and soul; requests of natural temperament, related to the body insofar as it is composed of the elements; and requests of adventitious nature, which arise according to impulses originating in the bodily faculties.",
      "reason": "Restores the source's numbered classes and identifies rather than silently smoothing the unstable first and second clauses; removes explanation carried over from previous pair."
    },

Effective petition also requires correspondence between the recipient's actual receptivity and what is requested: asking for what the relevant order excludes—for example prophetic commissioning in the present age—will not produce its fulfillment. The preceding, more fundamental “requests” do not require verbal articulation ...",
      "new_en": "These requests arising from nature are what he says are expressed—that is, through words indicating them once they have settled in the heart—by the tongue of the seeking recipient. This suggests that a supplicant is answered only when he seeks from God with complete knowledge and fully compliant receptivity. Requesting the impossible does not secure an answer, as with requesting prophethood in this age. The preceding requests, however, are not things voiced in words ...",

    {
      "id": "MSH-P128",
      "pair_sequence": 1,
      "old_en": "[Completion of the prior page:] The more primordial receptive requests do not ordinarily find expression in words. Understand.\n\n**Qūnawī:** “In summary, the highest rank of recipients in receiving the Real's influx and gifts is to perceive the face of the Real within the conditions and causes called intermediaries and throughout the ordered series. Such a recipient knows whence he takes, and witnesses that the causal intermediaries are nothing other than determinations of the Real at divine and cosmic levels, diverse as their kinds may be. That is to say, between the received divine effusion and the recipient there is nothing but the effusion itself becoming determined through restricted receptivity, without any additional ruling of contingency being attached to it through its passage across the successive intermediary ranks or becoming coloured by their contingent judgements.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Every category of recipients admits further degrees. At their highest, those who receive through preparedness, a spiritual state or some other request behold the divine aspect in both the one original effusion and the particular gifts in which it becomes articulated. They thus recognize the face of the Real both in causes and in conditions.\n\nA *condition* (*sharṭ*) is something upon which an occurrence depends but which does not by that fact produce it; a *cause* (*sabab*) is something on which it depends with a causally effective relation. The distinction is not erased by saying that both function as mediating links (*wasāʾiṭ*) between the first effusion and its recipient. The ordered series concerns beings that emerge through their respective levels, from the divine ranks onward to the human ...",
      "new_en": "... at all. Understand.\n\n**Qūnawī:** ‘In summary, the highest rank of recipients in receiving what comes to them from the Real's effusion and gifts is to see the face of the Real in the conditions and causes called intermediaries, and in the chain of ordered sequence. The recipient thus knows and witnesses that the causal intermediaries are nothing other than determinations of the Real in the divine and cosmic ranks, with all their different kinds. This means that between the received effusion of the Real and the recipient there is only the effusion's own determination through qualified receptivity, without the addition of a contingent ruling required and necessitated by the effect of the effusion's passage through the intermediary ranks and its being coloured by the rulings of their contingencies.’\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** In every class of recipients distinguished by the requests already mentioned there is a further gradation. The highest rank of recipients—whether they receive through a request of preparedness, state or otherwise—is qualified by ‘in their receiving’ [the following explanation of this qualification is unclear in the supplied text]. He uses the singular for the Real's effusion because it is originally one, and also mentions His gifts, which articulate that effusion. He mentions both to indicate that their vision of His face follows one and the same course in undifferentiated and differentiated reception: they see the face of the Real in conditions and causes.\n\nA condition is that upon which something depends without its exercising an effect on it; a cause is that upon which it depends together with an effect. Mentioning both indicates seeing His face in what exercises an effect and what does not. They are called ‘intermediaries’ because they intervene between the first effusion and the recipient, and ‘the chain of ordered sequence’, that is, the order of the beings proceeding by effusion from divinity to ...",
      "reason": "Restores absolute negation in page continuation, the recipient as subject of knows/witnesses, singular/plural reasoning and causal definitions; removes extra interpretive assertions and flags unstable source syntax."
    },
    {
      "id": "MSH-P129",
      "pair_sequence": 1,
      "old_en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī (continuing):** The ordered chain extends as far as the human level. Qūnawī names both conditions and causes to show that mediating terms are not confined to conditions. A proximate cause is itself a mediator between the ultimately effective principle and the recipient, and a remote cause still more obviously so. The series of causal influence differs from the broader series of ordered beings: conditions are not necessarily constituents of the former though they are included in the latter.\n\nThe highest recipient sees the face of the Real in all these links. The one who possesses theoretical knowledge understands how reception occurs; one who possesses direct witnessing sees it immediately. In this account the mediators are not separate self-subsistent agents over against the Real, but His determinations at the levels of names and attributes, and at cosmic levels such as fire in burning or water in drowning. The manifest disparity and apparent lowliness of some worldly causes do not imply that such forms fall outside the doctrine of determination, nor that all determinations must have equal rank or perfection. Their differences belong to relational and perspectival orderings (*nisab wa-iʿtibārāt*), not to a newly acquired plurality in the unrestricted Essence.\n\nTwo propositions are required to clarify this. The first is that nothing independently other than the first intelligible (*maʿnawī*) effusion intervenes between that effusion and a sensory recipient; rather, the effusion itself becomes determined by the receptivity appropriate to an ordered divine or cosmic rank. The qualification “intelligible” is deliberate: an observer confined to sensory causation may suppose the successive mediators to be alien realities added between the first effusion and the tangible recipient. But the claim is not about a merely sensory stream of physical effects.\n\nNo separate contingency-property is superadded to the effusion merely as a result of passage through the intermediary ranks or through its being described as “coloured” by their possibility. Qūnawī mentions both that something *requires* and that it *necessitates* a result, so that voluntary and necessary accounts of operation are both covered. Al-Mahāʾimī insists that a governing determination actually belongs to its appropriate locus; the contingent rulings of intermediary things reside in those intermediaries and cannot be transferred wholesale as if the same accident inhered in two distinct subjects. His final premise uses the scholastic maxim that one and the same accident does not inhere in two subjects.",
      "new_en": "... humanity.\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** He mentions these two designations to indicate that both encompass causes and conditions. Intermediaries are not restricted to conditions: a proximate cause mediates between the true agent and the recipient, all the more a remote cause. Nor is the chain of ordered sequence restricted to causes: although conditions do not enter the chain of agents, they enter the chain of ordered beings. Thus one sees the face of the Real in all of them. The recipient knows this if he belongs to the people of knowledge, and witnesses it if he belongs to the people of direct vision.\n\nHe mentions causal intermediaries particularly because, if these effective things are identical with the Real despite their apparent independence and do not subsist through their own essence, non-effective things have still less claim to independence [the intervening wording is unstable]. They are nothing other than determinations of the Real in the divine ranks, such as names and attributes, and the cosmic ranks, such as fire and water in burning and drowning, despite the different kinds of causes and conditions. This indicates that the lowliness of some does not prevent them from being His determinations because of His exaltedness; nor should one say that, if all were His determinations, they would be equal or close in degree. Their disparity arises only from relations and considerations.\n\nTheir being identical with the determinations of the Real depends upon two premises. First, between the Real's first, non-sensible effusion and the recipient among sensible things there is nothing except that first effusion's own determination through receptivity qualified by a divine or cosmic rank. The qualification ‘non-sensible’ is needed because the veiled person imagines many intermediaries other than the effusion between it and a sensible recipient, but imagines no intermediary between a sensible effusion and its recipient. Without the qualification one might suppose that the sensible effusion was meant, and the argument that the intermediaries are identical with the non-sensible effusion would not be established.\n\nNo contingent ruling is added to that non-sensible effusion, such that the combination of effusion and ruling would mediate between the effusion and the recipient. The contingent ruling in question is what the effect of the effusion's passage through the intermediary ranks ‘requires’ and ‘necessitates’. He uses both terms to include operation by choice and by necessity. He mentions the ‘effect’ so that one does not suppose that passage alone imposes a contingent ruling on the effusion without affecting it. That is not so: a thing's ruling is its established effect. This effect is the effusion's being coloured by the rulings of the intermediaries' contingencies. The evidence that such rulings are not added to the effusion that passes through the intermediaries is that those rulings subsist in the intermediaries, and a single accident does not subsist through two causes [the supplied word بسببين requires verification].",
      "reason": "Replaces interpretive summary with continuous translation; restores the two chains, causal-intermediary reasoning and exact subjects; does not silently substitute ‘subjects’ for the received ‘causes’ in the final premise."
    },
    {
      "id": "MSH-P130",
      "pair_sequence": 1,
      "old_en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī:** The preceding argument grants that the effusion becomes determinate in passing through successive ranks, so that the mediators can be called determinations of the effusion. To conclude that they are determinations of the Real requires a second premise. Qūnawī states it as follows.\n\n**Qūnawī:** “One sees that the effusion is a self-disclosure from among the disclosures of the Real's inward aspect. The multiplicity of determinations that occurs in it belongs to the rulings of the name the Outward (*al-Ẓāhir*), since the outward aspect of the Real is the site in which His inward aspect becomes disclosed. The rulings of outward appearance make multiple the absolute unity of inwardness. These rulings are what are called the recipients (*qawābil*), and they are nothing other than the forms of the divine affairs (*ṣuwar al-shuʾūn*). Understand: God speaks the truth and guides whom He wills to a straight path.”\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Effusion is specified as disclosure of the inward Real, not merely a disclosure under a particular outward aspect. The differentiated determinations of effusion depend on the multiplicity of its receptive loci; plurality as such is a ruling of the name *al-Ẓāhir*, under which what is inward becomes displayed. The unity of inwardness is not a unity opposed to the possibility of plurality; it comprehends that plurality without yet presenting it as distinct. Outward manifestation makes that intelligible plurality apparent in its several forms.\n\nThe rulings called “recipients” are identified with the fixed entities and with forms of the divine affairs. Since the form of a thing marks its determination, these are characterized as determinations of the Real, not a freestanding ontological population existing over against Him. In that restricted sense the intermediate terms are none other than His determinations. One must nevertheless preserve the sequence of explanatory steps: determining effusion is not synonymous with creating an extrinsic accident in the divine Essence; nor is a phenomenal difference asserted to be sheer nothingness.\n\nAl-Mahāʾimī admits that this is what can be inferred from the expression under the perspective of unveiling. The full unity to which it alludes cannot be adequately stated in subject–predicate language: any verbal assertion contains at least a source and an asserted act, an agent and an object, or a subject and predicate. He identifies the “straight path” here with a tasted realization of unity that ordinary expressions cannot convey. The special reference to divine willing suggests, he conjectures, a bestowal of guidance outside acquisitive reasoning; proofs drawn from intellect or transmitted reports are not sufficient *as such* for this particular apprehension. This does not deny their validity in their own registers.",
      "new_en": "**Al-Mahāʾimī:** Certainly, the effusion acquires a determination through passing through them; the intermediaries are therefore determinations of the effusion. That is one premise. The other is that the determinations of the effusion are determinations of the Real. This is explained by the Shaykh's words:\n\n**Qūnawī:** ‘One sees that the effusion is a self-disclosure among the self-disclosures of the inward aspect of the Real. The multiple determinations that attach to it are the rulings of the name the Outward, insofar as the outward aspect of the Real is a locus of disclosure for His inward aspect. The rulings of manifestation multiply the unrestricted unity of inwardness. These rulings are what are called recipients, and they are the forms of the divine affairs, nothing else. Understand. God speaks the truth and guides whom He wills to a straight path.’\n\n**Al-Mahāʾimī:** This explains that the effusion's determinations are determinations of the Real: one sees the effusion as a self-disclosure among the self-disclosures of the inward aspect of the Real. He specifies this because the Real has many self-disclosures from the side of the Outward. Its being affected by multiplicity shows that it is a disclosure of the Inward: the effusion multiplies with the multiplicity of recipients, while multiplicities belong to the rulings of the name the Outward. Thus the effusion is the name the Outward, and the effusion is a self-disclosure of the Real through the Real, insofar as the outward aspect of the Real is a locus of disclosure for His inward aspect. The rulings of manifestation multiply the unrestricted unity of inwardness—that is, the unity belonging to the Inward [the connective wording is unstable]. This is unrestricted unity, not unity opposed to multiplicity; rather, it includes multiplicity.\n\nThe rulings of the name the Outward make that multiplicity manifest from it. Those rulings are called recipients, namely the fixed entities. The fixed entities are the forms of the Real's affairs. Thus the rulings in the name the Outward are forms of the Real's affairs, which are rulings of the name the Inward. The forms of a thing are its determinations; these are therefore determinations of the Real. Accordingly, the intermediaries are identical with His determinations, and a fortiori are nothing other than them. Understand.\n\nThis is what can be drawn from the expression that indicates unification by way of unveiling. God speaks the truth, which is unification itself, containing no multiplicity whatsoever. Otherwise, an expression necessarily indicates ‘unification’ as a verbal noun, ‘the one who unifies’ as an active participle, ‘what is unified’ as a passive participle, and a subject and predicate. He guides whom He wills among His servants to a straight path of tasted unification, which cannot be expressed. He qualifies this by mashīʾa because it is above irāda. Perhaps it is pure guidance—that is, acquisition has no part in it, since intellectual and transmitted proofs have no part there. He calls it the straight path because whatever lies below it is not free of a claim to partnership with God. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him.",
      "reason": "Restores the full chain from Inward/Outward to recipients/fixed entities, literal effusion-as-Outward assertion, grammatical argument and final guidance claim; removes translator's unsolicited doctrinal qualifications and softening."
    }
  ],
  "notes": [
````

````json
{
  "status": "Superseded historical drafts and separate online excerpts; retained for audit, excluded from the continuous reader.",
  "entries": [
    {
      "id": "QNW-001",
      "title": "Qūnawī original · Invocation, absoluteness, and three ranks of effusion",
      "heading_is_editorial": true,
      "printed_pages": [
        0,
        0
      ],
      "source_url": "https://www.ibnalarabi.com/qunawi/khusus.php?id=32",
      "speaker_layer": "Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī — separately printed original al-Nuṣūṣ (not al-Mahāʾimī commentary)",
      "edition_layer": "qunawi_original",
      "appendix_segment": 1,
      "arabic_transcription_status": "not_imported",
      "editorial_note": "Original independently printed Arabic matn: English source-section translation; printed pagination and full clause-by-clause collation not yet verified. Do not attribute these paragraphs to al-Mahāʾimī. Underlying Arabic available through Source page.",
      "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "",
          "en": "## Invocation and praise\n\nIn the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Ever-Merciful.\n\nPraise belongs to God, who has made clear, through the settled stations of aspirational resolve, the ranks and degrees of knowledge by certainty, the eye of certainty and the truth of certainty. Through the stilling of the seekers' anxiety He has clarified their attainment of the utmost that their souls desired, in accordance with their differing degrees in the stations through which they approach knowledge of Him, exalted is He. He has distinguished His elect from the rest of creatures by appointing for them no end other than His very Essence—not any of His worlds, nor any of the presences of His names and attributes. Rather He has made the highest object of their aspirations the noblest objects of His essential knowledge and the highest of His objects of will, so that the ultimate object of their striving is what He wills by Himself for Himself.\n\nFrom the standpoint of the loftiest aspects of His primary essential affairs (*shuʾūn*) and highest determinations, He Himself is their knowledge of certainty, eye of certainty and truth of certainty throughout the ranks of His essential knowledge. This knowledge is related first to Him and thereafter to what He knows, while they are effaced in Him under the aspect of their own selves, and the ruling of their existence and its diffusion remain throughout His existents and presences.\n\nMay God bless the one who has realized this in the most perfect witnessing and in the most complete, exalted and comprehensive knowledge, abiding continually in His presence through all his stations, circumstances, ranks and constitutions—our master Muḥammad, his family, and the elect among his community and brethren who receive from God his most complete legacy of sciences, states and stations. May their special shares, through which they are distinguished from others, bear their fruits along with the effects of following him and the relationships mediated through him. May this blessing continue in its ruling and remain fruitful through the endurance of time, according to time's universal reality and the detailed manifestations of its years, months, days and hours.\n\n## First noble text — Absoluteness is prior to even the attribution of unity\n\nKnow that the Real, considered in His essential absoluteness (*iṭlāq dhātī*), cannot rightly be subjected to a judgment, defined through a description or assigned any relation, whether of oneness, necessary existence, principiality, the requirement of bringing into existence, the issue of an effect, or the relation of knowledge directed towards Himself or towards another. All these involve determination and qualification. Every conceivable determination presupposes non-determination; consequently such predicates conflict with sheer absoluteness when applied at that level.\n\nIndeed, even to conceive of the Real's absoluteness it must be conceived as a **negative description**, not as an absoluteness which is merely the opposite of restriction. It is freedom from unity and multiplicity as they are ordinarily conceived; freedom even from limitation to the contrast between absoluteness and qualification, from confinement to their combination, and from confinement to transcendence above either. Consequently affirmation and negation of these predicates, taken at that level, stand alike: neither has precedence over the other. Once this is understood, it becomes clear that the attribution of unity, principiality, influence, the act of making things exist, and the like, is appropriate to the Real **under the consideration of determination**.\n\nThe first of the determinations bearing such relations is the intrinsic relation of knowing (*al-nisba al-ʿilmiyya al-dhātiyya*). Its distinction from the Essence is relative, **not a real separation**. By means of this intrinsic relation of knowledge the Real's unity, necessity of existence and principiality may be conceived. In particular, His knowledge of Himself in Himself is the ground of His knowledge of everything. Things are determinations of His universal and detailed intelligitions; quiddities are these intelligitions considered as intelligible forms. Their intelligible ordering is such that some are consequent upon others—not because fresh intelligitions successively arise in God's knowing, which would be unworthy of Him, but because there is an order of ranks within what is eternally and abidingly known. All are eternal intelligitions, remaining in one manner in His knowledge and related to by that knowledge in accordance with what their realities require.\n\nThe requirements of those realities can be considered in two ways. The first is their multiplicity being effaced within the unity of the Real: the detailed is understood within the undifferentiated, just as the knowledgeable person may contemplate in a single seed the branches, leaves and fruits that it can produce, and within each fruit a further seed bearing the analogous potential, and so on without end. The second is that the rulings of unity are conceived group after group, each with the quiddities contained within it as forms of the many intelligitions that differentiate the one existence. This is the converse of the first effacement: there multiplicity was absorbed in unity; here unity is, as it were, absorbed in multiplicity. Know this.\n\nConsidered in His encompassing absoluteness, the Real bears no name, has no judgment assigned to Him, and is determined by neither description nor mark. Under that standpoint the attribution of exigency or requirement (*iqtiḍāʾ*) has no priority over its denial, for any exigency conceived or rejected would itself be a determinate predicate. Nevertheless, insofar as exigency is considered essential, it has **three ranks**.\n\nIn its first rank the determination of its effect depends upon no condition or necessitating factor. In its second rank, it is related to one condition alone. In its third rank, the appearance of its rulings depends upon many conditions, causes and intermediaries. The ruling of the first is essential effusion (*al-fayḍ al-dhātī*), without a necessitating cause and without being conceived as corresponding to a recipient and its receptivity. The second is conditioned by one existential reality: the First Intellect, taken here as the intermediary between the Real and those possible things whose occurrence is apportioned until the Day of Resurrection. The third concerns the plurality of conditions through which effects appear, as in other existents.\n\nI do **not** mean that there are three requirements possessing different realities. It is **one requirement with three ranks**, according to each of which an effect or multiple effects become determinate and manifested. Understand.\n\n## Subsequent divine text — Essential knowledge and the things known\n\nThe Real's unitary essential knowledge is described as multiple only insofar as it is related to many objects of knowledge. Apprehension of those objects is realized through the determinations and relations of that knowledge. Its relation to each known thing follows the known thing as it is in itself: whether simple or composite, temporal or spatial, neither temporal nor spatial, receptive at a particular time or without such temporal restriction, finite or unbounded in ruling and description. This must be understood without importing plurality into the reality of the essential knowledge itself.\n\nAmong the corollaries is that every judgment made by a judging subject about a judged subject follows both the state of the judge when judging and the state of the judged subject under that judgment. If the subject is of a kind that changes from state to state, the judgments concerning it vary with the states under which it is considered. If it is fixed in one manner, the particular judgment remains fixed according to its definite relation. The judge himself may change through different states, or he may remain stable while the states of the judged object vary. These two considerations exhaust the principal respects under which judgments of any subject and object vary.\n\nAnother corollary is that **knowledge follows existence**: wherever existence is found, knowledge is not separated from it. The degrees of knowledge differ according to the degree to which a quiddity receives existence, perfectly or imperfectly. Where existence is received in a more complete manner, knowledge is correspondingly more complete; where receptivity is deficient, knowledge is deficient to the same extent. The predominance of possibility over necessity reverses the proportion previously described. Understand this."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "QNW-002",
      "title": "Qūnawī original · The limits of knowledge and first determination",
      "heading_is_editorial": true,
      "printed_pages": [
        0,
        0
      ],
      "source_url": "https://www.ibnalarabi.com/qunawi/khusus.php?id=32",
      "speaker_layer": "Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī — separately printed original al-Nuṣūṣ (not al-Mahāʾimī commentary)",
      "edition_layer": "qunawi_original",
      "appendix_segment": 2,
      "arabic_transcription_status": "not_imported",
      "editorial_note": "Original independently printed Arabic matn: English source-section translation; printed pagination and full clause-by-clause collation not yet verified. Do not attribute these paragraphs to al-Mahāʾimī. Underlying Arabic available through Source page.",
      "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "",
          "en": "### Completeness of knowing and knowledge of what lies beyond the object\n\nAnother corollary of the firmly established texts is this. Although I have briefly indicated aspects of it in some of my other works while discussing other matters, those discussions were expressed in the idiom appropriate to their subject. This book, however, is expressly devoted to the definitive statements derived from the distinctive experiential knowledge of the **station of perfection**, not to the ordinary idioms of restricted unveilings enjoyed by the possessors of particular spiritual stations, whose original grounding lies in the presence of a specific divine name or attribute. I have therefore been obliged to set apart those things that belong to the most comprehensive and perfect station, so that their validity corresponds to what God knows of the thing expressed in the highest, most complete and most perfect degree of His knowledge. I am not concerned merely to establish that a statement is true in relation to one station rather than another, one state or time rather than another, or under some such qualification.\n\nAfter this universal introduction, I state the text under discussion. Whatever is known by a human being—whether apprehended through consideration, unveiling, sensation or imagination, collectively or individually—has **not** been apprehended perfectly if the knower's consideration, unveiling or other act of apprehension fails to reach what lies **beyond** that thing, even after he has known its essential constituents and universal concomitants. In that case he has attained neither complete apprehension nor genuine comprehensive knowledge of it.\n\nThis holds whether the subject is the world in respect of its meanings and spirits, or in respect of its forms and accidents, or the Real Himself. Upon receiving a disclosure of the matter in its clarity, including the mode in which each known reality is determined within divine knowledge, the knower finds the matter as I describe. If knowledge of God has not reached the sheer absoluteness and pure unity of His true Essence—which no name, description, judgment or distinguishing mark identifies, which no witnessing or intellection circumscribes, and which cannot be confined to any specific reality—one has not learned that there is no final aim beyond God, that to encompass Him through knowing or witnessing is impossible, and that beyond unqualified true existence there is only imagined non-being.\n\nThere is another way, higher, more complete and more unveiling, to know **why it is impossible to know God as He knows Himself**. By God's favor I have known this by spiritual tasting and witnessing. Its expression and writing down, however, are forbidden; the most that can be said is the indication already given.\n\nA knower may attain the end proper to the divine name whose presence is the orientation of his station. This is especially so under the consideration that the name and the named are identical. Such an end is nevertheless **relative**. Principles and ends mark relative perfections, whereas true perfection transcends them. The Qurʾānic verse “And to your Lord is the ultimate end” (Q 53:42) indicates this. It does not say “your ultimate end is to your Lord” in a manner restricting the end to an individual's attained station. Rather the end of lordship as such is the ultimate end of all ends, beyond which are only endlessly differentiated degrees in greater and greater perfection, without a stopping point.\n\nThe Prophet's supplication elucidates this: “I seek refuge in Your good pleasure from Your wrath, in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot enumerate praise of You: You are as You have praised Yourself.” In other words, the worshipper cannot compass all that belongs to God. This combines the impossibility of total comprehension with the attainment of the end of all ends in knowledge of the Real. Prophetic reports contain many indications of the same truth for the reader who is alert to them.\n\nThe station and taste referred to have several terms of expression. Within Qurʾānic discourse one may refer to the distinguishing signs by which people are known; the ability to discern their marks arises from attaining a culminating standpoint from which one can survey what lies beyond. In the idiom of prophethood it is the *maṭlaʿ*, the rising-point or prospect of the meanings of a verse. A transmitted report refers to the Qurʾān's outward and inward aspects, boundary and rising-point, and to multiple inward depths. I have treated this in my commentary on the Opening (*al-Fātiḥa*). **The variants and chains of that report require separate verification.**\n\nAmong the people of God it is called the *mawqif*: the limit of each station, from which the next becomes visible. In the experiential knowledge of the station of perfection, when considered between two stations, it is their encompassing **isthmus** (*barzakh*); in relation to the distinctive station of perfection itself, it is the **isthmus of isthmuses** (*barzakh al-barāzikh*).\n\n### Noble text — Identity, unity, and the first intelligible determination\n\nThe unseen of the identity of the Real (*ghayb huwiyyat al-Ḥaqq*) refers to His absoluteness as non-determination. His real unity effaces all considerations, names and attributes. Relations and attributions are expressions of the Real's knowing Himself and apprehending them under the aspect of His determination. Although such determined knowing follows the sheer absoluteness referred to, compared with the determination of the Real in the apprehension of any apprehender under any specific self-disclosure, it is an **unqualified determination**—the most comprehensive determination. It is the witnessing of the perfected ones, the essential self-disclosure, and belongs to the highest station of unification.\n\nThe principiality of the Real follows this determination. Principiality is the root of considerations, the source of relations and attributions: those manifest in existence and those concealed within the field of intelligitions and minds. To say of Him that He is one, necessary and unqualified existence concerns the determination of existence within the intrinsic divine relation of knowledge. Under this relation the realized knower calls the Real the Principle (*al-mabdaʾ*), not under an unrelated attribution. Understand and reflect on this: I have included in this text the principle of the principles of divine knowledge. God is the guide.\n\nEvery wayfarer, by whichever path he proceeds, has the Real as his ultimate goal, provided he attains some felicity from Him. Thus every such wayfarer has an ascent (*miʿrāj*), and his travelling is an ascension. Understand."

      "pairs": [

          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "",
          "en": "### Comprehensive noble text — What does it mean for one thing to act upon another?\n\nKnow that anything described as possessing causal influence over one thing or several cannot be said to exercise that influence completely unless it affects the very reality of the thing, considered in itself, without adding any other qualification to the essence of the supposed agent, or any external condition whatsoever. I insist on these restrictions because of the effects attributed to things under their specific ranks or under considerations necessarily attached to their realities. I also insist on them because the following opinion has become widespread among speculative thinkers and many people of spiritual tasting: that everything called a mirror, whether intelligible or sensible, has an effect upon the form reflected within it. The rationale is that the mirror reflects the image back to the original, and that the image appears in the mirror in accordance with the mirror's properties.\n\nThat assertion is correct **in one respect, but not absolutely**. For the mirror could truly be said to affect the original only if it affected its very reality. It does not. An effect can be ascribed to the mirror in the apprehension of one who does not know the reflected reality itself and has only encountered it in the mirror. The mirror is not a container for the reality of the thing reflected. It is a locus in which its representation and **some** of its appearances are disclosed. The appearance of the form is a relation attributed to the original insofar as its image is impressed in the mirror; it is not itself the reality of the original.\n\nBy saying “some of its appearances” I intend an especially important distinction: specific essential self-disclosures (*al-tajalliyāt al-dhātiyya al-ikhtiṣāṣiyya*) do not occur **inside any locus or mirror** or according to any restricted rank. Whoever apprehends the Real through these disclosures witnesses the reality beyond the mirror, as reality itself, not according to a particular manifesting place, name, attribute, state or other determination. He knows by immediate experience that the mirror has no influence upon reality itself.\n\nOur master, the Imam—may God sanctify his spirit—called these the **lightning-like essential disclosures** (*al-tajalliyāt al-dhātiyya al-barqiyya*). At the time I did not know why he called them that or what he meant by the designation. The experience is obtained only by one who has become entirely vacant of the acquired descriptions, states and judgments connected with the necessity of the divine names and with contingent possibility. This is an absolute vacancy, which does not differ from the absoluteness of the Real. Yet it cannot endure for more than a single breath; hence it is likened to lightning.\n\nThe reason for its impermanence is the comprehensive nature (*jamʿiyya*) of the human reality. Just as human comprehensiveness does not allow that state to endure, so, if it did not contain the capacity for the vacancy and absoluteness through which this disclosure is received, it would not encompass every description and state. Human comprehensiveness both establishes the possibility of this experience and prevents its permanence. When God granted me this self-disclosure, I found extraordinary effects in my inward and outward being. Though it did not last for two breaths, it left in the locus qualities and sciences whose number none but God could encompass.\n\nOn the very night when I wrote down what had come to me, I knew that anyone who had not tasted this witnessing was not fit to bear the inheritance [in the fullest sense]. Nor would such a person grasp the secret of the saying ascribed to the Prophet, “I have with God a time in which none but my Lord can contain me”; nor the saying, “God was and there was nothing with Him”; nor His statement, “Our command is only one, like a flash of the eye” (Q 54:50). Neither could he grasp the secret of principiality in bringing into existence when there was no existing time. **The precise provenance and wording of these transmitted reports are subject to a separate ḥadīth-critical inquiry.**\n\nThe one who has tasted this witnessing and who knows that the fixed entities are the realities of existents, that they are not made, that the Reality of the Real is transcendent above being made or being affected, and that there is no third independently existing thing besides the Real and the entities, must realize—provided the vision has been attained in the way I describe—that **nothing produces an effect in the very reality of anything else**. Things are described as affecting their own effects. What people call causes and agents are conditions for the manifestation of the effects of things within their own realities; no separate reality acts upon the intrinsic reality of another.\n\nUnderstand accordingly the matter of assistance or supply (*madad*). Nothing independently supplies existence to some other thing as though transferring a constituent of itself. Supply reaches the outward from the inward aspect of the thing, and existential luminous disclosure reveals that inward supply. Manifestation is not a modification of the intrinsic reality of what becomes manifest. Relations are described as influencing one another only in the sense that certain relations condition the emergence of others and the appearance of their rulings in the reality from which they arise.\n\nAn additional insight of the one tasting this disclosure is that the fixed entities, **insofar as they are mirrors**, have no effect upon the essential divine existential disclosure except the appearance of the multiplicity hidden within that disclosure. Their influence is on the **relation of manifestness**, which is the condition of outward disclosure. The Real is too exalted to be affected by any other, and the realities of beings, inasmuch as they are considered under their own essential realities, are likewise beyond being acted upon by something other than themselves. Under the taste of perfection their realities, in this respect, are the intrinsic affairs of the Real. No mirror, merely as mirror, modifies the reality of what is reflected in it.\n\nUnderstand and contemplate this text; I have included in it precious sciences and secrets whose value none but God can assess. This is the truth of certainty and the clear definitive text. Anything you hear that conflicts with it, even if correct, is correct only **relatively**; this statement is the unqualified truth without doubt. God is the guide and one who directs.\n\n### Corollaries about causes, fruits, and the uniqueness of every disclosure\n\nSome universal texts have been mentioned in my *Miftāḥ ghayb al-jamʿ wa-tafṣīlihi* and in other writings I composed—not by appropriating other people's words, for God has enriched me with His gifts—but because this book is especially assigned to these texts I must mention the most relevant of them again.\n\nOne says: anything that is the cause of multiplicity or many things, **insofar as it is their source**, cannot be determined in some single manifestation or appear to an observer except in relation to the observer's particular field of vision. Another says: a thing does not, from itself as itself, issue forth or produce what contradicts its reality, or what differs altogether from it, whatever the kind of fruit—intelligible, spiritual, imaginal, imaginative, sensible or natural. This is a general principle concerning everything described as a source or a fruitful root, considered simply as itself and under a further subtle consideration apprehended by only a few realized knowers.\n\nWhen something seems to contradict the principle, the difference arises from **external conditions or qualifications**, and from the configuration produced by the conjunction of the source's reality with those conditions and with the rulings of the rank in which that conjunction becomes determinate. The Qurʾān says: “Each acts according to his own disposition” (Q 17:84).\n\nNor does a thing produce its very own identical reality, or what is exactly like it in every respect, for that would entail the same existence appearing twice, in one reality, one rank and one manner—an empty re-attainment of what is already attained. Such purposeless repetition would be unworthy of the Real, the wise and knowing Agent. The origin and its fruit must differ in some respect. The contingent possibilities are without end while the effusion of the Real, origin of origins, is one. Thus there is **no repetition in existence** for the one who understands.\n\nFor this reason realized masters say that God does not disclose Himself twice to the same person in precisely one form, nor to two different people in precisely the same form. Some respect of distinction must always be present. Remember this; God is the guide."
````
