      "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "",
          "en": "### Noble text — Gifts of the Essence and gifts of the Names\n\nKnow that since no name, attribute or judgment—negative or affirmative—can be attributed to the Real under His absolute aspect, all such predications must concern determinations. Every plurality, whether outwardly existent or intellectually conceived, must be preceded by a unity. Thus the many determinations by which names, attributes and rulings are ascribed to the Real must be preceded by a determination from which all determinations originate. Beyond this first determination is nothing but sheer absoluteness, itself a negative expression that denies to the innermost divine Essence every description, judgment, determination and consideration, as well as confinement to any name or aspect.\n\nOne who possesses sound reason, even without authentic unveiling, may reflect on the names and attributes that follow this first determination. If his intellect cannot conceive names and attributes prior to those at which it has arrived, then those are, *relative to his attainment*, names of the Essence. During the veil of discursive reasoning he may infer their precedence from the comprehensiveness of their rulings and the dependency of subsequent names on them. From this principle divine gifts are understood: every benefit that comes from the Real to creatures is either **an essential gift**, **a gift of the names**, or a gift attributable jointly to Essence and names.\n\nEssential gifts do not fall under reckoning; their determinations are not captured or enumerated by number. Gifts of the names, including those jointly attributed to Essence and names, may stand closer to the divine Essence or closer to the domain of names and attributes. Where the relation to names and attributes predominates, the gift is subject to reckoning, easy or difficult according to the strength of the relevant rulings. Where its relation to the Essence predominates, it belongs among gifts without reckoning. A profound secret lies in this matter that cannot be disclosed. What is essential, or possesses a stronger intrinsic relation to the Essence, is given and received through **intrinsic affinity** (*munāsaba dhātiyya*) and not through some other independent necessitating factor.\n\nWithout this principle the real meaning of the Qurʾānic descriptions of provision “without reckoning” remains hidden, as in Q 3:27 and Q 24:38, and of the gift “without reckoning” in Q 38:39. A prophetic report likewise speaks of great multitudes of the Prophet's community entering the Garden without reckoning. They receive gifts of the names, but their relation to the Essence is stronger than their relation to names and attributes; hence they follow those who possess intrinsic affinity and share in their states.\n\nNow that we have distinguished the kinds of gifts and their rulings, consider the kinds of recipients. They differ in accordance with the requests constituted by their readiness, spiritual state, station, spirit, natural temperament or accidental natural condition—each of which has, as it were, a language of asking. The highest recipients see the Face of the Real **in the conditions, causes and intermediaries** through which gifts are received. They know by witnessing that these mediating causes are determinations of the Real in divine and cosmic ranks. Between the effusion received and its recipient nothing stands as an independent created efficacy; the effusion is itself differentiated through the particular receptivity in which it becomes manifest. The knower does not suppose that the effusion became fundamentally altered merely by travelling through a chain of intermediary causes and taking on the contingencies of each. He sees the effusion as a manifestation of the inwardness of the Real. Its multiple determinations belong to the rulings of the name *al-Ẓāhir* (the Manifest), for the outward aspect of the Real manifests His inward aspect. Rulings of appearance differentiate the unqualified unity of hiddenness; those rulings are the recipients, the forms of the intrinsic affairs. God speaks the truth and guides whom He wills to a straight path.\n\n### Definitive text — Prayer, right apprehension, and response\n\nA lucid text and universal measure by which divine answering or non-answering, and human compliance, may be known: the complete and valid standard for determining when a servant truly obeys his Lord, and when divine response comes swiftly **in precisely what he asks for**, without substitution or postponement, is **correctness of knowledge** and **perfection of compliance** (*muṭāwaʿa*).\n\nThe more accurate one's knowledge and conception of the Real, the swifter the response to the exact matter requested. The more completely one attends to divine commands and hastens to perform them in willing compliance, the greater is the correspondence of divine response to him. For this reason most prayers of the great among the people of God receive an answer, due to the completeness of their compliance and the accuracy of their knowledge and conception of God. The Qurʾān says: “Call upon Me; I will answer you” (Q 40:60).\n\nA person lacking genuine knowledge through witnessing and possessing only a relative, restricted conception is not, in the required sense, directing his prayer to the Real whom God has promised to answer. Rather, he turns to a particular image formed in his mind by his thinking and imagination, or by what he has inherited from the thinking and imagination of others. For this reason response to the *very object* of his request may be withheld or delayed. If such a person nevertheless receives an answer, the explanation can lie in the secret of divine presence with all things, or in the comprehensive concentration characteristic of those in extremity: their necessity gives rise to a readiness for receiving the promised response.\n\nThe person who has accurate knowledge and conception, by contrast, brings the Real to presence in his awareness and actually directs his aspiration to Him. His knowledge need not encompass every aspect; even a true orientation through a particular rank, name or attribute suffices to distinguish him from the first case. Such is the condition of the intermediate ranks among the people of God; the former condition is that of the veiled.\n\nThe perfected ones and certain unique individuals have a further condition. Their orientation follows the essential self-disclosure through which they have attained the station of perfection. That witnessing yields a comprehensive apprehension of the respects of the divine names, attributes, ranks and considerations. Their conception of the Real is thus sound through the most perfect witnessing, and their prayers are not delayed. Moreover, some of them are admitted to the knowledge of the Preserved Tablet, the rank of the Pen, and even the divine presence of knowing. They recognize what has been allotted to occur; consequently they do not ask for an impossibility which has not been decreed, nor does their aspiration move toward willing it.\n\nI have explicitly mentioned **willing**, because some events are related to the will of such a person without any articulated prayer or request. For many years I witnessed innumerable instances of this in our master—may God sanctify his spirit. He told me that in one of his spiritual occurrences he had seen the Prophet, who gave him the glad tidings: “God is quicker to respond to you than you are to turn to Him in supplication.”\n\nThis is a station above that of prayers being answered, and derives from perfected compliance; indeed it lies above the station normally termed compliance. The latter means hastening to obey commands, seeking the things pleasing to God, and fulfilling divine rights as far as one is able. Qūnawī here adduces reports concerning the Prophet and Abū Ṭālib to illustrate divine responsiveness. **Their precise wording and historical attribution require examination; they are preserved here as reports cited in the primary text, not certified historical evidence.**\n\nThe higher station returns to the servant's essential reality corresponding completely to what the Real wills for him by the first universal will. That will relates to the complete bringing to light and self-manifestation (*al-jalāʾ wa-l-istijlāʾ*) for which the cosmos is created. The **perfect human** (*al-insān al-kāmil*) is specifically the intended locus; everything else is intended in a derivative manner, insofar as what is necessary for realizing an end is also willed for the sake of that end.\n\nThe perfect human is intended as such because he is the complete mirror of the Real. Through him the Real is manifested with respect to His Essence and all His names, attributes, rulings and considerations, in the manner in which He knows Himself and the realities of His objects of knowledge. The mirror must not impose a deficiency of receptivity or distortion such that what is displayed differs from what it is in itself. One whose reality is so constituted has no will standing apart from the will of the Real. He is the mirror of his Lord's will and the other attributes. Accordingly his supplication is effaced into a will not opposed to divine will, and what he wills occurs in accordance with the divine saying “Doer of whatever He wills” (Q 85:16).\n\nIf he supplicates, he does so as a mirror of all the worlds, speaking in their tongues and ranks. If he refrains from supplication, he does so under his aspect as a locus of manifestation turned toward the divine presence. Beyond this station is no further station to which a traveller could aspire. Beneath it stands the person whose sound conception and perfected knowledge make him a genuine addressee of “Call upon Me; I will answer you”; the promised divine response is true. Other forms of address and orientation cannot be treated as possessing precisely the same conditions.\n\nUnderstand this and you will attain precious secrets and extraordinary sciences that discursive thinking and written exposition have not reached. God is the guide."

      "edition_layer": "qunawi_original",
      "appendix_segment": 5,

      "editorial_note": "Original independently printed Arabic matn: English source-section translation; printed pagination and full clause-by-clause collation not yet verified. Do not attribute these paragraphs to al-Mahāʾimī. Underlying Arabic available through Source page.",
      "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "",
          "en": "### Noble text — Knowing through union and the one knowledge of the many\n\nKnow that the highest degree of knowledge of a thing, whoever knows it and whether the thing known is single or manifold, is realized through union with the known and the absence of otherness between knower and known. For the reason that ignorance prevents complete apprehension is the predominance of the factor by which the two are distinct. Distinction constitutes an intelligible distance, and distance prevents perfected apprehension. The ranks of knowledge vary with the predominance of that through which the knower and the known are one; this is true nearness, overcoming the separation that is true distance.\n\nIf you witness and taste this through a verified unveiling, you will know that the perfection of the Real's knowledge of things comes from His manifesting them to Himself within Himself, their plurality and otherness being absorbed within His unity. For a thing's being present in any locus, intelligible or formal, is in accordance with the way it is determined and displayed there. Hence we say that the Real knows Himself through Himself and knows things in Himself through the very knowledge through which He knows Himself. The report that God was when nothing was with Him points to the absence of the things' otherness when considered in the unity in which they are contained; their later differentiated consideration does not invalidate the priority of the Real in unity.\n\nWhen the multiplicity of things that had previously been implicit in unity becomes individually intelligible, and the judgment of unity is brought together with their distinction, the perfection previously hidden in unity becomes outwardly disclosed. Thus there opens the door of perfected manifestation and self-manifestation (*jalāʾ* and *istijlāʾ*), which is the genuine object of the process. The judgments of unity appear within multiplicity and those of multiplicity within unity.\n\nUnity makes multiplicity one by becoming the common existential respect among many things distinguished in their intrinsic realities; by gathering these things in itself, it connects what distinguishes them. The many, in turn, cause the One to appear as many through determinations that diversify its appearance, like colouring and the qualities required by the differing preparedness of the numerous loci of one self-disclosure. Thus comes the differentiation of knowledge of kinds of disclosure and their accompanying rulings, including the relational effects of making and undoing, outwardly and inwardly, above and below, within time and beyond particular time, in correspondence or lack of correspondence. All this rests on the connecting disclosure of the One that gathers the manifold.\n\nKnowledge, delight and felicity vary with *munāsaba*, the proportion of affinity; ignorance, suffering and misery vary with the strength of separation and difference. Where the rulings of joining and separation intermingle, the relative dominance of each determines the outcome. The common source and reference-point of a cluster of such rulings in a particular kind of affinity is a **rank** (*martaba*). Understand.\n\nAs I began writing this text, it was said to me inwardly that the rulings belonging to unity and to the one Real—referred to as the rulings of necessity—derive, from the standpoint of unity, from **one ruling**, the reality of *qaḍāʾ* (decree). The apportioned measures (*maqādīr*) arise through the plurality of known things under that one ruling. The appearing of one existence according to that plurality has a primary effect, and then a secondary effect in the measured things by returning their influence to them. Reflect on this unusual distinction; God is the guide.\n\n### Further noble text — Two signs of complete knowledge of something other than the Real\n\nThe highest degree of knowledge of any thing **other than the Real** is to know it by a knowledge resulting from seeing it completely within divine knowledge. There are two signs of this attainment. First, the knowledge obtained is sufficient, so that one has no need to revisit and reconsider the subject in pursuit of increased knowledge. An increase after one has claimed already to know it demonstrates that the earlier knowledge was incomplete. Complete knowledge of an object would leave nothing additional to discover about it, as is the case of divine knowledge, and requires complete intellectual encompassment of the known.\n\nThe second sign is that the ruling of knowledge extends beyond the object's restricted determination until one apprehends its ultimate limit as joined to the absoluteness of the Real. Knowledge of the Real Himself, however, is not like this. What is known of Him is only what appears through some determination in a rank, locus, state, respect or consideration. Whenever a particular determination comes within one's grasp, a further determination of the unqualified Essence becomes manifest to the knower according to the state under which the Real is now disclosed. Human states do not reach a final point at which they cease to change, and the modes of the Real's manifestation to human beings likewise do not come to an end.\n\nI have previously indicated that the names are names of states. The fixed entities are subject to the passing of states over them, whereas the Real is disclosed in the states, as indicated by “Every day He is upon some affair” (Q 55:29). Understand. Do not be satisfied merely with reinterpretation: strive to witness first, then trust and surrender; God grants success.\n\n### Noble text — Every absolute thing has a conditional respect\n\nNo existent in the world described as unqualified lacks a respect in which it is conditioned—even if only by the way it is determined within the conception of one or more knowers. Likewise no existent judged conditioned lacks some respect in which it relates to absoluteness. Only one who knows things perfectly after knowing the Real, and knows the respects by which they are understood, can apprehend this. Whoever has not tasted this witnessing has not yet fully realized knowledge of the Real and the created order.\n\n### Text — Essential perfection and the appearance of greater perfection\n\nThe Real has an essential perfection and a perfection of the names whose outward manifestation is related to the creation of the cosmos. Under the consideration of **determination**, both may be called perfections of the names: every judgment about an object presupposes that the object has been distinguished within the judge's knowledge. Were the Essence not first conceived as distinct by its intrinsic independence from all else, one would not describe a perfection as “essential.” Every determinate respect considered of the Real may be called a name, for the names, according to the realized knowers, are determinations of the Real.\n\nUnder this respect all perfection ascribed to Him may be called a perfection of the names. But from another respect, the generation of the names from the presence of His unity belongs to the requirements of His own reality; accordingly every perfection ascribed to Him may be called **essential**. From this distinction it follows that an intrinsic perfection does not become deficient when external accidents or concomitants appear in some ranks; nor can an inherent defect be imagined that these accidents would repair. Rather, in certain ranks the description of **greater perfection** (*akmaliyya*) comes into appearance, including the realization that the intrinsic perfection is unaffected by those manifestations.\n\n### Very noble text — The reality of the Real and that of the creature\n\nThe reality of the Real is the form of His knowledge of Himself considered under the determination of His knowing Himself, where knower, knowledge and known are one. His intrinsic attribute, not distinct from His Essence, is the oneness of a comprehensive gathering (*aḥadiyyat jamʿ*) beyond which no further gathering, relation or consideration is conceivable. To witness and know this attribute properly is to recognize that the Real is called determined within each determined thing in accordance with the respect that permits His apprehension there, **without** thereby being restricted to that determination. He is in Himself not determined even while one predicates determination of Him under the aspect of manifestation, whether one considers the locus identical with what appears or distinct from it.\n\nThe reality of the created order is the form of its Lord's knowledge of it. Its intrinsic attribute is **poverty** (*faqr*) of the kind that opens upon unqualified sufficiency—not every poverty indiscriminately. Understand.\n\n### Very noble text — Three modes of transcendence (*tanzīh*)\n\nThe result of **rational transcendence** (*tanzīh ʿaqlī*) is to distinguish the Real from what is called “other” through negative attributes, in order to ward off defects imagined by the intellect though not existing as independent realities. The outcome of **revealed or scriptural transcendence** (*tanzīh sharʿī*) is to deny multiple independent existences and partnership in the rank of divinity. Scripture maintains this even when created things share the linguistic predication of affirmative qualities with God, so as to exclude equality and likeness. Hence verses speak of God as the best of providers, best of forgivers, most excellent of creators and most merciful of the merciful, and say that God is greater.\n\n**Transcendence according to unveiling** (*tanzīh kashfī*) affirms comprehensive gathering in the Real without circumscription, while distinguishing the distinct rulings of the names. Not every effect can properly be attributed to every divine name: some relations are impossible for certain names though true of others. The same holds for the attributes. Its fruit is the denial of independent otherness without denying that numerical distinctions appear under their own respect, without presuming either an external defect to negate or an acquired perfection to append. Peace.\n\n### Noble text — The locus conditions how something is present\n\nThe presence or being of anything within anything else follows the nature of the locus, whether that locus is intelligible or formal. Thus possible things, considered as eternally determined and represented in divine knowledge, are described in respect of their fixed intelligible relations as eternal; considered under another aspect, however, each determination also bears a relation to origination. The world's existence and the knowledge of its inhabitants are originated and receptive; divine existence and knowledge are not. Know this and you will be guided, God willing.\n\n### Comprehensive noble text — Divine names and the ranks of their determination\n\nThe word **Essence** (*dhāt*) is appropriately applied to the Real only under a determination: the first intelligible determination following, in the understanding of those not perfected, the nameless, indescribable absoluteness which is indicated only negatively. The positive determination is first; it encompasses intrinsically the essential names, **keys of the unseen** (*mafātīḥ al-ghayb*), and the Essence named is not distinct from these names in any respect. The names differ among themselves and may stand in opposition, though they are also united under the all-inclusive Essence. Unity of singularity (*aḥadiyya*) describes determination, not the absolutely unqualified as such: the latter bears neither name nor attribute.\n\nFrom the aspect that these names are not other than the Essence, one can say that the Real acts essentially. There is one intrinsic concomitant of the Essence, distinguished from it **only relatively**: **knowledge** (*ʿilm*). Unity is affirmed of the Real under the consideration of knowledge, for in and through it the rank of divinity, the other ranks, and all objects of knowledge become determined and inscribed. Knowledge is a mirror of the Essence with its essential names, which are not other than the Essence itself. It is the root and source of intelligible multiplicity. To call it a mirror of the known realities and of the Essence is to consider its distinction from Essence as a conceptual one through which the Real's knowing of Himself in Himself can be expressed. His essential knowledge is, as it were, a mirror of Himself.\n\nAs we have said elsewhere, the reality of the Real is the form of His knowledge of Himself. Every thing made manifest in a locus is distinct from that locus in some respect, **except that the Real may be said to be both the appearing and the locus under the different considerations explained**. Do not turn this into a multiplication of independent existents.\n\nRanks are comprehensive determinations contained in the single intrinsic concomitant—knowledge. They resemble stations through which the unqualified effusion passes, in the sense already explained concerning the relation of disclosure to what is disclosed. They have a qualified role in the manifestation of causal effects, not independent causality. Every rank is an intelligible locus in which a grouping of the rulings of necessity and possibility appears, from the essential names and the principal divine names and their derivative names. Ranks have fixed entities within the field of knowledge and intelligition. Their influence is not independent: it occurs through existence. By the way the effusion is determined in their receptivity, the ranks function like forms or moulds that condition the appearance of what passes through them. They are thus points of gathering, sources and returns of relational effects. Understand.\n\nThe ranks are understood as proceeding from one another, and similarly the names. Divinity (*ulūhiyya*) with its chief names—Living, Knowing, Willing and Powerful—is the shadow of the Essence considered as containing the keys of the unseen. A subtle distinction remains: divinity can be considered as distinct from the principal names, whereas the Essence cannot be distinguished from its **essential** names by the one who witnesses essential disclosure. Any such distinction is a product of the understanding of someone veiled from that disclosure. The names differ in their relations while remaining inseparable; some follow others, as Creator, Originator and Fashioner follow their own principal names. Remember this."

          "en": "### Connection concerning the secret of affinities\n\nThe secret of affinities (*munāsabāt*) is participation in a respect that removes the rulings of mutual otherness from precisely the aspect in which affinity is established. Their first and highest form is **intrinsic affinity** (*munāsaba dhātiyya*). Such affinity between the Real and the human being who is specifically intended is established under two aspects.\n\nFirst, the human being's mirrorhood exerts only a weak modifying effect upon the self-disclosure determined in him. That is, the mirror does not give the disclosed Real any character that compromises His holiness; there is only the qualification of determination, which cannot impair the divine greatness, majesty or unity. Such a person is free of most of the limitations of possibility and of the properties of the intermediaries. From this perspective the degrees of the intimate ones and the unique individuals differ.\n\nThe second aspect of affinity with the Real is the servant's share of **the form of the divine presence**. This share varies according to his comprehensiveness (*jamʿiyya*). Affinity grows stronger or weaker as the circle of his comprehensive capacity widens or narrows; sometimes he receives a fuller portion, and at other times less.\n\nThe one who encompasses the attributes and rulings of the ranks of necessity and possibility, and everything of them that can become actual in each age and time, while also possessing the first kind of affinity, has **perfection**. He is loved by the Real and intended for his own sake. By the reality of being the **isthmus of isthmuses** (*barzakh al-barāzikh*), he is the mirror both of the Essence and of divinity with their concomitants. One who possesses only the first aspect of intrinsic affinity may be beloved and brought near, but is not thereby the all-comprehensive perfect human. I have indicated this distinction earlier.\n\n### Intrinsic affinity between people: temperament and spirituality\n\nIntrinsic affinity among human beings likewise arises under two aspects, parallel to the two just mentioned. One is a shared **temperament** (*mizāj*): the degrees of temperamental equilibrium occupied by the two persons may coincide within the range of human temperaments, or one degree may stand next to the other. This is a major principle in the way of realization, though few truly know it by taste.\n\nThe differentiation of human spirits and their ranks of nobility and elevation is connected to the number and distance of intermediaries, and to how the rulings of possibility increase or decrease with them. After the prior decree and determination of God, bodily temperament is the condition according to which a particular spirit is determined. What approaches the point of true equilibrium—the center proper to the perfected souls—is capable of receiving a more noble spirit with a higher relationship to the ranks of superior intellects and souls. What stands farther from that point has a correspondingly lower relation. The preceding statement about shared temperaments is therefore a preliminary to knowing the **spiritual affinity** of the second aspect, which resembles the hidden and pure intrinsic affinity with the Real.\n\nWhen you understand this through witnessed disclosure or verified understanding, you will see that some spirits have their origin of determination in the Preserved Tablet, others in the spirituality of the Throne under the station associated with Isrāfīl, others in the Footstool under Mīkāʾīl, and others in the Lote Tree under Jibrīl. The ranks descend to the nearest heaven, whose governing angel Qūnawī here calls Ismāʿīl. The variation in their degrees depends, after the precedence of divine knowledge, providence, decree and will, upon temperaments and their nearness to or distance from equilibrium. Divine care and will appear in the proper formation of the body, followed by the breathing of the spirit and its determination.\n\n**Editorial caution:** these are medieval metaphysical, angelological and physiological correspondences. Their hierarchy and reported names should be documented as source claims, not silently presented as scientific facts or universally accepted theological assertions.\n\n### Rank-based affinities and the origins of spirits\n\nAffinities based on rank (*munāsaba martabiyya*) have several forms. One concerns the original mines or sources of determination of spirits. The highest human spirits—the spirits of the perfected—have their principial rank in the Mother of the Book (*Umm al-Kitāb*). Others are determined through the Supreme Pen, also termed the First Intellect and Universal Spirit; others through the Preserved Tablet; others through the throne-related rank of Isrāfīl, the Footstool and Mīkāʾīl, the Lote Tree and Jibrīl, and then the other classes descending to the ruler of the nearest heaven. Qūnawī reports the correspondence of the last with the **Active Intellect** of the Peripatetic philosophers.\n\nAnother form of rank-based affinity depends on **imaginal manifestations**. Spirits at their diverse ranks have forms or loci in which they become manifest. Apart from the perfected, the first such human locus is the **absolute imaginal world** (*ʿālam al-mithāl al-muṭlaq*). Even where an imaginative form has its materials in the subtle powers of the natural constitution, and in purified spiritual capacities, its manifestations in the Garden depend upon the spirituality, powers and properties of those original imaginal forms.\n\nThe dwellings of the inhabitants of Paradise are thus signs of the ranks of their spirits in relation to the Real and their primary imaginal manifestations. Qūnawī cites reports concerning the proximity of dwellings in the Garden and the ability of believers to recognize their own dwellings there. He interprets these reports through affinity and rank rather than crude spatial distance alone.\n\nThe **market of Paradise**, containing beautiful human forms that inhabitants may choose to assume, is described as part of the river-system or channels of the absolute imaginal world. It is a source of imaginal forms and of supplies communicated to the spirits of the inhabitants. Their food, drink, clothing and other joys are manifested according to the planes of their deeds, convictions, traits, states and degrees of equilibrium. Qūnawī thereby ties eschatological imagery to his account of imaginal receptivity rather than treating it as merely an analogue of material goods.\n\nThe robes of honor and gifts carried by angels to the generality of the people of Paradise when they are brought to the hill of vision for an audience with the Real manifest the rulings of names and attributes upon which these visitors depend, even when they do not know it. The gifts strengthen their affinity with the Real, renewing the subtle threads connecting them with Him through the names and attributes having lordly authority over them.\n\nThe command to the angels, “Return them to their palaces,” is interpreted as the ending of the particular rulings through which they had been gathered in the audience. When the opposed rulings of names that distinguish and separate come into effect, the visitors again experience separation and veil. The diversity of their ranks during the audience follows their standing before the Real, the accuracy of their beliefs, their knowledge and genuine witnessings, and the degree to which they preferred the divine presence above other things in their earlier lives. The length of their company, the honor of the address made to them and what they apprehend of it all vary accordingly. Their apprehension is also conditioned by how they present to themselves what they knew or believed of God, and by the particular disclosure associated with the hill of vision.\n\n### The perfected ones and modes of posthumous affinity\n\nThe condition of the **perfected** is different. They have passed beyond the presences of names and attributes and the self-disclosures particular to them, reaching the field of **essential disclosure**. Qūnawī adduces a report describing a class of inhabitants of Paradise from whom the Lord does not conceal Himself. Because they cannot be confined by Paradise, another world, time, place or any particular presence, they are with Him wherever He is, in a manner that is not defined by *where*, bodily distance, a veil, a journey to an audience, or a meeting whose duration ends under a temporal ruling. Thus their state does not depend on periodic transit through specific places of visitation. Seek a portion of their high ranks, for God is the bestower of good.\n\nAs for affinities between people through their **intermediate or barzakh** ranks, the Prophet's account of the Night Journey provides an example. He saw Adam in the nearest heaven with multitudes of his descendants to his right and left, the blessed and the wretched, and Adam's different response to the two. Qūnawī reads this as an indication of ranks corresponding to general felicity and misery after death. The wretched differ in their degrees; he records reports concerning locations where certain spirits are gathered. In the highest regions of the nearer world the blessed also differ, and more particular stations are associated in the Night Journey with prophets in the succeeding heavens—Jesus, Joseph, Idrīs, Aaron, Moses and Abraham, peace upon them.\n\nThose participating in the prophetic legacies inherit differentiated ranks under these spiritual stations. But the visions of those seven prophets need not exhaust the ranks of all messengers, prophets, saints and inheritors: many others have their own degrees. Qūnawī adduces a report of multiple ascensions of the Prophet and appeals to Abū Nuʿaym in connection with their transmission. **The exact number, provenance and authenticity of that report remain to be verified.**\n\nThe sevenfold mapping is, on his argument, an **example** of particular correspondences operative in one disclosure, not a final exhaustive inventory of prophetic ranks. Thus one prophet can be associated with another in certain manifestations—for example John (Yaḥyā) may be understood as sharing a station now with Jesus and now with Aaron—because of an affinity of attributes, activities or states. Think about this and you may be guided, God willing."

          "en": "### Very noble text — Existence is one without being the opposite of multiplicity\n\nKnow that the Real is **pure existence** (*al-wujūd al-maḥḍ*), in which there is no difference, and that He is one by a genuine unity. This unity is not conceived as the opposite of multiplicity, nor does its reality or the correct conception of it depend on conceiving an opposite. Rather it is established through itself, establishing and not requiring to be established. When we say “unity,” we do so to indicate transcendence and to facilitate understanding, **not** to ascribe to the Real the restricted notion of unity conceived in veiled minds.\n\nConsidered in this unity, in abstraction from loci of manifestation and from attributes assigned according to manifestation and His appearing in them, He cannot be apprehended, encompassed, known, named or described. Whatever a person perceives within concrete entities or witnesses in the cosmos, by whatever mode or in whichever presence, insofar as it is perceived *in a locus*, is of a different order. The exception is knowledge of intelligible realities as they are in the unseen rank, apprehended by unveiling. What is apprehended in a locus comprises colours, lights, surfaces and the manifold differences of quality and quantity. Their analogues appear in the imaginal world connected with the human constitution, or within the imaginal world considered in another respect as separate from it. Their plurality is sensible; any unity affirmed of them is intellectually apprehended or intuited.\n\nAll these are rulings of existence, forms of the relations of divine knowledge, or attributes accompanying existence under the consideration of its relation to the entities in which it appears and through which it is made manifest. However one describes these appearances, **they are not existence itself**. Existence is one and is not grasped through anything considered as other than it. The one insofar as it is one is not apprehended through plurality simply insofar as it is plural, and conversely. A human being does not apprehend something through a unity completely identical to the unity of existence: apprehension requires his existence, life, possession of knowledge, and an affinity between him and the thing approached, together with the removal of obstacles. He therefore apprehends through the many respects of his constitution, not through the sheer oneness devoid of all multiplicity. I have explained further secrets of this point in *Kashf sirr al-ghayra ʿan sirr al-ḥayra*, and more will follow elsewhere.\n\n### Existence and quiddities: the fixed entities are known, not independently made\n\nExistence in respect of the Real is identical with His Essence. In respect of any other existent, existence is conceptually added to its reality. The reality of each existent is the relation of its eternal determination within its Lord's knowledge: the realized knowers call this its **fixed entity** (*ʿayn thābita*); other thinkers call it a quiddity, a known non-existent, a fixed thing, or something similar.\n\nFrom the standpoint of the unity of His existence, nothing proceeds from the Real but **one**, for what is simply one as one cannot bring forth a plurality under precisely that same respect. Yet what proceeds as one is not, in our account, a separately existing First Intellect in the manner described by certain philosophers. It is the **general existence effused** upon the entities of generated beings, including those that have become outwardly actual and those whose actuality is eternally known but not yet manifested. This one existence is shared by the Supreme Pen, also named the First Intellect and described as the first existent, and by all the other existents. According to realized knowledge there is not a third independent ontological class between the Real and the world. The world consists of realities known by the Real under their determinations and described by their relation to existence.\n\nBecause the determinate images of these realities are eternally known in the intrinsic divine knowledge, those realities **under that respect** cannot themselves be things newly made. To make them in the essential knowing would require originated changes in God and would construe the divine Essence as either a container for other things or something contained. They are not called produced or made because what is produced through creation is the *existence* manifested under their determinations. A thing without independent existence cannot become an independently produced existent merely by being eternally known.\n\nIf it were said that their intrinsic determinations were made, either they would have to possess the same existential rank as the divine Knower, or the Knower would have to be a subject acted upon by His own action within Himself. Both alternatives violate the unqualified unity and independence being affirmed. Nor can the effused existence be conceived as simply an accident received by a separately existent possible substance already possessing the existence to receive it. That would involve duplicating what one had already presupposed. The entities, under the consideration mentioned, are thus **unmade**; and there are not two existences in rivalry but one existence shared across the possible things and derived from the Real.\n\nThis one existence related to contingent things does not differ in **existential reality** from the unmanifest existence of the Real abstracted from determinate loci, except through relations and considerations: manifestness, determination, plurality through association with loci, the ruling of common predication, and other descriptions that arise through connection with manifestations. The source of these manifestations in relation to His self-disclosure is the rank of the *ʿamāʾ*, mentioned in a prophetic report, the station of divine descent and an outpouring of generosity from the unseen of identity. The first unseen and eternal relation of mutual orientation is posited in this rank, by which the presences of divine names open through essential eternal orientations. The details of this imagery must be considered carefully; the term *ʿamāʾ* and the report underlying it require textual and ḥadīth verification.\n\n### Two considerations of existence; essential knowledge neither increases nor changes\n\nExistence has two considerations. First, inasmuch as it is sheer existence, it is the Real. Under this respect there is neither multiplicity nor composition, neither attribute, name, description, relation nor judgment, but pure existence. Even our naming it “existence” is only a concession to understanding, not an adequate true name. Name, attribute and Essence are not three distinct entities here. Its perfection is intrinsic existence arising from itself and not another. His life and power are identical in reality with His knowledge. His eternal knowledge of things is the same as His knowledge of Himself: He knows Himself through Himself and everything through the knowledge by which He knows Himself.\n\nIn Him differing things are gathered without containing or being contained as physical vessels; multiplicities proceed through the appearances permitted by His singularity. His unity is the origin of every multiplicity, His simplicity is the ground upon which all composition may be understood, and His priority and finality, manifestness and hiddenness, are not two opposed changes of state within the Essence. No conceptual opposition between unity and multiplicity, or between absoluteness and restriction, can capture the whole truth. The Real's comprehensive meaning pervades every articulated relation, and His perfection embraces every genuine quality. Even what appears deficient to the veiled knower can, under the appropriate disclosure, be seen as an expression of some divine perfection, a locus for majesty or beauty. The many names and attributes do not destroy the unity of what they name, nor does the Real need external manifestation in order to perfect Himself.\n\nHis veil, majesty, independence and holiness mean that His reality is other than what would oppose it, and that nothing outside it establishes or preserves His existence. No thing is established by itself or through another except in dependence on Him. Intellects and reflections cannot comprehend Him under that respect, nor can spatial directions contain Him, nor inward or outward witnessing encompass Him. He is above bodily and intelligible restrictions, quantitative or qualitative estimation, and the total knowledge of created faculties, perfected or imperfect. Rational negations describe what He is **not**, and yet cannot confer comprehensive true acquaintance with His holiness.\n\nThe ground of His knowledge of the cosmos is His knowledge of Himself; the appearance of its relations is the appearance of the known realities. He knows indefinitely many things both because His knowledge embraces all that is known and because He is their source. He knows His Essence and its concomitants and the concomitants of those concomitants collectively and severally, generally and distinctly, without limit. What is determined according to a condition or cause He eternally knows **with its condition, cause and consequence**; what is not so determined He knows through Himself in the way He wills. His knowledge does not become new, and no created judgment restricts Him to a particular changing state.\n\nHis perfection belongs to Himself, His existence is actual rather than potential and necessary rather than possible. He is above change and origination. Created things do not contain Him, whether to reveal or shelter Him, and He does not create them to repair His own need. Things are related to Him as their source of determination; He is not related to their independence in the manner they are related to His necessity. They depend upon Him for their existence, but He does not depend upon them.\n\n### Providence and determined manifestation\n\nThe relation of things to the Real is called **providential care** (*ʿināya*). Their veil from Him consists in ignorance, deception and imagination, paradoxically arising because of the extremity of His nearness and His exalted majesty. Providence, in its true sense, is the effusion of His existential light upon the form inscribed in the mirror of each fixed entity—an entity considered as a relation of being known—and made ready to receive His ruling of bringing it into outward existence and manifesting Himself through it. “There is nothing like Him” (Q 42:11) pertains to the first consideration; “He is the Hearing, the Seeing” pertains to the second.\n\nWhenever He is apprehended, witnessed, addresses another or is addressed, His unqualified self remains behind the veil of His majesty. The event involves the relation of manifestness, the self-disclosure of nearness, and the shining of universal existential light upon possible realities. It is not the joining of two independent substances. In this conditioned aspect the determination of existence under the properties of possible entities, their affairs, special properties, accidents, periods, ranks and locations is called **creation** and “otherness.” Under that aspect every name and description can be predicated of it through its manifestations, and the appropriate faculties apprehend the various forms.\n\nThe light pervading these loci is nonetheless holy above division, spatial partition or **indwelling** (*ḥulūl*) in spirits and bodies. It becomes manifest when and as He wills. It is capable of being considered under the two opposed rulings of unqualified freedom from forms and conditioned manifestation through them, not because an external constituent is added to the Real but because of different relations. When He wills a form appears; without such willing no form is attributed under the aspect of that particular creation. Apparent individualization through forms does not lessen His majesty, perfection or holiness. Like an image shown in a changing mirror, the determination alters within the locus, not within the underlying unqualified reality.\n\nThrough existential disclosure, hidden things become visible and blessings pass from the unseen to the witnessed world under the names **Expander** (*al-Bāsiṭ*) and **Originator** (*al-Mubdiʾ*). When the ruling of intimate nearness is lifted, those outwardly manifest become hidden under the names **Contracter** (*al-Qābiḍ*) and **Restorer** (*al-Muʿīd*). Under the standpoint of concealment by majesty He is Forgiving or Concealing (*Ghafūr*); when He loves to be known and appears as He wills, He is Loving (*Wadūd*). Through love He brings the realities forth and draws them back. Nothing escapes His grasp, irresistible power or volition.\n\nQūnawī identifies the glorious Throne, in this technical context, as a locus of the display of power, wisdom and the ordered effects of unveiling and concealment. He connects the sequence of divine names with Q 50:37 and Q 85:12–16, culminating in “Doer of whatever He wills.” The final phrase blocks the error of treating the ranked order or its first intermediary as necessary to divine efficacy: the Real acts according to His will, not because He is constrained by an independent cause.\n\n### Last noble text — No independent appearance of the fixed entities\n\nKnow that the greatest doubts and veils arise when the multiplicities taking place **within the one existence** are mistaken for the fixed entities themselves having become existent. These multiplicities arise together with the **effects** of the fixed entities, but the entities, considered in themselves, have never appeared and will never appear. In themselves they do not require their own outward manifestation.\n\nIf a realized knower speaks otherwise, or ascribes existence and manifestness to the entities, his speech follows the language of a particular rank or a restricted spiritual taste. It can be true in relation to a particular station or group of stations, without being the truth proper to the all-comprehensive station of perfection. What I have explained is the **definitive statement that cannot be superseded** by a higher station. In this book I have stated matters from that standpoint. Other utterances may be equally true unconditionally or may be true only in relation to their specific stations.\n\nUnderstand, therefore, that manifestation belongs to **existence**, but under the condition of multiplicity with the effects of the entities in it. Hiddenness belongs intrinsically to the fixed entities and also to existence considered in the unity that cannot be partitioned. Matters move between appearance and concealment according to the strength and predominance of their rulings. What diminishes under the aspect of the manifest is included under the aspect of the hidden, and conversely. Relations and attributions are forms of states and rulings that arise among ranks: some manifest others and some conceal others according to the relative predominance already mentioned. Understand.\n\n**End of the independently printed original text.** Praise belongs to God alone; may God bless our master Muḥammad, his family and companions and grant them peace."

The Real is not enclosed by any of these alternatives: in this consideration neither predication nor its denial takes precedence. It follows that unity, principiality, causal efficacy, and the act of bringing into being are rightly attributed to the Real only under a consideration of determination."

      "pairs": [

          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "اعلم أن الحق من حيث إطلاقه وإحاطته لا يسمّى باسم، ولا يضاف إليه حكم، ولا يتعيّن بوصف ولا رسم، ليس نسبة الاقتضاء إليه بأولى من نسبة اللا اقتضاء، فإن الاقتضاء المتعقل إذ ذاك أو المنفي هو حكم متعين ووصف مقيّد. ثم لتعلم أن الاقتضاء وإن كان ذاتيّا فإن له ثلاث مراتب: حكمه من حيث المرتبة الأولى هو أنه لا يتوقف على شرط، ولا موجب يكون سببا لتعيّنه. وحكمه من حيث المرتبة الثانية هو أن يتوقف تعيّنه على شرط واحد فحسب. وحكمه من حيث المرتبة الثالثة هو أن ظهور أحكامه يتوقف على شروط وأسباب ووسائط. فحكم الاقتضاء الأول هو الفيض الذاتي لا لموجب، ولا يتعقل في مقابلة قابل أو استعداده، وحكم الاقتضاء الثاني التوقف على شرط واحد وجوديّ فحسب، وذلك الشرط الوجودي هو العقل الأول الذي هو واسطة بين الحق وبين ما قدّر وجوده من الممكنات إلى يوم القيامة، وأما حكم الاقتضاء من حيث المرتبة الثالثة فإن ظهور أثره وحكمه موقوف على شروط شتى كباقي الموجودات. ولست أعني بهذا أن ثمة اقتضاءات ثلاثة مختلفة الحقائق، بل هو اقتضاء واحد وله ثلاث مراتب، يظهر ويتعين به من حيثية كل مرتبة منها أثر أو آثار فافهم.",

          "ar": "ومن تفاريع ما ذكرنا من النصوص المحققة أيضا، وإن كنت قد ألمعت بطرف منه في بعض المواضع من كتبي في ضمن أمر آخر وبلسانه، لكن لما أفردت هذا الكتاب لذكر النصوص من الأذواق المختصّة بخصوص مقام الكمال، دون لسان عمومه من الأذواق المقيّدة الحاصلة لأرباب المقامات المخصوصة والمستندة من حيث الأصالة إلى حضرة اسم أو صفة من الصفات، والأسماء الإلهية التي هي محتد ذلك الذوق الخاص ومنبعه، وجب عليّ أن أفرد وأميز ما يختص بذوق المقام الأكمل الأجمع، وصحة ثبوته ومطابقته لما يعلمه اللّه تعالى في أعلى درجات علمه وأتمها وأكملها من ذلك الأمر المترجم عنه، دون تقرير صحته وثبوته بالنسبة والإضافة إلى مقام دون مقام، وباعتبار حال ووقت دون غيرهما من الأوقات والأحوال وما ذكر. فنقول بعد تمهيد هذه المقدمة الكلية في بيان هذا النص الذي قصدنا إيضاحه:",
          "en": "A further implication of the verified texts—something I have already intimated in places in my books, though within another discussion and in its own language—should be set out independently. For I have devoted this book to articulating texts derived from the particular spiritual tastings that belong to the station of perfection, rather than speaking in the general idiom of restricted tastings received by those who occupy particular stations. Such stations refer primarily to the Presence of some divine Name or attribute, from which that particular tasting proceeds. I must therefore distinguish what belongs specifically to the tasting of the most perfect, most comprehensive station: its validity, its reality and its correspondence with what God knows of the matter being expressed at the highest and most complete degree of knowledge. The purpose is not merely to establish that a proposition is valid relatively—true from one station rather than another, or in one condition or moment rather than others. Having set down this general preliminary statement, I now explain the text in question."
        }

      "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "إن كل معلوم أدركه الإنسان بنظره أو كشفه أو حسه أو خياله جمعا وفرادى، ولم ينته نظره أو كشفه لذلك الأمر، أو إدراكه إيّاه حسّا وخيالا إلى إدراك ما وراءه بعد معرفة ذاتياته ولوازمه الكلية، فإنه لم يدرك ذلك الأمر حق الإدراك تماما، ولم يعرفه حق المعرفة. وسواء كان متعلق إدراكه ومعرفته العالم من حيث معانيه وأرواحه، أو من حيث صوره وأعراضه، أو كان متعلق معرفته الحق، فإنه متى كشف له عن جلية الأمر وصورة تعين كل معلوم في علم الحق وجد الأمر كذلك، فإنه ما لم ينته معرفته بالحق إلى إطلاقه وصرافة وحدة ذاته الحقيقية، التي لا اسم يعيّنها ولا وصف ولا حكم ولا رسم، ولا تنضبط بشهود، ولا تعقل، ولا تنحصر في أمر معين، لم يعرف أن ليس وراء اللّه مرمى، وأن الإحاطة به علما وشهودا محال، وأن ليس بعد الوجود الحق المطلق إلا العدم المتوهم، هذا وإن كان لمعرفة تعذّر العلم باللّه على نحو ما يعلم نفسه طريق آخر أعلى وأتم وأكشف، عرفناه ذوقا وشهودا بحمد اللّه ومنّه، لكن ذلك مما يحرم بيانه وتسطيره وغاية البيان عنه هذا الإلماع المذكور. هذا وإن كان الذوق والمعرفة الحاصلة لصاحبه والشهود من حيث استناد ذلك الذوق، والمقام إلى حضرة اسم من الأسماء الإلهية الذي هو قبلة ذلك المقام، وغاية معرفته من الحق نهايته، سيما من الوجه الذي يقضي بأن الاسم عين المسمّى، كما أوضحناه في مواضع من كلامنا، لكن تلك غايات نسبية، فإن المبادئ والغايات أعلام الكمالات النسبية، والأمر من حيث الكمال الحقيقي بخلاف ذلك.",
          "en": "Whenever a person apprehends something known—through inquiry, unveiling, the senses, or imagination, separately or together—yet does not proceed, after discerning its essential features and universal concomitants, to apprehend what lies beyond that thing, he has not apprehended it fully as it should be apprehended or known it as it should be known. This holds whether the object is the world in its meanings and spirits, the world in its forms and accidents, or the Real Himself. Once the intrinsic character of the affair and the mode in which each known thing is determined in divine knowledge are unveiled to him, he finds this to be so. Unless his knowledge of the Real reaches the consideration of His absoluteness and the pure unity of His true Essence—determined by no name, attribute, judgement, or distinguishing description, neither confined by vision nor conceived and bounded in some specific matter—he will not understand that there is no goal beyond God, that encompassing Him in knowledge or witnessing is impossible, and that beyond absolute true existence lies only imagined nonexistence. There is, moreover, another path, higher, fuller and more revealing, to knowing the impossibility of knowing God in the way that He knows Himself. Through God's bounty we have known it by direct tasting and witnessing, but its articulation and transcription are prohibited; the utmost permissible indication is the allusion just given. Nonetheless, the tasting, knowledge, and witnessing available to a person through a spiritual station may derive from the Presence of one of the divine Names, which is the orientation and limit of that station. Even when the Name is considered identical with the Named, as I have explained elsewhere, such termini remain relative. Beginnings and ends mark relative perfections; the affair viewed from the standpoint of true perfection is otherwise."

      "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "نصّ شريف عزيز المنال: غيب هوية الحق إشارة إلى إطلاقه باعتبار اللاتعين. ووحدته الحقيقية الماحية لجميع الاعتبارات والأسماء والصفات. والنسب والإضافات هي عبارة عن تعقل الحق نفسه، وإدراكه لها من حيث تعيّنه، وهذا التعقل والإدراك التعيّني وإن كان يلي الإطلاق المشار إليه فإنه بالنسبة إلى تعين الحق في تعقل كل متعقل في كل تجلّ تعين مطلق، وإن أوسع التعينات، وهو شهود الكمّل، وهو التجلّي الذاتي، وله مقام التوحيد الأعلى. ومبدئية الحق تلي هذا التعين، والمبدئية هي محتد الاعتبارات، ومنبع النسب والإضافات الظاهرة في الوجود، والباطنة في عرصة التعقلات والأذهان. والمقول فيه أنه وجود مطلق واحد واجب، فهو عبارة عن تعين الوجود في النسبة العلمية الذاتية الإلهية، والحق من حيث هذه النسبة يسمّى عند المحقق بالمبدأ، لا من حيث نسبة غيرها، فافهم هذا وتدبّر، فقد أدرجت لك هذا النص أصل أصول المعارف الإلهية، واللّه المرشد.",
          "en": "A noble text, difficult of attainment. The unseen of the Real's Identity points to His absoluteness considered as nondetermination, and to His true unity, which effaces every consideration, name, and attribute. Relations and attributions concern the Real's apprehension of Himself and of them under the consideration of determination. Although this determinate understanding and apprehension immediately follows the absoluteness mentioned, relative to the Real's determination in any knower's conception and in each self-disclosure, it is an unrestricted determination—the most extensive of determinations. This is the witnessing of the perfected, the essential self-disclosure, and it belongs to the highest station of tawḥīd. The principiality of the Real comes next after this determination. Principiality is the origin of considerations and the source of relations and attributions, manifest in existence and concealed in the domain of intellections and minds. The expression 'one, absolute, necessary existence' concerns the determination of existence in the divine essential relation of knowledge. From the standpoint of this relation, the Real is called the Principle by the realised knower, not from every standpoint whatsoever.       "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "فإن لها، أي لتلك المرآة، أثرا في المنطبع فيها، لردها صورة المنطبع إليها، وظهور صورة المنطبع فيها بحسبها. وهذا صحيح من وجه ليس مطلقا؛ فإن الأثر للمرآة في المنطبع إنما كان يصح أن لو أثرت في حقيقته من حيث هو، وذلك غير واقع، وإنما يثبت الأثر للمرآة في المنطبع من حيث إدراك من لم يعرف حقيقة المنطبع ولم يدركه إلا في المرآة، وليست المرآة بمحل لحقيقة المنطبع، بل هي مجلى لمثاله وبعض ظهوراته، والظهر نسبة تضاف إلى المنطبع من حيث انطباع صورته في المرآة ليس عين حقيقة المنطبع. ومرادي من قولي ببعض ظهوراته التنبيه على أن التجليات الذاتية الاختصاصية لا تكون في مظهر ولا في مرآة، ولا بحسب مرتبة ما، فإن من أدرك الحق من حيث هذه التجليات فقد شهد الحقيقة خارج المرآة من حيث هي لا بحسب مظهر ولا مرتبة كما قلنا، ولا اسم ولا صفة ولا حال معين ولا غير ذلك، وهو يعلم ذوقا أن المرآة لا أثر لها في الحقيقة.",
          "en": "It is claimed that the mirror affects what is reflected in it, since it returns the reflected thing’s image to it and the form appears in the mirror according to the mirror’s character. This is true in one respect, but not without qualification. The mirror would affect the reflected thing properly only if it acted upon the reality of that thing as such, which does not happen. The mirror’s supposed effect holds only from the standpoint of someone who knows the reflected thing solely by perceiving it in the mirror. The mirror is not the locus of the reflected reality; it is a site in which its likeness and some of its appearances become manifest. Appearance is a relation attributed to the reflected thing insofar as its form is reflected, not the reflected reality itself. By saying ‘some of its appearances’ I intend to indicate that the special essential self-disclosures are not in a manifestation, mirror, or determinate rank. The one who apprehends the Real through these disclosures witnesses Reality beyond the mirror, not according to a manifestation, rank, name, attribute, particular state, or anything else. By direct tasting he knows that the mirror does not affect Reality."

      "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "ولا سر قوله عليه السلام: «كان اللّه ولا شيء معه». ولا سر قوله تعالى: ﴿وَمَا أَمْرُنَا إِلَّا وَاحِدَةٌ كَلَمْحٍ بِالْبَصَرِ﴾ [القمر: 50]، ولا يعرف سر مبدئية الإيجاد لا في زمان موجود، كما أنه من ذاق هذا المشهد وقد كان علم أن الأعيان الثابتة هي حقائق الموجودات، وأنها غير مجعولة، وحقيقة الحق منزّهة عن الجعل والتأثير، وما ثم أمر ثالث غير الحق والأعيان، فإنه يجب أن يعلم إن صح له ما ذكرنا أن لا أثر لشيء في شيء، وأن الأشياء هي المؤثرة في أنفسها، وأن المسمّاة عللا وأسبابا مؤثرة هي شروط في ظهور آثار الأشياء في أنفسها، لا أن ثمة حقيقة تؤثر في حقيقة غيرها وهكذا، فلتعرف الأمر في المدد، فليس ثمة شيء يمد شيئا غيره، بل المدد يصل من باطن الشيء إلى الظاهر، والتجلّي النوري الوجودي يظهر ذلك، فليس الإظهار بتأثير في حقيقة ما أظهره، فالنسب هي المؤثرة بعضها في البعض، بمعنى أن بعضها سبب لانتشاء البعض، وظهور حكمه في الحقيقة التي هي محتدها. ومن جملة ما يعرفه ذائق هذا التجلّي أن لا أثر للأعيان الثابتة من كونها مرائي في التجلّي الوجودي الإلهي، إلا من حيث ظهور التعدد الكامن في غيب ذلك التجلّي، فهو أثر في نسبة الظهور الذي هو شرط في الإظهار، والحق يتعالى عن أن يكون متأثرا من غيره، وتتعالى حقائق الكائنات أن تكون من حيث هي حقائقها متأثرة، فإنها من هذا الوجه في ذوق الكمال عين شؤون الحق، فلا جائز أن يؤثر فيها غيرها، فلا أثر لمرآة ما من حيث هي مرآة في حقيقته المنطبع فيها لما مرّ بيانه.",
          "en": "Nor does he know the secret of the saying, ‘God was, and there was nothing with Him,’ or of God's words, ‘Our command is but one, like the blink of an eye’ [Q 54:50]. He does not know the secret of origination's principiality outside an existent time. Likewise, one who tastes this witnessing, having already known that the fixed entities are the realities of existents, that they are not made, that the reality of the Real is beyond being made or being affected, and that there is no third thing beyond the Real and the fixed entities, must understand—if the preceding insight is sound—that no thing acts upon another thing's reality. Things disclose their own effects, whereas what are called efficient causes are conditions for those effects to become apparent within them, not realities that transform the inner reality of another. Assistance does not reach a thing from an independently acting other; it arrives from its inward aspect to its outward. The luminous, existential disclosure reveals this. Making manifest is not an operation upon the reality of what is manifested. Relations affect one another insofar as one relation is the occasion for another’s emergence and for the appearance of its judgement within the reality that is its source. One who tastes this disclosure also knows that fixed entities considered as mirrors have no effect on the divine existential disclosure except with respect to the appearance of the multiplicity hidden within that disclosure. This is an effect in the relation of manifestation, which is a condition of making manifest; the Real is above being affected by another, and the realities of created things, as realities, are above being affected—for from this standpoint and in the taste of perfection they are among the affairs of the Real. A mirror as mirror does not act upon the reality of what it reflects."
        }
      ]

      "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "ومن النصوص الكلية نصوص ذكرتها في كتاب مفتاح غيب الجمع وتفصيله، وفي غيره من الكتب التي أنشأتها لا بكلام أحد من الناس، فإن ذلك ليس من دأبي؛ إذ قد عصمني اللّه من ذلك، وأغناني بهباته الخالصة العلية عن العواري الخارجية السفلية، غير أنه لما اختصّ هذا الكتاب بذكر هذه النصوص وجب ذكر تلك النصوص أيضا هنا. فأقول من جملتها أن كل ما هو سبب في وجود كثرة وكثير، فإنه من حيث هو كذلك لا يمكن أن يتعين بظهور، ولا يبدو لناظر إلّا في منظوره. ومنها أن الشيء لا يصدر عنه، ولا ينمي ما يضاده، ولا ما يباينه على اختلاف ضروب الإثمار وأنواعه المعنوية والروحانية والمثالية والخيالية والحسية والطبيعية، وهذا عام في كل ما يسمّى مصدرا لشيء أو أشياء، أو أصلا مثمرا، لكن إنما يكون له هذا الوصف باعتبار تعقله من حيث هو هو، وباعتبار آخر خفي لا يطّلع عليه إلا الندر من المحققين. ومتى توهم وقوع خلاف ما ذكرنا فليس ذلك إلا بشرط خارج عن ذات الشيء، أو شروط وبحسبها وبحسب الهيئة المتعقلة الحاصلة من تلك الجمعية، أعني جمعية الحقيقة الموصوفة بالمصدرية مع الشروط والاعتبارات الخارجية، وأحكام المرتبة التي يتعيّن فيها ذلك الاجتماع.",
          "en": "Among the universal texts are some I have set forth in the *Key to the Unseen of Gathering and Its Differentiation*, and in other books composed not by borrowing anyone's discourse. God, I say, has spared me such borrowing and enriched me with His higher, unalloyed gifts. But since this book is devoted to these texts, I must include those statements here as well. One is that anything which is a cause of the existence of a multiplicity, insofar as it is that cause, cannot itself become determinate through its appearance; it appears to an observer only within what the observer beholds. Another is that a thing does not issue forth, or bring to fruition, what is opposite to it or wholly alien to it, whatever the kind of fruition—intelligible, spiritual, imaginal, imaginative, sensible, or natural. This principle covers every purported source or fruitful root, but it applies when the thing is apprehended in its own identity and under another, more hidden consideration known only to rare realised knowers. If something contrary appears to occur, it must be due to one or more conditions extrinsic to the thing, and to the constituted configuration produced by bringing together the source-reality, those external conditions and considerations, and the determinations of the rank in which they are combined."

      "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "قال تعالى: ﴿كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَى شَاكِلَتِهِ﴾ [الإسراء: 84]. ولا يثمر شيء، ولا يظهر عنه أيضا عينه ولا ما يشابهه مشابهة تامة، فإنه يلزم من ذلك أن يكون الوجود قد حصل مرتين، وظهر في حقيقة واحدة ومرتبة واحدة على وجه ونسق واحد، وذلك تحصيل للحاصل، وأنه محال لخلوه عن الفائدة، وكونه من قبيل العبث، ويتعالى الفاعل الحق الحكيم العليم من فعل العبث، فلا بدّ من اختلاف ما بين الأصول وثمراتها، فالممكنات غير متناهية، والفيض من الحق الذي هو أصل الأصول واحد، فلا تكرار في الوجود عند من عرف ما ذكرنا فافهم. ولهذا قال المحققون: إن الحق سبحانه وتعالى ما تجلّى في صورة واحدة لشخص واحد مرتين، ولا لشخصين أيضا في صورة، فلا بدّ من فارق واختلاف من وجه أو وجوه، كما أشرت إليه من قبل، فافهم واللّه المرشد.",
          "en": "God says: ‘Each acts according to its own disposition’ [Q 17:84]. Nothing brings forth, as its own fruit or appearance, the very same thing or something absolutely identical to it; otherwise existence would have occurred twice in the very same reality and rank in one and the same manner. This would be the production of what is already produced, devoid of purpose and amounting to futility; the Real, wise and knowing Agent is exalted above such futility. There must therefore be some difference between roots and their fruits. The possibles are without end, while the effusion from the Real, the Root of roots, is one. For one who understands this there is no repetition in existence. Hence the realised knowers say that the Real never discloses Himself twice in exactly one form to a single person, nor in a wholly identical form to two persons. There must be difference in one respect or another. Understand, and God guides."

      "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "نصّ شريف: اعلم أن الحق لما لم يكن أن ينسب إليه من حيث إطلاقه صفة ولا اسم، أو يحكم عليه بحكم ما سلبيّا كان أو إيجابيّا، علم أن الصفات والأسماء والأحكام لا يطلق عليه ولا ينسب إليه إلا من حيث التعينات. ولما استبان أن كل كثرة وجودية أو متعقلة يجب أن تكون مسبوقة بوحدة، لزم أن تكون التعينات التي من حيث ما تضاف الأسماء والصفات والأحكام إلى الحق مسبوقة بتعين هو مبدأ جميع التعينات ومحدتها، بمعنى أن ليس وراءه إلا الإطلاق الصرف، وأنه أمر سلبيّ يستلزم سلب الأوصاف والأحكام والتعينات والاعتبارات عن كنه ذاته سبحانه، وعدم التقيد والحصر في وصف أو اسم أو تعين، أو غير ذلك مما عدّدنا أو أجملنا ذكره. ثم إن لذوي العقول السليمة وإن عدموا الكشف الصحيح أن يعتبروا الصفات والأسماء التالية، فإن تعذّر عليهم تعقل أسماء وصفات وراء ما تصورت وانتهت إليه ادراكاتهم العقلية، فتلك أسماء الذات بالنسبة إليهم، ويستدل بحقائقها في طور العقل النظري حال الحجاب؛ لشمول حكمها، وتبعية غيرها من الصفات والأسماء لها، وتوقف تعين ما بعدها عليها، فالعطايا الإلهية الذاتية والأسمائية تعرف من هذه القاعدة، بمعنى أن كل عطاء وخير يصل من الحق إلى الخلق، إما أن يكون عطاء ذاتيّا أو أسمائيّا، أو أن يكون مجموعا من الذات والأسماء.",
          "en": "A noble text. Since no attribute or name can be related to the Real with respect to His sheer absoluteness, and no judgement, negative or affirmative, may be passed upon Him in that regard, it follows that attributes, Names and judgements are ascribed to Him only under determinations. Since every multiplicity, whether existent or conceived, must be preceded by a unity, the determinations by virtue of which these predicates apply must themselves be preceded by a determination serving as the principle and source of all determinations. Beyond that determination lies nothing but sheer absoluteness, understood negatively: it excludes attributing qualities, judgements, determinations, and conceptual considerations to the ultimate reality of His Essence, or confining it to any name or qualification. Those of sound intellect, even without authentic unveiling, can consider the next succeeding names and attributes. If they cannot conceive names or attributes beyond the point their rational apprehensions reach, those will count for them as Names of the Essence. In the veiled state of speculative reason, they infer their reality from the comprehensive reach of these names, the subordination of the remaining names and attributes, and the dependence of later determinations upon them. This rule enables one to distinguish divine gifts: every gift or good that reaches creation from the Real may be essential, name-related, or a conjunction of Essence and Names."

          "ar": "فأما العطايا الذاتية فلا حساب عليها، ولا تنضبط تعيناتها بعدد ولا تنحصر فيه، وأما العطايا الأسمائية والمنسوبة إلى الذات والأسماء جميعا فلا يخلو إما أن تكون نسبتها إلى حضرة الذات أقوى وأتم من نسبتها إلى حضرة الأسماء والصفات، أو بالعكس، فإن غلبت نسبتها إلى الأسماء والصفات على نسبتها إلى الذات وقع الحساب عليها، إما عسيرا أو يسيرا، بحسب الغلبة والمغلوبية الواقعة هناك. وهنا سرّ كبير لا يمكن إفشاؤه، وإن كانت نتيجة الغلبة والمغلوبية قوة نسبة تلك العطايا إلى حضرة الذات، فذلك الذي لا حساب عليه؛ لأن العطايا الذاتية وما قويت نسبتها إليها لا يصدر ولا يقبل إلا بمناسبة ذاتية، فلا موجب لها غير تلك المناسبة. ومن لم يعرف هذا الأصل لم يعلم حقيقة قوله تعالى: ﴿وَتَرْزُقُ مَنْ تَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾ [آل عمران: 27]، ولا سر قوله تعالى: ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾ [النور: 38]، ولا سر قوله تعالى: ﴿هَذَا عَطَاؤُنَا فَامْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾ [ص: 39]، ونحو ذلك مما تكرّر ذكره في الكتاب العزيز. وفي الأحاديث النبوية أيضا مثل قوله عليه السلام: «إنه يدخل الجنة من أمته سبعون ألفا بغير حساب ومع كل ألف سبعون ألفا». هؤلاء أصحاب العطايا الأسمائية، غير أن نسبتهم إلى حضرة الذات أقوى من نسبتهم إلى حضرة الأسماء والصفات، ولهذا اتبعوا أصحاب المناسبة الذاتية، وشاركوهم في أحوالهم، فاعلم ذلك.",
          "en": "Gifts belonging to the Essence are not subject to reckoning, and their determinations cannot be confined within a numerical count. Name-related gifts, and those attributed jointly to Essence and Names, are otherwise graded: their relation to the Presence of the Essence may be stronger and more complete than their relation to the Presence of Names and attributes, or the reverse. Where the latter relation prevails, reckoning attends the gift, whether difficult or easy according to the balance of those relations. Here lies a great secret that cannot be disclosed. When the stronger relation is to the Essential Presence, no reckoning applies, since essential gifts and those predominantly related to it issue forth and are received only through an essential correspondence, without some separate necessitating condition. Whoever fails to grasp this foundation will not fully understand the scriptural expressions ‘You provide for whom You will without reckoning’ [Q 3:27], ‘God provides for whom He wills without reckoning’ [Q 24:38], and ‘This is Our gift; bestow or withhold without reckoning’ [Q 38:39]. The prophetic reports similarly speak of seventy thousand members of the community entering Paradise without reckoning, with seventy thousand accompanying each thousand. In Qūnawī's classification these recipients belong to the gifts of the Names but have a stronger relation to the Essential Presence, and thus follow and participate in the states of those whose correspondence is essential."
        }
      ]

      "pairs": [
        {

          "ar": "وإذ قد ذكرنا أقسام العطايا وأحكامها فلنذكر أقسام القابلين لها، فإنهم في أخذهم على طبقات يتعدد بحسب سؤالاتهم الاستعدادية، أو الحالية، أو المرتبية، أو الروحانية، أو الطبيعية المزاجية، أو الطبيعية العرضية التي يترجم عنها لسان الطالب القابل. وعلى الجملة فأعلى مراتب القابلين في قبولهم لما يرد عليهم من فيض الحق وعطاياه رؤية وجه الحق في الشروط والأسباب المسمّاه بالوسائط وسلسلة الترتيب، بحيث يعلم الآخذ، ويشهد أن الوسائط السببية ليست غير تعينات الحق في المراتب الإلهية والكونية على اختلاف ضروبها، بمعنى أنه ليس بين فيض الحق المقبول وبين القابل إلا نفس تعين الفيض بالقابلية المقيّدة دون انضمام حكم إمكاني يقتضيه ويوجبه أثر مرور الفيض على مراتب الوسائط، والانصباغ بأحكام إمكاناتها، ويرى الفيض أنه تجل من تجليات باطن الحق، فإن التعددات والتعينات التي لحقته هي أحكام الاسم الظاهر من حيث أن ظاهر الحق مجلى لباطنه، فأحكام الظهور تعدّد مطلق وحدة البطون، وتلك الأحكام هي المسمّاة بالقوابل، وهي صور الشؤون ليس غيرها فافهم. واللّه يقول الحق وهو يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم.",
          "en": "Having discussed the classes of gifts and their governing characteristics, let us consider the classes of their recipients.       "pairs": [
        {
          "sequence": 1,
          "ar": "فالعديم المعرفة الصحيحة الشهودية النسبي التصور، ليس بداع للحق الذي ضمن له الإجابة بقوله له: ﴿ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ﴾، وإنما هو متوجه في دعائه إلى الصورة الشخصية في ذهنه، الناتجة من نظره وخياله، أو خيال غيره ونظره، أو المتحصلة من المجموع المشار إليه، فلهذا يحرم من هذا شأنه الإجابة في عين ما سأل فيه، أو يتأخر عنه، أعني الإجابة. ومتى أجيب مثل هذا فإنما سببه سر المعية الإلهية المقتضية عدم خلو شيء عن الحق، أو الجمعية التامة الحاصلة للمضطرين، الموعود لهم بالإجابة للاستدعاء الاضطراري، والاستعداد الحاصل به: أي بالاضطرار. وحال من هذا وصفه مخالف لحال ذي التصور الصحيح والمعرفة المحققة، فإنه مستحضر الحق، ومتوجّه إليه استحضارا وتوجها محققا، وإن لم يكن ذلك من جميع الوجوه لكن يكفيه كونه متصورا ومستحضرا للحقّ في توجهه، ولو في بعض المراتب، ومن حيثية بعض الأسماء والصفات، وهذا حال المتوسطين من أهل اللّه، والحال إلى المقدّم ذكره حال المحجوبين. وأما الكمّل والأفراد فإن توجّههم إلى الحق تابع للتجلّي الذاتي المشار إليه، الحاصل لهم، والموقوف تحققهم بمقام الكمال على الفوز به، فإنه مثمر لهم معرفة تامة جامعة لحيثيات جميع الأسماء والصفات والمراتب والاعتبارات، مع صحة تصور الحق من حيث تجليه الذاتي المشار إليه، الحاصل لهم بالشهود الأتم، فلهذا لا يتأخر عنهم الإجابة.",
          "en": "Someone who lacks sound, witnessed knowledge and has only an inadequate conception does not, in the intended sense, address the Real who promises, ‘Call upon Me and I shall answer you.’ In petition he addresses instead a particular image within his mind, formed from his own thought and imagination, someone else's, or their combination. Thus he may be denied the response to exactly what he requested, or the response may be delayed. When such a person does receive an answer, it follows either from the mystery of divine accompanying-presence, by which nothing is wholly devoid of the Real, or from the concentrated comprehensiveness attained by those in dire need, to whom a response is promised through their compelling need and the readiness it produces. Such a person holds the Real present and turns truly toward Him, even if not from every possible standpoint; it suffices that the Real is apprehended in a certain rank and through certain Names and attributes. This is the condition of those at intermediate stages of the way, in contrast with the veiled condition just described. But the perfected and certain singular individuals turn toward the Real under the essential self-disclosure discussed earlier; attainment of that disclosure constitutes their verification in the station of perfection. It yields a comprehensive recognition gathering the considerations of all Names, attributes, degrees and relations, alongside a true conception of the Real under the essential disclosure witnessed in the fullest way. For this reason, Qūnawī says, the response to them is not delayed."
